VOLUME 6 (PART 1): AVALOKITESHVARA BODHISATTVA'S PERFECT PENETRATION THROUGH THE EAR ROOT

Brief Commentary on the Shurangama Sutra — Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

THE SUTRA OF THE GREAT BUDDHA CROWN, THE TATHAGATA'S SECRET CAUSE, THE COMPLETE MEANING OF CULTIVATION AND CERTIFICATION, AND THE MYRIAD PRACTICES OF ALL BODHISATTVAS: THE SHURANGAMA

VOLUME 6 – PART 1

— o0o —

LECTURED BY VENERABLE MASTER HSUAN HUA

— o0o —

THE PERFECT PENETRATION OF THE EAR ROOT
Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva


Sutra text: 爾時觀世音菩薩即從座起, 頂禮佛足而白佛言。

Transliteration: Nhĩ thời Quán Thế Âm Bồ-tát tức tùng toà khởi, đảnh lễ Phật túc nhi bạch Phật ngôn:

Translation: At that time Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha's feet, and said to the Buddha:

Commentary: In the previous section, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva presented the method of cultivating the Buddha-recitation dharma-door. That is a method most suitable for everyone in the present age. That method is most effective. Why? The sutra tells us that in the Dharma-Ending Age, among a million people who cultivate, not even one will become enlightened. Many cultivate, but few attain certification. So what should we do? Do not worry. The sutra teaches, "It is solely through the Buddha-recitation dharma-door that all living beings are taken across to liberation." The Buddha-recitation method is very easy to practice. By practicing Buddha-recitation, we escape the three realms horizontally and are reborn with our karma intact.

What is meant by escaping the three realms horizontally? It is like an insect living inside a bamboo stalk: if it bores its way out lengthwise through the stalk, it must pass through each joint, which takes a very long time. But if that insect knows how to gnaw a hole through the side of the stalk, it can get out of the bamboo tube very easily. People who recite the Buddha's name are like the insect that escapes through the side of the bamboo; they escape the three realms horizontally — right from their own level. "Rebirth with karma" — the karma people carry with them is karma from past lives, not of this life; it is karma already created, not new karma. This means that before you knew of the Buddha-recitation method, you had already created karmic obstructions.

You may carry that karma with you when you are reborn in the Pure Land. But you must not continue creating evil karma once you have learned Buddha-recitation, for you cannot carry that evil karma with you. Once you know how to recite the Buddha's name, you should change your way of life. Do not deliberately create bad karma. If you do, you will pile up evil karma and increase your obstructions. That is called "knowingly and deliberately transgressing." In that case, your karmic obstructions triple. You may carry your old karma to rebirth, but now that you understand the Buddhadharma, you cannot say, "Oh! I can recite the Buddha's name on the one hand, and create evil karma on the other, because in the future I can carry the karma I create to the Land of Ultimate Bliss with me."

That is a mistake! Not only will you be unable to carry your karma with you, you will be unable to be reborn there at all, because you will be obstructed by your own karma. We who have faith in the Buddha must be careful not to create further karmic obstructions once we have learned Buddha-recitation. This chapter on Mahasthamaprapta's perfect penetration through Buddha-recitation is extremely important. Everyone should understand what the Buddha-recitation method essentially is.

Why should we recite the Buddha's name? Because we have a great affinity with Amitabha Buddha.

Amitabha Buddha became a Buddha ten kalpas ago. Before that, his dharma name was the Bhikshu Dharma Treasury. At that time, he made forty-eight vows. In his thirteenth and fourteenth vows, he vowed: "If any living being throughout the ten directions recites my name and yet does not become a Buddha, I vow not to attain right enlightenment." In other words, if any living being recites his name without becoming a Buddha, he vows not to become a Buddha himself. And through the power of Amitabha Buddha's vows, everyone who recites his name will be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

The Pure Land dharma-door is one of the five schools of Chinese Buddhism.
1. The Chan (dhyāna) school.
2. The Teaching school.
3. The Vinaya school.
4. The Esoteric school.
5. The Pure Land school.

The Pure Land school will be the last school to survive. In this world, in the Dharma-Ending Age, the Shurangama Sutra will be the first to disappear. After that, the other sutras will vanish one after another, and only the Amitabha Sutra will remain. While the Amitabha Sutra still remains in the world, it will take very many people across to liberation. After a thousand years or more, the Amitabha Sutra will also disappear completely.

The "Dharma-Ending Age" simply means that the right Dharma vanishes entirely. Once the Amitabha Sutra has disappeared, only the phrase "Namo Amitabha Buddha" will be left. This extraordinary phrase will also take very many people across to liberation; yet after another thousand years, it too will disappear. All that remains will be the name "Amitabha Buddha," which will also stay in the world for a hundred more years before vanishing. By then, no more Buddhadharma will circulate in the world. While we are still before the Dharma-Ending Age, we should cultivate and preserve the ways of the Right Dharma age. That is called "requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel."

In the Dharma-Ending Age, we should not fear any hardship. I do not mind the difficulty of expounding the Dharma for you, and you should not fear the hardship of coming to hear the sutra. Rouse your spirits! Do not say you are tired and must go rest. Forget yourselves for the sake of the Dharma. Consider how Shakyamuni Buddha lived in the Snow Mountains for six years seeking the Way. We do not go to live six years in the mountains, but the least we can do is to study Buddhism. Regard the Buddhadharma as the food you need to eat. "If I do not go hear the sutra lecture, it is as if I will have nothing to eat for the next few days."

You should think in this way. "I must go hear the Dharma. I must certainly find a way to truly understand the Way." Where can you gain a genuine understanding of the Buddhadharma? You must often listen to sutra lectures. Without hearing sutra lectures, you cannot open wisdom. This is especially true of the Shurangama Sutra, for it is precisely the sutra that opens wisdom for living beings. Take for example this chapter on the dharma of perfect-penetration cultivation expounded by the twenty-five sages.

One of them perfected his Way through the dharma of the Fire-Light samadhi. One attained perfect penetration through the element of wind; another through the element of space. One cultivated from his eye root and succeeded, and another cultivated from his ear root. Each of the six sense roots was taken up by one sage or another for cultivation. Each category within the eighteen realms was entered and cultivated to certification by one of them. Hearing these principles, you should apply them to yourselves.

You will ask, "Which root should I cultivate?" Do not be impatient. The very ear root that Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva used in cultivation is best for you. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva perfected his cultivation effort through the ear root, and Ananda will follow Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva in cultivating this dharma-door. The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of former lives have passed down to us a wonderful dharma-door; we should follow the cultivation from the ear root to attain perfect penetration. This is the easiest method.

At that time Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha's feet, and said to the Buddha:

"Guan" means to contemplate, to regard with attention.
Using the power of wisdom to regard attentively, the cultivator contemplates the objective world.

With the power of wisdom, the cultivator regards the realm that is being contemplated. The contemplative power of wisdom is inherent in Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's own nature. The objective world being contemplated is the sounds emitted by all living beings. You should contemplate the crying sounds of suffering, the jubilant sounds of happiness, the sounds of neither suffering nor joy, the sounds of good, the sounds of evil, the sounds of truth, the sounds of falseness — contemplate every kind of sound.

"Shi" is the world, in the sense of time — past, present, and future. Contemplate the past causes and effects of living beings. Contemplate the karma living beings are now creating. Contemplate the retribution living beings will undergo in the future. "Why does that person suffer so much?" You reflect, and then realize: "Oh! In a past life he was unfilial to his parents and generally unkind to people. That is why his retribution in this life is suffering."

Yin: regard every sound attentively.
"Bodhisattva" means "one who enlightens sentient beings." It also means "a sentient being with a vast heart for the Way." A Bodhisattva is also called "an enlightened sentient being," which refers to self-enlightenment. When we say a Bodhisattva is "one who enlightens sentient beings," that refers to enlightening others. Combining these two meanings, a Bodhisattva is a being who is enlightened and wishes to help all living beings become enlightened.

What a Bodhisattva does is to enlighten himself and enlighten others, to benefit himself and benefit others.

You who are studying the Buddhadharma must firmly remember the meaning of "Bodhisattva." Do not be like the person who chaired a conference on "Sangha Harmony," yet when asked what "Sangha" meant could only remain silent. That is truly inconceivable!

Sutra text: 世尊,憶念我昔無數恒河沙劫。於時有佛出現於世,名觀世音。我於彼佛發菩提心。彼佛教我從聞思修入三摩地。

Transliteration: Thế tôn, ức niệm ngã tích vô số hằng hà sa kiếp. Ư thời hữu Phật xuất hiện ư thế, danh Quán Thế Âm. Ngã ư bỉ Phật phát bồ-đề tâm. Bỉ Phật giáo ngã tòng văn tư tu nhập tam-ma-điạ.

Translation: World Honored One, I recall that in the past, countless kalpas ago as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, a Buddha appeared in the world named Avalokiteshvara. I brought forth the bodhi resolve in the presence of that Buddha. That Buddha taught me to enter samadhi through hearing, contemplating, and cultivating.

Commentary: Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva said to Shakyamuni Buddha: World Honored One, I recall that in the past, countless kalpas ago as numerous as the sands of the Ganges — reaching back a very long time, a great many kalpas too numerous to count, like the sands of the Ganges River — a Buddha appeared in the world named Avalokiteshvara. This is the Avalokiteshvara of the past. That is the Tathagata Avalokiteshvara, who also cultivated perfect penetration through the ear root. I brought forth the bodhi resolve in the presence of that Buddha. I brought forth the resolve to cultivate and certify to the Way of liberation. That Buddha taught me to enter right concentration through hearing, contemplating, and cultivating. The past Buddha Avalokiteshvara taught Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva the process of hearing, contemplating, and cultivating — that is, to enter samadhi through the wisdom of hearing, the wisdom of contemplating, and the wisdom of cultivating. "Contemplating" here does not mean using the discursive thought of the sixth consciousness. Rather, it means using the effort of sitting in meditation in cultivation.

Sutra text: 初於聞中,入流亡所。所入既寂,動靜二相,了然不生。如是漸增,聞所聞盡。盡聞不住,覺所覺空。空覺極圓,空所空滅。生滅既滅,寂滅現前。

Transliteration: Sơ ư văn trung, nhập lưu vong sở. Sở nhập ký tịch, động tĩnh nhị tướng liễu nhiên bất sanh. Như thị tiệm tăng, văn sở văn tận. Tận văn bất trụ, giác sở giác không. Không giác cực viên, không sở không diệt. Sanh diệt ký diệt, tịch diệt hiện tiền.

Translation: At first, dwelling in hearing, I entered the flow of perfect penetration and the state of what-is-heard ceased to be. The entering having become still, the two characteristics of movement and stillness clearly did not arise. Thus progressing step by step, hearing and what-is-heard both came to an end. Not dwelling in the ending of hearing, awareness and what-is-awakened-to became empty. With the emptiness of awareness perfected to the utmost, the emptiness and what-is-emptied both vanished. With arising and ceasing already quenched, still extinction manifested.

Commentary: At first, dwelling in hearing, I entered the flow of perfect penetration and the state of what-is-heard ceased to be.

With the wisdom of hearing, the cultivator hears what is within, not what is without. Not following after sense-objects of sound means not running after them. Earlier, the sutra text already spoke of not chasing after the six sense roots and not being directed by them. This is called:

Returning the hearing to hear the self-nature — turning the faculty of hearing inward to recognize one's own nature.
Turning the hearing inward means not listening to outer sounds, but instead turning back, directing inward, to hear one's own nature. That is,
gathering it into one's own body and mind.
"Within hearing." Pay special attention to these two words: it is not within the physical eye, not within ear-consciousness, not within mind-consciousness..., but precisely within the hearing-nature that neither ariss nor ceases — which is precisely the Tathagatagarbha nature.

Turning the light around to shine within — revolving the light back to illuminate the inside.
That means not seeking outside.

This passage of sutra text says that Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva "entered the flow," which means he turned his hearing inward to hear his own nature.

Entering the Dharma-nature flow of the sages — entering the flow of the Dharma-nature of the sagely ones.

He had "entered the flow and forgotten the abode" — meaning that all defiling objects, the six sense-objects perceived by the six sense roots, had been entirely cut off.

This means he had entered the illuminating flow of his own nature, no longer turning outward to seek and pursue; the mind, luminous, constantly dwelt within. To be outside the flow is to remain bound to external conditions. If one pursues external sense-objects of sound, one is entangled in the turning wheel of birth and death. When all outer sounds are forgotten, there is no longer the characteristic of movement — that is, the first knot, that of agitated sense-objects, has been untied. Hence it is called "entering the flow and forgetting the abode." "Forgetting" means liberation; "abode" means sense-objects of sound.

The abode entered into also became still, and the two characteristics of movement and stillness clearly did not arise.

The source of the six sense roots and the six sense-objects all ceased. This is most difficult. Here Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva had entered the flow of his own nature. When the utmost stillness was reached, the characteristics of movement and stillness both vanished. Since the realm of stillness belongs to the region of the form skandha, one must not dwell in the realm of stillness. Only when neither movement nor stillness arises has one reached what is called the stillness of what is entered. At that point, the second knot — that of stillness — has been untied. Sense-objects of sound are entirely stilled, and the two characteristics of movement and stillness clearly no longer arise. That is, the form skandha has been destroyed.

Thus progressing step by step, hearing and what-is-heard both came to an end.

The bonds tied at the sense roots have been untied; cultivation advances gradually, samadhi power is strengthened, so the hearing root accords with what is heard and both are entirely ended — there is no more experiencer and experienced. That is, the third knot — that of the sense roots — has been untied, and at the same time the first five consciousnesses of the feeling skandha have been destroyed.

Not dwelling in the ending of hearing, awareness and what-is-awakened-to became empty.

Hearing and what-is-heard have both been exhausted, yet perception remains, self-image remains, so one must continue advancing in cultivation until reaching "one should produce the mind without dwelling anywhere," arriving at knowing yet not knowing, awakening yet not awakening, until both awareness and what-is-awakened-to are empty — only then is the fourth knot, that of awareness, untied. Only when the awakener and what-is-awakened-to are both gone is it called being entirely free of attachment — that is, the sixth consciousness, the thinking skandha, is destroyed.

With the emptiness of awareness perfected to the utmost, the emptiness and what-is-emptied both vanished.

The awakener and what-is-awakened-to have both become empty; one must continue to advance, investigating what this emptiness relies upon to exist, until the emptiness-nature of awareness is ultimately perfected, and then the emptier and the emptied are both entirely eliminated. The mind capable of creating is eliminated, and the realm that this mind rendered empty is also eliminated, to the point where even emptiness no longer remains. For as long as emptiness remains, one is still attached to the nature of emptiness. And now, for Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, even the nature of emptiness no longer remains — that is, the fifth knot, that of the emptiness of awareness, has been untied, and at the same time the seventh consciousness, the formations skandha, is destroyed.

With arising and ceasing already quenched, still extinction manifested.
The emptier and the emptied both became still and extinct, yet the idea of "extinction" remained — and where extinction remains, arising remains — so one must continue advancing in cultivation until the characteristics of both arising and ceasing are entirely eliminated; only then can the sixth knot, that of the idea of "extinction," be untied. At the same time, the eighth consciousness, the alaya consciousness of the consciousness skandha, is destroyed. The two words "arising and ceasing" refer precisely to the knots: when movement ends, stillness arises; when the roots cease, awareness arises; when awareness ceases, emptiness arises; when emptiness ceases, extinction arises. These six knots are precisely the dharma of arising and ceasing. The characteristic of extinction is most difficult to untie; the characteristic of extinction must be entirely eliminated before one can reach the state of neither arising nor ceasing, before one can see one's own original face. Now the six knots have been untied, the five skandhas have been completely destroyed, falseness is entirely exhausted and all truth is revealed — that is, with arising and ceasing already quenched, still extinction manifests, and ultimate perfect penetration is certified.

Sutra text: 忽然超越世出世間,十方圓明,獲二殊勝。

Transliteration: Hốt nhiên siêu việt thế xuất thế gian, thập phương viên minh, hoạch nhị thù thắng.

Translation: Suddenly I transcended the mundane and the transcendental worlds; throughout the ten directions a perfect, luminous oneness manifested, and I obtained two supreme states.

Commentary: When the state of still extinction had manifested, suddenly I transcended the mundane and the transcendental worlds. This refers to the realm of sentient beings and the material world. Throughout the ten directions a perfect, luminous oneness manifested. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva merged as one with the worlds of the ten directions, without obstruction. And I obtained two supreme states.

Sutra text: 一者上合十方諸佛本妙覺心。與佛如來同一慈力。

Transliteration: Nhất giả thượng hợp thập phương chư Phật bổn diệu giác tâm. Dữ Phật Như Lai đồng nhất từ lực.

Translation: First, above, I united with the fundamentally wonderful enlightened mind of all Buddhas of the ten directions. I attained the same compassionate power as the Buddhas, the Tathagatas.

Commentary: Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's compassionate mind is entirely the same as the compassionate minds of all Buddhas.

Sutra text: 二者下合十方一切六道眾生。與諸眾生同一悲仰

Transliteration: Nhị giả hạ hợp thập phương nhất thiết lục đạo chúng sanh. Dữ chư chúng sanh đồng nhất bi ngưỡng.

Translation: Second, below, I united with all living beings of the six paths throughout the ten directions. Together with living beings I share the same ngưỡng of compassion.

Commentary: Second, below, I united with all living beings of the six paths throughout the ten directions.

What are the living beings of the six paths throughout the ten directions? To take the simple aspect of human beings — eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind — these are the beings of the six paths. They are the turning in birth and death through the six paths, just as form, sound, scent, taste, touch, and mental objects are also a turning through the six paths. Those are the six paths of living beings within one's own nature. There is a mutual relationship between the inner six paths and the outer six paths. The outer six paths are the realms of gods, asuras, humans, animals, hungry ghosts, and hells. The asura realm includes all beings fond of contention.

Asuras are beings who put their contentious nature to useful service in the army and in defending their country. Asuras are those who channel their contentious nature in a bad direction, leading to such things as robbery and gangsterism. Asuras may dwell among the gods, among humans, among animals, or as ghosts. Sometimes asuras are counted among the three wholesome paths — gods, asuras, and humans. Sometimes they are ranked among the four evil destinies — hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and asuras. When asuras are grouped together with gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and hells, that grouping follows the turning wheel of birth and death in the six paths.

The Buddhas' realm is above Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, so the Bodhisattva says, "Above, I unite with the compassionate minds of the Buddhas." The beings of the six paths are in a realm lower than Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, so the Bodhisattva says, "Below, I unite with the beings of the six paths." "Living beings" are defined as those born from many causes and conditions. Many factors are involved in the birth of a living being. The Bodhisattva continues: Together with living beings I share the same compassionate ngưỡng. Living beings all thirst for and look up to the pity of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Sutra text: 世尊由我供養觀音如來。蒙彼如來授我如幻聞薰聞修金剛三昧。與佛如來同慈力故。令我身成三十二應入諸國土。

Transliteration: Thế tôn, do ngã cúng dường Quán Âm Như Lai. Mông bỉ Như Lai thọ ngã Như huyễn văn huân văn tu kim cang tam-muội. Dữ Phật Như Lai đồng từ lực cố. Linh ngã thân thành tam thập nhị ứng, nhập chư quốc độ.

Translation: World Honored One, through my making offerings to the Tathagata Avalokiteshvara, I received from that Tathagata the Vajra samadhi of illusory hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation. Because I share the same compassionate power as the Buddhas, the Tathagatas, my body has perfected thirty-two response bodies, and I can enter all lands.

Commentary: World Honored One, through my making offerings to the Tathagata Avalokiteshvara, I received from that Tathagata the Vajra samadhi of illusory hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation. "Illusory" is spoken of because one cultivates yet does not cultivate, does not cultivate yet cultivates. It means the cultivator always knows what is happening at all times and never forgets. Yet, though never forgetting, the cultivator does not actually remember them either. He does not think of them, yet neither does he forget them.

"Hearing-perfumation" means that daily, the Bodhisattva constantly cultivated the dharma-door of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature until this effort thoroughly permeated him. This is the Vajra samadhi dharma. When the cultivator develops this samadhi power, the Vajra samadhi is perfected.

Because I share the same compassionate power as the Buddhas, the Tathagatas, my body has perfected thirty-two response bodies, and I can enter all lands. I have obtained compassion-power the same as the Buddhas, which enables me to have thirty-two response bodies. Thus I can go to all lands to teach living beings.

Sutra text: 世尊若諸菩薩入三摩地。進修無漏勝解現圓。我現佛身而為說法令其解脫。

Transliteration: Thế tôn, nhược chư Bồ-tát nhập tam-ma-địa, tấn tu vô lậu, thắng giải hiện viên, ngã hiện Phật thân nhi vị thuyết pháp, linh kỳ giải thoát.

Translation: World Honored One, if there are Bodhisattvas who enter samadhi, advance in cultivation of the unconditioned, have attained superior understanding and manifest perfection, I appear before them in a Buddha's body, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation.

Commentary: World Honored One, if there are Bodhisattvas who enter samadhi, advance in cultivation of the unconditioned — they have already attained right concentration (samadhi) and wish to continue their effort to reach the true realm of no-dwelling nirvana. They are those who have attained superior understanding and manifest perfection. Their wisdom is most subtle and wonderful, and they have revealed the perfect penetration of the six sense roots. I appear before them in a Buddha's body, speak Dharma for them, and enable those Bodhisattvas to attain liberation. When I meet such beings, I at once manifest a Buddha's body. Although I myself have not yet become a Buddha, my compassionate power is the same as the Buddhas'. Through this compassionate power I can manifest a Buddha's body and speak Dharma for the ranks of Bodhisattvas, helping them reach liberation.

Sutra text: 若諸有學寂靜妙明勝妙現圓,我於彼前現獨覺身而為說法令其解脫。

Transliteration: Nhược chư hữu học tịch tĩnh diệu minh, thắng diệu hiện viên, ngã ư bỉ tiền, hiện Độc giác thân nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ giải thoát.

Translation: If there are learners who cultivate the still, wondrously luminous perfection and manifest wondrous perfection, I appear before them in the body of a Solitary Enlightened One, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation.

Commentary: If there are learners who cultivate the still, wondrously luminous perfection. "Learners" refers to those who have not yet reached the fourth fruition of Arhatship. They are those who have attained wondrous perfection — their wisdom is most supremely subtle and they have entered perfect penetration. "I appear before them in the body of a Solitary Enlightened One and speak Dharma for them, enabling them to attain liberation. For this class of beings, I shall manifest as a Solitarily Enlightened One" — meaning one of the Two Vehicles who certified to the Way when no Buddha was manifest in the world. They cultivate the dharma of the Twelvefold Conditioned Origination and become enlightened.

In spring they contemplate the white peach blossoms blooming,
In autumn they contemplate the yellow leaves falling.

They awaken to the natural principle of arising and ceasing operating through the myriad phenomena of the world. That is how the Solitarily Enlightened Ones became enlightened. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will appear as a Solitarily Enlightened One to speak Dharma for them, enabling them to become enlightened.

Sutra text: 若諸有學斷十二緣。緣斷勝性,勝妙現圓。我於彼前。現緣覺身。而為說法令其解脫。

Transliteration: Nhược chư hữu học đoạn thập nhị duyên. Duyên đoạn thắng tánh, thắng diệu hiện viên. Ngã ư bỉ tiền, hiện Duyên giác thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ giải thoát.

Translation: If there are learners who sever the twelve conditioned links, and through the severing of the links give rise to a superior nature, with wondrous perfection manifest, I appear before them in the body of a Condition-Enlightened One, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation.

Commentary: If there are learners who sever the twelve conditioned links, and through the severing of the links give rise to a superior nature. Again, "learners" refers to first-stage Arhats.

The twelve conditioned links have been explained in the earlier text. Those points are most important.
1. Ignorance conditions activity;
2. Activity conditions consciousness;
3. Consciousness conditions name-and-form;
4. Name-and-form conditions the six sense entrances;
5. The six sense entrances condition contact;
6. Contact conditions feeling;
7. Feeling conditions craving;
8. Craving conditions grasping;
9. Grasping conditions becoming;
10. Becoming conditions birth;
11. Birth conditions old age and death.

This is the door of flowing — the direction of outflow.
When ignorance ceases, activity ceases;
When activity ceases, consciousness ceases;
When consciousness ceases, name-and-form cease;
When name-and-form cease, the six entrances cease;
When the six entrances cease, contact ceases;
When contact ceases, feeling ceases;
When feeling ceases, craving ceases;
When craving ceases, grasping ceases;
When grasping ceases, becoming ceases;
When becoming ceases, birth ceases;
When birth ceases, old age and death cease.

This is the door of cessation (the direction of still extinction). Arhat cultivators of the Way become very clear about ignorance and the connections leading to arising. From birth to death, beings are born and then die in turn. We end the wheel of birth and death by first extinguishing ignorance. When ignorance is entirely cut off, the other links successively dissolve. When they sever these links, they give rise to a superior nature. "They become those whose superior nature is perfected. I (Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva) appear before them in the body of a Condition-Enlightened One, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation."

Sutra text: 若諸有學得四諦空。修道入滅勝性現圓。我於彼前現聲聞身。而為說法令其解脫。

Transliteration: Nhược chư hữu học đắc tứ đế không. Tu đạo nhập diệt thắng tánh hiện viên. Ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Thanh văn thân. Nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ giải thoát.

Translation: If there are learners who have attained the emptiness of the Four Noble Truths, cultivate the Way, enter extinction, with superior nature manifest in perfection, I appear before them in the body of a Hearers, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation.

Commentary: If there are learners who have attained the emptiness of the Four Noble Truths, cultivate the Way, and enter extinction. They may be Hearers, Arhats, who have realized the emptiness-nature of the Four Noble Truths, cultivated the Truth of the Way, and certified to the wonderful bliss of nirvana. They have attained superior nature manifest in perfection; they have revealed the state of perfect penetration. I appear before them in the body of a Hearer, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation.

Why does the Bodhisattva manifest a Hearer's body? Because only thus does he become like them, and mutual understanding comes easily. The Bodhisattva becomes a good friend, and much mutual trust is established. If one has no relationship with people, then no matter what one says, they will not believe. The Bodhisattva, as it were, befriends them in order to teach them. Hearers certify to the Way by hearing the Buddhas' discourses. They are those of the Two Vehicles.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生。欲心明悟。不犯欲塵欲身清淨。我於彼前現梵王身。而為說法令其解脫。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh, dục tâm minh ngộ, bất phạm dục trần, dục thân thanh tịnh. Ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Phạm vương thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ giải thoát.

Translation: If there are living beings whose minds wish for clear awakening, who do not offend against sense-objects of desire and wish their bodies to be pure, I appear before them in the body of a Brahma King, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation.

Commentary: If there are living beings — these beings are not Hearers, not Condition-Enlightened Ones, not Bodhisattvas; they are ordinary beings of the six paths. They are beings who wish their minds to attain clear awakening, who wish to attain enlightenment — true understanding. They are those who do not offend against worldly sense-objects of desire. They stay far from greed and desire in the world of ordinary passions, because they wish their bodies to be pure. I appear before them in the body of a Brahma King, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to attain liberation. I shall manifest as the Great Brahma Heaven King and speak Dharma for them, enabling them to attain liberation.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生欲為天主統領諸天。我於彼前現帝釋身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh dục vi thiên chủ thống lĩnh chư thiên. Ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Đế thích thân. Nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who wish to be lords of the heavens, ruling over all the heavens, I appear before them in the body of Shakra, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who wish to be lords of the heavens — that is, the Christian God. They wish to rule over all the heavens. They wish to govern the heavens. I appear before them in the body of Shakra (Śakra), speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. I manifest the body of Shakra for this kind of being. Shakra is the lord of the heavens — God.

Did you know that the Holy Mother of Catholicism is precisely Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva? Catholics believe in the Holy Mother because they wish to be reborn in the heavens. Thus Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva manifests as a goddess to teach them, enabling them to be born in the heavens. Of course, from the heavens they will fall again, but gradually they will progress. Why does Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva manifest and speak Dharma to help people be born in the heavens? His ultimate purpose is to lead beings to believe in the Buddhas. But since at the time their wish is to be born in the heavens, he teaches them how to be born in the heavens. When they fall back from the heavens, eventually they will believe in the Buddhas. Ordinary people see the time this process takes as very long, but in the Buddha's eye it is but an instant, but the blink of an eye.

This method is like parents who want their child to master an excellent trade, while the child does not want to learn that trade. The parents must indulge the child's wish to study whatever field it likes, but after a few initial failures, in the end it must change direction and study the trade the parents recommended. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's method of teaching beings is to respond to whatever wishes beings desire. But his ultimate purpose is always to bring beings to the perfection of Buddhahood.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生欲身自在遊行十方。我於彼前現自在天身。而為說法令其成就

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh dục thân tự tại, du hành thập phương, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Tự tại thiên thân. Nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who wish for a body at ease, roaming through the ten directions, I appear before them in the body of an Easeful Heaven god, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who wish for a body at ease — they wish to be at ease, to go wherever they want. I appear before them in the body of an Easeful Heaven god, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish. The gods of the Great Ease Heaven can go wherever they wish.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生欲身自在飛行虛空。我於彼前現大自在天身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh dục thân tự tại phi hành hư không, ngã ư bỉ tiền, hiện Đại Tự tại thiên thân. Nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who wish for a body at ease, flying through empty space, I appear before them in the body of a Great Easeful Heaven god, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who wish for a body at ease, flying through empty space. They wish to be at ease, their bodies transforming at will. They wish their bodies to fly through empty space. Because they have this wish, I shall rely upon the compassionate power of the Buddhas to enable them to manifest bodies as they wish. And I shall appear before them in the body of a Great Easeful Heaven god and speak Dharma for them, enabling them to accomplish their wish. The Great Easeful Heaven gods are most autonomous and full of blessings. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva manifests as one of them to help beings accomplish their wishes.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛統鬼神救護國土。我於彼前現天大將軍身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái thống quỷ thần, cứu hộ quốc độ, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Thiên Đại tướng quân thân nhi vị thuyết pháp, linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who wish to command ghosts and spirits to rescue and protect their country, I appear before them in the body of a great heavenly general, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who wish to command ghosts and spirits to rescue and protect their country. There are some people who like to command ghosts and spirits. They do this work out of a patriotic spirit, to rescue and protect the homeland. I appear before them in the body of a great heavenly general, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛統世界保護眾生。我於彼前現四天王身,而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái thống thế giới, bảo hộ chúng sanh, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Tứ thiên vương thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp, linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who delight in ruling the world and protecting living beings, I appear before them in the body of one of the Four Heavenly Kings, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who delight in ruling the world and protecting living beings. They wish to govern the world in order to protect the beings in that world; I appear before them in the body of one of the Four Heavenly Kings, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. The Four Heavenly Kings are:

1. Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Guardian of the Nation Heaven (s: Dhṛtarāṣṭra 持國天), who oversees the continent Purvavideha in the East;
2. Virūpākṣa, the Broad-Eyed Heaven (s: Virūpākṣa 廣目天), who oversees the continent Aparagodaniya in the West;
3. Virūḍhaka, the Growth Heaven (s: Virūḍhaka 増長天), who oversees the continent Jambudvipa in the South.
4. Vaiśravaṇa, the Much-Hearing Heaven, or Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa (s: Vaiśravaṇa 多聞天), who oversees the continent Uttarakuru in the North.

For those who wish to rule the world and protect living beings, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will manifest the body of one of these Four Heavenly Kings.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛生天宮驅使鬼神。我於彼前現四天王國太子身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái sanh thiên cung, khu sử quỷ thần, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Tứ thiên vương quốc Thái tử thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who wish to be born in heavenly palaces and command ghosts and spirits, I appear before them in the body of a prince, son of one of the Four Heavenly Kings, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who wish to be born in heavenly palaces, delighting in the blessings and bliss of the heavens. While in the heavens, they can command ghosts and spirits. They can order ghosts and spirits to do various tasks for them. They summon ghosts and spirits and assign them work. In fact, the ability to command ghosts and spirits is quite ordinary. People find it strange, but it really is not so. For those who wish to command ghosts and spirits, I appear before them in the body of a prince, son of one of the Four Heavenly Kings, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生樂為人主。我於彼前現人王身,而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh nhạo vi nhơn chủ, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Nhơn vương thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who delight in being rulers of people, I appear before them in the body of a human king, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are people who delight in ruling the human realm, I at once appear before them in the body of a human king to speak Dharma for them.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛主族姓世間推讓。我於彼前現長者身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái chủ tộc tánh, thế gian suy nhượng, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện trưởng giả thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who wish to head a clan of noble family, respected by the world, I appear before them in the body of an elder, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who wish to head a clan of noble family, respected by the world. They delight in wealth and in presiding over a great clan. They wish to be respected by everyone in the world. I appear before them in the body of an elder, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. I shall manifest the body of a wealthy elder before them to speak Dharma for them.

A person must have ten virtues to earn the title of elder. They are:
1. Noble nature: born of a great noble family.
2. High position: holding the post of a senior official.
3. Great wealth: abundant possessions, rich.
4. Awesome courage: dignified and valiant.
5. Profound wisdom: lofty and deep wisdom.
6. Senior age: advanced in years, weighty in virtue.
7. Pure conduct: lofty, pure character, worthy to be a model.
8. Complete propriety: in dealing with people and things, always courteous.
9. Praised above: praised by kings above.
10. Respected below: accorded the hearts of the people below.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛談名言清淨其 居。我於彼前現居士身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái đàm danh ngôn, thanh tịnh kỳ cư. Ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện cư sĩ thân. Nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who delight in discussing fine words and living a pure life, I appear before them in the body of a lay follower, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who delight in discussing fine words. They may delight in poetry, or in the fine works of famous writers. They may memorize many works of this kind by heart. They delight in living a pure life. If asked to do something they consider unworthy of such pursuits, they will have nothing to do with it. I appear before them in the body of a lay follower, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. I shall manifest the body of a lay follower and speak Dharma for them.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛治國土,剖斷邦邑。我於彼前現宰官身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái trị quốc độ, phẫu đoán bang ấp. Ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Tể quan thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who delight in governing the country, judging and deciding matters of the states and cities, I appear before them in the body of a minister, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who delight in governing the country, judging and deciding matters of the states and cities. They settle the great affairs of the nation. I appear before them in the body of a minister, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. I shall manifest as a prime minister or high official to speak Dharma for them.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生愛諸數術攝衛自居。我於彼前現婆羅門身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sanh ái chư số thuật, nhiếp vệ tự cư, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Bà-la-môn thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who delight in the arts of reckoning, gathering their minds and guarding themselves, I appear before them in the body of a Brahman, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who delight in the arts of reckoning. They delight in studying reckoning arts — that is, astronomy and geography, yin-yang and the five phases. "Arts" means medicine, divination, astrology, water mantras and written charms for nursing body and mind and protecting life. "Reckoning" refers to using numbers and calculations to predict the future. "Arts" also refers to demonic magic and other crafts. It further means the mantras of non-Buddhist paths. The Brahma-heaven mantra of the Kapila outsiders used by Maudgalyayana's mother is an example of this kind. These people delight in gathering their minds and guarding themselves. They understand that if they learn a mantra or a teaching, that mantra and teaching can protect them.

I appear before them in the body of a Brahman, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. Brahmanism is a religion of India. That name means "originating from purity" and represents the cultivation of pure conduct. These people have a great many magical arts. They can recite mantras and have many magical crafts. And so Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, ever according with all beings, also manifests as a Brahman to speak Dharma, so that such people may obtain what they wish.

Sutra text: 若有男子好學出家持諸戒律。我於彼前現比丘身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu nam tử hiếu học xuất gia, trì chư giới luật, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện tỷ-khưu thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there is a good man who delights in learning to leave the home-life and upholds the precepts, I appear before him in the body of a bhikshu, speak Dharma for him, and help him accomplish his wish.

Commentary: If there is a good man who delights in learning to leave the home-life and upholds the precepts. Such people study the sutras and resolve to live the homeless life. Which homes do they leave? They leave three kinds of homes:
1. They leave the worldly home.
2. They leave the home of afflictions.
3. They leave the home of the three realms.

The worldly home is one's family. The home of afflictions means dwelling in ignorance. We must escape from the home of ignorance. The three realms, also called the Triple Existence, refer to life in the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm. It is not until one leaves the home of the Triple Realm that one certifies to Arhatship.

When such people leave home, they receive and uphold the precepts. The precepts are most important. One who keeps the precepts cannot lie or exaggerate. At the minimum, keep the five precepts: no killing, no stealing, no sexual misconduct, no lying, and no intoxicants or drugs. The precepts here, of course, are not only the first ones. Such people receive and uphold the five precepts, the eight precepts, the Bodhisattva's ten major and forty-eight minor precepts, the bhikshu's 250 precepts and the bhikshuni's 348 precepts. They keep the precepts and never violate them. I appear before them in the body of a bhikshu, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

A bhikshu has three meanings:
1. Mendicant;
2. Frightener of demons;
3. Destroyer of evil.

Every day bhikshus carry their bowls to beg for food. They do not cook food for themselves. Thus they are called mendicants. There are three ordination platforms when receiving the complete precepts. When ascending the platform to receive bhikshu precepts, the Karmadana master asks:
"Are you a great hero?"
The precept candidate answers: "Yes, I am a great hero."
The Karmadana asks further: "Have you brought forth the bodhi resolve?"
The candidate answers: "Yes, I have brought forth the bodhi resolve."
Frightener of demons: When a person has been transmitted the bhikshu precepts, the earth-traveling yakshas pass this news to the space-traveling yakshas, the news passes to the flying yakshas, until it reaches the demons on the heavens of the Six Desires. They announce: "A person in the world has just left home and become a bhikshu." This terrifies the Demon King, who says, "My retinue will lose one person and the Buddha's retinue gains one more."

Destroyer of evil: Which evil does a bhikshu destroy? The evil of afflictions. One never knows why people give rise to afflictions all the time. When they give rise to afflictions, they lose every talent except the ability to turn toward evil. For example, a lifelong vegetarian may want to quit, and first he decides to end his eating of pure food. He decides: "I will eat meat." Once affliction has arisen, they forget everything except finding ways to create evil karma. Or suppose someone has quit smoking for a long time. When he gives up, the first thing he does is grab a cigarette. And before long he will be back to heroin, opium, and every drug in a single breath!

He inhales and exhales like a storm. He breathes in and out very rapidly, as if he had become an immortal who can exhale clouds and spit out mist. An alcoholic swears he will never touch another drop. But when he gets angry about something, he buys a bottle and drinks to drown his sorrow. Who would guess that the more he drinks, the more desperate he becomes. When he wakes after a drunken binge, every joint in his body aches. Ask anyone who has drunk alcohol, and they will tell you the next morning is truly terrible. If he is broke at the time, he can do nothing but endure. But if a little money remains, of course he will buy another bottle and start drinking again. He knows only one thing: to be drunk.

In general, when afflictions arise, you will do things you would never ordinarily do. This happens even when someone has sworn never to kill — yet when affliction flares up, he utterly disregards everything and decides to kill everyone in the world. He grabs a knife and sets to work! Thus afflictions are to be avoided. Do not give rise to afflictions. You must leave the home of afflictions. We also wish to leave the home of the Triple Realm, and so leaving home must fully embody these three meanings.

Sutra text: 若有女子好學出家持諸禁戒。我於彼前現比丘尼身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu nữ tử hiếu học xuất gia trì chư cấm giới. ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện tỷ-khưu-ni thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there is a believing woman who wishes to study to leave the home-life and uphold the precepts, I appear before her in the body of a bhikshuni, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Commentary: If there is a believing woman who wishes to study to leave the home-life and uphold the precepts. She wishes to study the Buddhadharma. She also wishes to leave the worldly home, leave the home of afflictions, and leave the home of the Triple Realm. Women must uphold more precepts than men. They must keep 348 precepts. It is commonly said that women have bodies with five kinds of outflows. Hence they must keep more precepts. I appear before her in the body of a bhikshuni, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Sutra text: 若有男子樂持五戒。我於彼前現優婆塞身。而為說法令其成就。若[1]復女子五戒自居。我於彼前現優婆夷身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu nam tử nhạo trì ngũ giới, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Ưu-bà-tắc thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu. Nhược phục nữ tử ngũ giới tự cư, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện Ưu-bà-di thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there is a good man who delights in upholding the five precepts, I appear before him in the body of an upasaka, speak Dharma for him, and help him accomplish his wish. If there is a believing woman who abides by the five precepts, I appear before her in the body of an upasika, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Commentary: If there is a good man who delights in upholding the five precepts — no killing, no stealing, no sexual misconduct, no lying, no alcohol — I appear before him in the body of an upasaka, speak Dharma for him, and help him accomplish his wish. I shall manifest as a layman to speak Dharma for them. If there is a believing woman who delights in the five precepts — she too wishes to keep these precepts — I appear before her in the body of an upasika. I shall manifest as a laywoman and speak Dharma for her to help her accomplish her wish.

Sutra text: 若有女人內政立身以修家國。我於彼前現女主身。及國夫人命婦大家。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu nữ nhơn nội chánh lập thân, dĩ tu gia quốc, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện nữ chủ thân, cập quốc phu nhân mạng phụ đại gia, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there is a woman who establishes herself in domestic administration to regulate the family or the nation, I appear before her in the body of a queen, or in the bodies of a king's consort, a titled lady, or a noblewoman, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Commentary: If there is a woman who establishes herself in domestic administration to regulate the family or the nation. Sometimes these women manage household affairs; sometimes they hold power in the court, administering the nation's business. I appear before her in the body of a queen, or in the bodies of a king's consort, a titled lady, or a noblewoman, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva may manifest as a woman administering state affairs, or as the wife of a ruler. Sometimes the Bodhisattva manifests as a powerful titled lady or an elegant, refined woman of society. In all these cases, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva responds to their wishes.

Sutra text: 若有眾生不壞男根。我於彼前現童男身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu chúng sanh bất hoại nam căn, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện đồng nam thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings whose male faculty is intact, I appear before them in the body of a young boy, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings whose male faculty is intact. For young men who have never known women and are still pure, I appear before them in the body of a young boy, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若有處女愛樂處身不求侵暴。我於彼前現童女身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu xử nữ ái nhạo xử thân, bất cầu xâm bạo, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện đồng nữ thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there is a maiden who delights in remaining a virgin and does not seek violation, I appear before her in the body of a young girl, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Commentary: If there is a maiden — meaning a woman who has never known a man and has never married. Who delights in remaining a virgin and does not seek violation. They do not wish to be intimate with men, to marry, or to undergo the experience of being violated. I appear before her in the body of a young girl, speak Dharma for her, and help her accomplish her wish.

Sutra text: 若有諸天樂出天倫。我現天身而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu chư thiên nhạo xuất thiên luân, ngã hiện thiên thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are gods who delight in transcending their heavenly kind, I manifest a heavenly body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are gods who delight in transcending their heavenly kind. These goddesses and gods no longer wish to remain in the heavens; they wish to escape the Triple Realm. I manifest a heavenly body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish. Because they wish to transcend the heavens, I manifest before them, using every expedient to help them obtain what they desire.

Sutra text: 若有諸龍樂出龍倫。我現龍身而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu chư long nhạo xuất long luân, ngã hiện long thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are dragons who delight in transcending their draconic kind, I manifest a dragon's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are dragons who delight in transcending their draconic kind. The common view of the present age is that dragons are not real. Some people acknowledge the ancient legends of dragons, very huge and terrifying. There is no way to speak with certainty about the former view, but dragons are real. Where are they? The dragon palace lies beneath the sea. "We have plumbed the depths; why have we never passed that place?" you will ask. If you could find their dwelling, they would no longer be true dragons, for dragons are spiritual beings. They have spiritual powers and can transform themselves to be large or small at will. They can make themselves as vast as empty space. They can shrink as small as a mote of dust if needed. They can suddenly vanish, then reappear in an instant.

Their spiritual powers grant them the ability to transform in countless ways. Why, with such powers, do they bear the bodies of animals? Because in former lives' cultivation, they set their minds on the Great Vehicle, but they refused to keep the precepts. They were of the type "hasty with the vehicle, lax with the precepts." They were most careless. Because they were most zealous toward Great Vehicle cultivation — hasty with the vehicle — they obtained spiritual powers. But because they did not keep the precepts, they fell among animals. If dragons resolve to transcend the dragon's body, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will manifest a dragon's body before them, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若有藥叉樂度本倫。我於彼前現藥叉身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược hữu dược-xoa nhạo độ bổn luân, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện dược-xoa thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are yakshas who delight in transcending their own kind, I appear before them in a yaksha's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are yakshas. "Yaksha" is Sanskrit, translated into Chinese as "swift," meaning "speedy." It is also translated as "courageous and strong," meaning brave and mighty. Yakshas are a kind of ghost-spirit. There are three main kinds of ghost-spirits:
1. Earth-traveling ghosts;
2. Flying ghosts;
3. Space-traveling ghosts.

In the Shurangama Mantra there is the line: yaksha graha. In the mantra, the names of the kings of all the ghosts are called forth. Each ghost king commands many lower ghosts, and when the king's name is called, all the other ghosts and spirits must reverently obey the king's command. If they wish to transcend their own kind — they no longer wish to be ghost-spirits — I appear before them in a yaksha's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will manifest as a yaksha ghost to help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若乾闥婆樂脫其倫。我於彼前現乾闥婆身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược càn-thát-bà nhạo thoátkỳ luân, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện càn-thát-bà thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are gandharvas who delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them in a gandharva's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are gandharvas. "Gandharva" is Sanskrit, translated into Chinese as "fragrance-perfumed," because smelling fragrance creates their consciousness. They are the musicians of the Jade Emperor. When the Jade Emperor burns agarwood incense, they smell the fragrance and are at once drawn to it. They come to play music to delight the Jade Emperor. These gandharvas wish to transcend their kind; they no longer wish to be gandharvas. I appear before them in a gandharva's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若阿修羅樂脫其倫。我於彼前現阿修羅身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược a-tu-la nhạo thoát kỳ luân, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện a-tu-la thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are asuras who delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them in an asura's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are asuras who delight in transcending their kind. They wish to leave the retinue of the asura kind; I appear before them in an asura's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

This section covers the beings of the eight divisions of ghosts and spirits, yet the Shurangama Sutra makes no mention of the garudas. But the Universal Door chapter of the Dharma Flower Sutra does mention that Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva also manifests as a garuda.

"Garuda" is a transliteration of Sanskrit, meaning the golden-winged great peng bird. The garuda is one of the Eight Divisions, and the fact that the sutra text does not mention this kind is probably due to an omission error in copying the sutra, or perhaps it is understood to be included in the general category of "living beings" mentioned above.

Garudas eat only dragons. This bird's wings span 330 great yojanas. A small yojana equals 40 Chinese li (one li being about one-third of a mile). A middle yojana equals 60 li. A great yojana equals 80 li. With a single flap of its wings, the golden-winged great peng drains the sea dry. Its strength is that great. When the sea water has been drained dry, the dragons are exposed. In this way, the garudas were about to exterminate the entire dragon race. So the dragons came to see the Buddha to beg for rescue. "The golden-winged great peng birds (garudas) are nearly driving our dragon retinue to extinction. What should we do?"

They looked up to the Buddha's compassion for rescue; they hoped the Buddha would stop the golden-winged great peng birds from eating the dragons of their retinue. The Buddha gave the dragons a strip of his kashaya robe to wrap upon their horns. After that, the golden-winged great peng birds dared not eat dragons. With nothing to eat, the golden-winged great peng birds also came to cry to the Buddha, begging him to rescue them. The Buddha asked, "No one eats you; why do you come seeking rescue?"

The golden-winged great peng birds answered: "True, nothing threatens us, but there is nothing to eat; we shall starve to death. You no longer permit us to eat dragons; we shall die." Then they asked the Buddha in his compassion to devise a way to rescue them.

"You have nothing to eat, is that so? Very well, the Tathagata will help you. Henceforth, whenever the Tathagata and his bhikshu disciples take their meal, food will be offered for you to eat. You must no longer eat dragons."

That is why, when taking the noontime meal, the Sangha often takes some food outside to offer to the golden-winged great peng birds. This sutra text makes no mention of the golden-winged great peng birds, but we should know that all eight divisions of ghosts and spirits are included among these beings.

Sutra text: 若緊陀羅樂脫其倫。我於彼前現緊陀羅身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược khẩn-đà-la nhạo thoát kỳ luân, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện khẩn-đà-la thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are kinnaras who delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them in a kinnara's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are kinnaras who delight in transcending their kind,

"Kinnara" is Sanskrit, translated into Chinese as "doubtful spirits." They are so called because when they manifest in human form, they bear a horn upon their heads. They are also another kind of music spirit that often plays music for the Jade Emperor. I appear before them in a kinnara's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若摩呼羅伽樂脫其倫。我於彼前現摩呼羅伽身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược ma-hô-la-già nhạo thoát kỳ luân, ngã ư bỉ tiền hiện ma-hô-la-già thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are mahoragas who delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them in a mahoraga's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are mahoragas — "Mahoraga" is Sanskrit, translated into Chinese as "great python spirits," also called earth dragons. The dragons mentioned above can travel through the sky and are called heavenly dragons. These pythons, also called dragons, are confined to the ground. They have no spiritual powers. Mahoragas are also beings of the eight divisions of ghosts and spirits. If mahoragas delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them in a mahoraga's body, speak Dharma for them, and help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若諸眾生樂人修人。我現人身而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư chúng sinh nhạo nhân tu nhân, ngã hiện nhân thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are living beings who delight in the human state and cultivate to be human, I manifest a human body, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are living beings who delight in the human state and cultivate to be human. They wish, life after life, always to obtain a human body. Thus Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva says, "I manifest a human body, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish." He will speak Dharma for these beings to help them accomplish their wish.

Sutra text: 若諸非人有形無形。有想無想樂度其倫。我於彼前皆現其身。而為說法令其成就。

Transliteration: Nhược chư phi nhơn, hữu hình vô hình, hữu tưởng vô tưởng nhạo độ kỳ luân, ngã ư bỉ tiền giai hiện kỳ thân, nhi vị thuyết pháp linh kỳ thành tựu.

Translation: If there are non-human beings — with form or without form, with thought or without thought — who delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them all in bodies like theirs, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish.

Commentary: If there are non-humans. This refers to animals and other creatures different from humans — beings either with form or without form, either with thought or without thought. If such beings as these delight in transcending their kind, I appear before them all in bodies like theirs, speak Dharma for them, and enable them to accomplish their wish.

"With form" means having an actual visible form that can be seen.

"Without form" means having no form.

There are many beings "with thought." Beings "without thought" include earth, stone, wood, iron... Beings "without form" are in fact also beings, but they have been dispersed into emptiness and fallen into oblivion. Such cases are usually of the intermediate-bardo body, and at some point they undergo rebirth again and return as humans.

Sutra text: 是名妙淨三十二應,入國土身。皆以三昧聞薰聞修, 無作妙力自在成就 。

Transliteration: Thị danh diệu tịnh tam thập nhị ứng, nhập quốc độ thân. Giai dĩ tam muội văn huân văn tu vô tác diệu lực tự tại thành tựu.

Translation: These are called the thirty-two sublimely pure response bodies, all entering lands, perfected at ease through the samadhi of hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation and the wondrous power of non-doing.

Commentary: These are called the thirty-two sublimely pure response bodies, all entering lands, perfected at ease through the samadhi of hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation. The cultivator develops the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature through daily cultivation, and applies the wondrous power of non-doing. "Non-doing" refers to the subtle principle of "non-action" — with this principle, one need not pass through concepts of deliberation and processes of thought to find ideas, as everyone must do when wishing to do something. Bodhisattvas do not imagine or deliberate over such matters. In samadhi, they can do all things. In the samadhi of hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation they can attain the wondrous power of non-doing. And by this method, they perfect the power of ease. Quite naturally, all matters are settled well.

Sutra text: 世尊我復以此聞薰聞修金剛三昧無作妙力,與諸十方三世六道,一切眾生同悲仰故,令諸眾生於我身心,獲十四種無畏功德。

Transliteration: Thế tôn, ngã phục dĩ thử văn huân văn tu kim cang tam muội vô tác diệu lực, dữ chư thập phương tam thế lục đạo, nhất thiết chúng sanh đồng bi ngưỡng cố, linh chư chúng sanh ư ngã thân tâm, hoạch thập tứ chủng vô uý công đức.

Translation: World Honored One, further, through this Vajra samadhi of hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation and its wondrous power of non-doing, and because I share the same compassionate ngưỡng with all beings of the six paths in the ten directions and three periods, I enable living beings who merge into my body and mind to obtain fourteen kinds of fearlessness merit.

Commentary: World Honored One, further, through this Vajra samadhi of hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation and its wondrous power of non-doing, and because I share the same compassionate ngưỡng with all beings of the six paths in the ten directions and three periods — having a compassionate ngưỡng in the Buddhadharma toward beings of the six paths: gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and hells.

I go throughout the ten directions and three periods — past, present, and future. I cultivate the Vajra samadhi of hearing-perfumation and hearing-cultivation, and I need not deliberate or calculate about a task before carrying it out.

Enabling living beings who merge into my body and mind to obtain fourteen kinds of fearlessness merit. I have attained fourteen fearlessness merits.

Sutra text: 一者由我不自觀音,以觀觀者, 令彼十方苦惱眾生。觀其音聲即得解脫。

Transliteration: Nhất giả do ngã bất tự quán âm, dĩ quán quán giả, linh bỉ thập phương khổ não chúng sanh, quán kỳ âm thinh tức đắc giải thoát.

Translation: First, because I do not regard sounds by myself, but regard the regarder, I enable the suffering beings of the ten directions to regard their sounds and at once attain liberation.

Commentary: This is one of the fourteen fearlessness merits. First, because I do not regard sounds by myself, but regard the regarder, I enable the suffering beings of the ten directions in the three periods to regard their sounds and at once attain liberation.

It is not that he regards only the sounds of himself alone; he regards the sounds of beings in the world. "Because my effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature has been perfected, I need not regard myself. Rather, I can regard all beings throughout the world and help those suffering beings attain liberation from suffering. I listen to their cries of suffering, and I rescue them to liberation."

Sutra text: 二者知見旋復,令諸眾生設入大火火不能燒。

Transliteration: Nhị giả tri kiến triền phục, linh chư chúng sanh thiết nhập đại hoả, hoả bất năng thiêu.

Translation: Second, my knowledge and views having turned back, I enable beings, though they enter a great fire, not to be burned by the fire.

Commentary: My knowledge and views having turned back — meaning Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva has the function of shining the light back into his own mind — so I can enable beings, though they enter a great fire, not to be burned by the fire. If beings constantly cultivate and uphold Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, though they walk into a raging fire, the fire cannot burn them.

Sutra text: 三者觀聽旋復。令諸眾生大水所漂,水不能溺。

Transliteration: Tam giả quán thính triền phục, linh chư chúng sanh đại thuỷ sở phiêu, thuỷ bất năng nịch.

Translation: Third, my regarding and hearing having turned back, I enable beings swept away by great waters not to be drowned by the waters.

Commentary: Someone thinks: "I will test whether Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva truly responds. I will sit upon a pile of firewood and set it ablaze to see whether it burns."

In that case, you will be burned at once. "Then why does the sutra say that if one enters a raging fire, the fire will not burn?" That is because of the word "if" — meaning it only happens when you have no calculation at all.

Someone else says, "Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva says that if a person falls into deep water, they will not drown, so I will jump into the sea to test whether I drown." Certainly you will drown. Only when you unexpectedly meet with suffering or peril will Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva rescue you. But if you deliberately scheme to test him, you will receive no response, because fundamentally you do not believe in Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. If you truly believed, there would be no reason to test. The best course is not to test him.

Sutra text: 四者斷滅妄想,心無殺害。令諸眾生入諸鬼國鬼不能害。

Transliteration: Tứ giả đoạn diệt vọng tưởng, tâm vô sát hại, linh chư chúng sanh nhập chư quỷ quốc, quỷ bất năng hại.

Translation: Fourth, having cut off and extinguished false thoughts, with a mind free of killing, I enable beings entering ghost countries not to be harmed by ghosts.

Commentary: If false thoughts have been entirely cut off, and you no longer have a single thought of killing, and if you recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, then beings entering the dwellings of rakshasa ghosts can avoid being murdered by them.

Sutra text: 五者薰聞成聞。六根銷復同於聲聽。能令眾生臨當被害刀段段壞。使其兵戈猶如割水,亦如吹光性無搖動。

Transliteration: Ngũ giả huân văn thành văn. Lục căn tiêu phục đồng ư thanh thính. Năng linh chúng sanh lâm đương bị hại đao đoạn đoạn hoại. Sử kỳ binh qua du như cát thuỷ, diệc như xuy quang tánh vô dao động.

Translation: Fifth, through perfuming hearing into accomplished hearing, the six sense roots dissolve and return to be one with sound and hearing. I can enable beings, at the point of being harmed, to have knives break into pieces, making weapons that touch the body like cutting water, or like blowing upon light — the nature unmoved.

Commentary: Fifth, through perfuming hearing into accomplished hearing. The six sense roots all dissolve, returning to the original nature, one with the nature of hearing — meaning, when the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature has been perfected, the six roots function interchangeably. Thus I can enable beings, at the point of being harmed, to have knives break into pieces. For instance, suppose someone takes a knife intending to cut off another's head. The moment the knife touches the head, the knife shatters into fragments. I can make sharp weapons touching a person's body like cutting water, like blowing upon light — the nature unmoved. I can make a sharp weapon about to chop someone's shoulder like cutting into water; that is, when the knife passes through the shoulder, it simply passes through, and no wound remains. Or I can make the knife cut like blowing upon a light — that is, utterly without effect — for no matter how you blow upon a light, the light does not flicker.

Sutra text: 六者聞薰精明明遍法界, 則諸幽暗性不能全。能令眾生藥叉羅剎鳩槃茶鬼,及毘舍遮富單那等,雖近其傍目不能視。

Transliteration: Lục giả văn huân tinh minh minh biến pháp giới, tắc chư u ám tánh bất năng toàn. Năng linh chúng sanh dược-xoa, la-sát, cưu-bàn-trà quỷ, cập tỳ-xá-già, phú- đan-na đẳng, tuy cận kỳ bàng, mục bất năng thị.

Translation: Sixth, through perfuming hearing into luminous essence shining throughout the Dharma Realm, all dark natures can no longer remain whole. I enable beings — though yakshas, rakshasas, kumbhanda ghosts, and pishachas, putanas… come close beside them — to remain unseen by their eyes.

Commentary: Sixth, through perfuming hearing into luminous essence — meaning when the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature has been perfected — shining throughout the Dharma Realm, all dark natures can no longer remain whole. I enable beings — though yakshas, rakshasas, kumbhanda ghosts, and pishachas, putanas… come close beside them — to remain unseen by their eyes.

Yakshas are male ghosts; rakshasas are female ghosts. Both kinds of ghosts are most vicious. Their food is human flesh. They have mantras capable of dispelling the stench of corpses so they can eat the flesh. Kumbhandas are also the name of a kind of ghost, shaped like a round barrel, bringing nightmares to humans. For instance, while asleep, people see strange apparitions appear; though in the dream their spirits remain most alert, still they cannot move their bodies. They become paralyzed under the control of this nightmare-bringing ghost. Sometimes, when a person's yang energy is weakened and yin energy prevails, the person may be paralyzed for quite a long time, and that ghost may cause the person to die. This is a kind of ghost very numerous in the world.

Pishachas are ghosts that feed on human essence and also on the essence of grains. Putanas. They can make people fall ill and run fevers. If you cultivate the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature, or if you recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, then these ghosts cannot see you, though they come beside you — because you emit a light that frightens them. Indeed, owls and bats can see at all times. Since ghosts belong to yin, they cannot see you if you emit yang light. They see you only when you emit yin energy.

Sutra text: 七者音性圓銷。觀聽返入離諸塵妄。能令眾生禁繫枷鎖所不能著。

Transliteration: Thất giả âm tánh viên tiêu, quán thính phản nhập, ly chư trần vọng. Năng linh chúng sanh cấm hệ già toả sở bất năng trước.

Translation: Seventh, the nature of sound completely dissolved, my regarding and hearing turned back inward, apart from all false sense-objects. I can enable beings to be untouched by fetters, shackles, cangues, and locks.

Commentary: Seventh, the nature of sound completely dissolved, my regarding and hearing turned back inward, apart from all false sense-objects. There is no more sound, not even the nature of hearing, once the cultivator has turned the regarding-nature and the hearing-nature back into the self-nature. The cultivator leaves behind all false sense-objects and false thoughts. Then I can enable beings to be untouched by fetters, shackles, cangues, and locks. If you recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, all locks and fetters fall away by themselves. This happens very often; a number of people have had this experience. That is not merely talk — if a person sincerely recites Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, there will be such a response.

Someone had committed a crime and was locked in prison. He and seven or eight other prisoners together recited Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name. How did they know to do this? They knew a monk and begged the monk to rescue them from their miserable plight. The monk told them: "If you want me to rescue you, you must single-mindedly uphold Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name; you will escape this perilous situation." The prisoners all recited Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name for three days and three nights; locks, fetters, and chains suddenly came undone and they were free. But they still did not leave, thinking: "What meaning is there in our own escape when so many others remain imprisoned here?" So they told the other prisoners to recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name. After two more days of reciting together, the locks on those prisoners' shackles also came undone entirely. They all returned home. After that, they all single-mindedly recited Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name. They recited so sincerely that they moved the villagers to bring forth the resolve to cultivate.

Sutra text: 八者滅音圓聞,遍生慈力。能令眾生經過嶮路,賊不能劫。

Transliteration: Bát giả diệt âm viên văn, biến sanh từ lực, năng linh chúng sanh kinh quá hiểm lộ, tặc bất năng kiếp.

Translation: Eighth, the object of sound extinguished and hearing perfected, compassionate power arises everywhere, enabling beings passing along dangerous roads not to be robbed by bandits.

Commentary: Eighth, the object of sound extinguished and hearing perfected, compassionate power arises everywhere. When sound has vanished and the hearing-nature has achieved perfect penetration, compassionate power arises vastly. That is the sound of the ordinary world, and through returning the hearing to hear the self-nature one's hearing-nature achieves perfect penetration — meaning one does not use the mind-consciousness to recognize hearing, yet one still hears every sound.

Sutra text: 九者薰聞離塵,色所不劫。能令一切多婬眾生遠離貪欲。

Transliteration: Cửu giả huân văn ly trần, sắc sở bất kiếp, năng linh nhất thiết đa dâm chúng sanh viễn ly tham dục.

Translation: Ninth, through perfuming hearing, apart from sense-objects, forms cannot captivate; I can enable all lustful beings to leave greed and desire far behind.

Commentary: The ninth fearlessness power is separation from lust. Through perfuming hearing into purity, apart from sense-objects, forms, sounds... cannot drag one away. If a person daily cultivates the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature until perfection, they can leave the ordinary sense-object realms far behind.
