In particular, they can leave the defiled realm of form-objects.

We should not think beauty wonderful to get involved with. If you delight in beauty, it will rob your household of all its treasures. It will devour the precious ancient treasures and steal them all away. Rather, one should:
Nhãn kiến sắc trần nội vô hữu
Nhĩ văn thế sự tâm bất tri.
The eye sees forms, yet within nothing remains.
The ear hears worldly affairs, yet the mind does not discern.

When you see beauty, your mind should be as if seeing nothing at all. If you see beauty and your mind stirs, then ask yourself why your mind did not stir before you saw it. Do not let beauty rob you of the wealth in your own home.

Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva says: I can enable lustful beings to leave greed and desire far behind.

A passage in the Universal Door of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva in the Dharma Flower Sutra says: "If there are beings with much lust who constantly revere and recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, they at once leave lust behind."

That is also the representative meaning of the sutra text. "Much greed and desire" refers especially to sexual desire. The greatest problem in human life, the nearly insoluble problem, is sexual desire. Seeing through the entanglement of men and women and setting it aside — that is true freedom. If you cannot see through it and set it aside, you can have no freedom, and you cannot become enlightened. If you are truly honest in your effort, then when eating, you do not know you are eating; when dressing, you do not know you are wearing clothes. If you can forget eating and dressing, then you will all the more easily renounce everything external.

If a man can forget his girlfriend and a woman can forget her boyfriend — if you can smash this realm to pieces — then your effort has some substance. You are more or less attached to your siblings, to your sons and daughters, and to all your relatives. To study the Buddhadharma, you must set down everything. While studying the Buddhadharma, you should pay attention to nothing else. You should be as one beginning anew; forget all past affairs. In that way, the waters of the Buddhadharma can permeate the bodhi mind. If you cannot set down everything and cannot renounce anything, then the waters of the Buddhadharma cannot nourish the bodhi mind. If you can constantly recite the name and revere Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, then your lustful mind will vanish.

The most important matter in cultivation is utterly severing thoughts of lust. If you cannot do this, you cannot leave the Triple Realm. You cannot resolve to become enlightened yet remain unable to leave behind this world's experiences. If you cannot detach from worldly romances, you cannot become a Buddha. You cannot hope for both. Confucius also said:

One cannot have both fish and bear's paw at once.

Though people like eating fish and bear's paw, they cannot eat both at the same time. In the same way, you cannot enjoy worldly pleasures and transcendental blessings at the same time. You wish to become a Buddha, yet you cannot leave the five worldly desires of wealth, beauty, fame, food, and sleep. Then there is no way to succeed.

Sutra text: 十者純音無塵,根境圓融,無對所對,能令一切忿恨眾生離諸嗔恚。

Transliteration: Thập giả thuần âm vô trần, căn cảnh viên dung, vô đối sở đối, năng linh nhất thiết phẫn hận chúng sanh ly chư sân khuể.

Translation: Tenth, I retain only the pure single perfect sound, with no object of sound-dust; root and realm perfectly interfused, with no opposing subject and object, I enable all resentful and hateful beings to leave behind anger and hatred.

Commentary: The tenth fearlessness power is: I retain only the pure single perfect sound, with no object of sound-dust; root and realm perfectly interfused.

When one has turned the hearing back to hear one's own nature, sound becomes pure — which only means there is no sound at all within it. Sound is void and still, and sound-dust is extinct. At that point only the interfusion of the six roots and six sense-objects remains. In this world, no matter how evil anything is, it can become good if you know how to handle it. And everything good can become evil if you do not know how to handle it. Earlier in the sutra text the Buddhas of the ten directions instructed Ananda that the six sense-root thieves are precisely the cause of error, and that these same six roots are what can enable us to perfect Buddhahood.

It is the six roots and nothing else. If you know how to use them, they will help you. If you do not know how to use them, they will destroy you. It is like money: when you have money, if you know you should do meritorious deeds and good works to benefit people, then the money is not wasted. But if you use money for drugs, gambling, and other unwholesome things, you have used your money to create karmic obstructions. This principle is the same with the six roots.

When sound is gone and root and sense-object are perfectly interfused, there is no more opposing subject and object. It is non-dual; it has become one substance. Thus there are no more six roots or six sense-objects; and so the six roots are just the six roots and the six sense-objects are just the six sense-objects. There is no more conflict between the six roots and the six sense-objects when the cultivator reaches this state. Thus I can enable beings to leave greed, anger, delusion, and hatred far behind.

I can make beings' hot tempers, fierce minds, and resentful hearts vanish. "Anger and hatred" refer to wrathful minds and afflictions. The Dharma Flower Sutra says: "If a person is full of anger, constantly reveres and recites Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, then anger can be eradicated."

The essential point here is constancy of recitation. It is not reciting today and forgetting tomorrow; reciting in the morning and not reciting at night; nor reciting this month and not the next. You must recite daily in your effort to deserve to be called constant in recitation. "Reverence" does not mean you recite the Buddha's name yet do not believe in the Buddha. You harbor doubt: "Is it really so? Is there such power?" Once you start raising questions, you will never succeed. Thus with faith, constantly and reverently reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, you will no longer have an angry mind, and you will no longer have a violently afflicted mind. You have left those behind.

Sutra text: 十一者,銷塵旋明法界身心。猶如瑠璃,朗徹無礙。能令一切昏鈍性障,諸阿顛迦永離癡暗。

Transliteration: Thập nhất giả, tiêu trần triền minh pháp giới thân tâm. Du như lưu li, lãng triệt vô ngại. Năng linh nhất thiết hôn độn tánh chướng, chư a-điên-ca vĩnh ly si ám.

Translation: Eleventh, sense-objects dissolved, I turn the hearing back to the originally luminous nature; body, mind, and Dharma Realm bright as vaidurya, clear through and unobstructed. I enable all dull and stupid beings with obstructed natures, all atyantikas, forever to leave delusion and darkness.

Commentary: The eleventh fearlessness power is: sense-objects dissolved, I turn the hearing back to the originally luminous nature. When the realm of the six roots and six sense-objects has dissolved, I emit light. Body, mind, and Dharma Realm bright as vaidurya. Body and mind are the Dharma Realm; the Dharma Realm is body and mind. They become one. Body and mind pervade the Dharma Realm — is that not the Buddhas' realm? That is also Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's realm. Body and mind become like vaidurya jewels, clear through and unobstructed. From within one can see straight through to the outside; from the outside one can see straight through to the inside. There is no more inside or outside, small or large. Like the Chan Master Da Xiu of Ling Yen Mountain. He deserved such a name. The Master made himself a stone tomb just large enough to sit in. Then he made a stone door outside, carving upon it this couplet:

Vô đại vô tiểu, vô nội ngoại
Tự tu tự liễu, tự an bài.

In English:
Neither great nor small, neither inside nor outside.
Cultivate oneself, understand oneself, arrange for oneself.

Provisional translation:
Neither great nor small, neither inside nor outside.
One cultivates oneself, understands oneself, arranges for oneself.

That is, the Master cultivated by himself, understood by himself, and then buried himself. After the Master finished carving the couplet, he sat in the tomb, closed the stone door, and passed into stillness. He entered nirvana. That is an inconceivable matter. Thus when he had passed away, that was truly a great affair. His power of liberated ease was immensely great! I met the Master at Su Zhou on Ling Yen Mountain. The Master cultivated for himself and for everyone else. He troubled no one at all.

Thus I can enable dull and stupid beings — atyantikas — forever to leave delusion and darkness.

They have no wisdom and so they can see through and clearly understand nothing at all. Like a blunted knife that can cut nothing. They mistake right for wrong and wrong for right. But Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva can enable such people to leave far behind the obstructions that envelop them.

"Atyantika" is Sanskrit, meaning "extreme evil." If you suggest these people do something good, they never will. Rather than give someone a coin to do good, they clutch the coin in hand until the copper melts. If you tell them to help someone, their reaction is to consider it insane. "My money is for me to spend. Why should I give it to others?" Yet Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva can help such people escape their delusion and dark thinking. Those who will not help others are those with not a glimmer of light in their own natures; thus they are dark and stupid kinds of people.

The passage above mentioned greed and anger. This sutra passage speaks of the mind of delusion. The Dharma Flower Sutra says: If a person is full of anger, constantly reveres and recites Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, then delusion can be eradicated.

There was a very rich man, very greedy for money and unwilling to share with anyone. He had three sons. He named the eldest son Gold, the second son Silver. As for the third son, he feared the boy would give his money away in good works instead of hoarding it, so he named him Karmic Obstruction. When the old man was dying, he called the eldest son over and said, "I am about to go. Will you go with me?"

Gold said, "You senile old fool! How could I die with you? Ordinarily you loved me most. Now at death, why do you want to harm me?" Gold would not go with his father.

He thought, "Then I shall ask the second son." Then he called Silver over. "Your brother will not go with me. Will you? You have always been most filial."

The second son answered, "If you die, then die alone. Though I am your son, I cannot die along with you. You are most peculiar. I am still so young." Gold would not die along with his father; Silver neither. He called the third son, Karmic Obstruction. "Ordinarily you have been most disobedient, so I never loved you much. But now I am about to die, and your brothers Gold and Silver will not follow me. Think carefully whether you can follow me?" Karmic Obstruction answered, "I need not think at all. Of course I shall go. Now look at Gold and Silver, whom you loved most, yet they cannot grant your request. But I, Karmic Obstruction, shall follow you wherever you go. In life I accompany you, and in death I shall follow you too. See who is the most filial son?"

Nothing can be carried along.
Only karmic obstructions follow one.

The old father reflected, seeing that all the gold and silver he had hoarded would bring joy to his first and second sons, while he himself had to die. He was flooded with profound remorse. He thought, "Would that I had built a temple or a Way-place in the time remaining — but it is too late. Now I am about to die."

The moral of this story is: do not be like that old man. If you have the means, do good works at once.

Sutra text: 十二者融形復聞,不動道場涉入世間,不壞世界能遍十方。供養微塵諸佛如來,各各佛邊為法王子。能令法界無子眾生。欲求男者,誕生福德智慧之男。

Transliteration: Thập nhị giả, dung hình phục văn, bất động đạo tràng thiệp nhập thế gian, bất hoại thế giới. Năng biến thập phương. Cúng dường vi trần chư Phật Như Lai, các các Phật biên vi pháp vương tử. Năng linh pháp giới vô tử chúng sanh. Dục cầu nam giả, đản sanh phước đức trí huệ chi nam.

Translation: Twelfth, form dissolved, I return to hearing; unmoving in the Way-place, I merge into the world without destroying the world. Able to pervade the ten directions, I make offerings to the Buddhas, the Tathagatas, as numerous as dust motes; beside each Buddha I am a Dharma Prince. I enable childless beings of the Dharma Realm who seek sons to give birth to sons of blessings, virtue, and wisdom.

Commentary: The twelfth fearlessness power is: form dissolved, I return to hearing — when the body has been transformed and returned to the hearing-nature — unmoving in the Way-place, I merge into the world without destroying the world.

"The unmoving Way-place" means constantly dwelling in one's original Way-place. For instance, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva is now present in the Buddhist Lecture Hall, yet though he is here, he can still travel throughout the world. It is not that he goes from here; his transformation bodies appear everywhere. And the world is still not altered. With his Dharma body, he can make offerings to the Buddhas, the Tathagatas, as numerous as dust motes throughout the ten directions. He goes throughout the ten directions to do the Buddha's work. Beside each Buddha I am a Dharma Prince. I enable childless beings of the Dharma Realm who seek sons to give birth to sons of blessings, virtue, and wisdom.

Sutra text: 十三者六根圓通,明照無二含十方界。立大圓鏡空如來藏。承順十方微塵如來。祕密法門受領無失。能令法界無子眾生,欲求女者,誕生端正福德柔順,眾人愛敬有相之女。

Transliteration: Thập tam giả lục căn viên thông, minh chiếu vô nhị, hàm thập phương giới. Lập đại viên kính không Như Lai tạng. Thừa thuận thập phương vi trần Như Lai. Bí mật pháp môn thọ lĩnh vô thất. Năng linh pháp giới vô tử chúng sanh, dục cầu nữ giả, đản sanh đoan chánh phước đức nhu thuận, chúng nhân ái kính hữu tướng chi nữ.

Translation: Thirteenth, my six sense roots perfectly interfused, the illumination non-dual, containing the realms of the ten directions; establishing the great perfect mirror, the empty Tathagatagarbha, I receive and follow the secret Dharma-doors of the Tathagatas of the ten directions, as numerous as dust motes, without loss. I enable childless beings of the Dharma Realm who seek daughters to give birth to daughters of upright marks, blessings, virtue, and gentleness, loved and respected by all.

Commentary: The thirteenth fearlessness power is: my six sense roots perfectly interfused, illumination non-dual, containing the ten directions, establishing the great perfect mirror, the empty Tathagatagarbha.

Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind all unobstructed and perfectly interfused with one another. All things merge into one. The six sense roots function interchangeably. Like a great mirror revealing the empty, still treasury of the Tathagatas.

I receive and follow the secret Dharma-doors of the Tathagatas of the ten directions, as numerous as dust motes, without loss, enabling childless beings of the Dharma Realm who seek daughters to give birth to daughters of upright marks, blessings, virtue, and gentleness, loved and respected by all.

If people wish to bear daughters, they will obtain daughters upright and gentle. Everyone meeting such daughters at once loves and respects them. They will be virtuous and perfect daughters.

Sutra text: 十四者此三千大千世界百億日月。現住世間諸法王子。有六十二恒河沙數修法垂範。教化眾生隨順眾生。方便智慧各各不同。

Transliteration: Thập tứ giả, thử tam thiên, đại thiên thế giới, bá ức nhật nguyệt. Hiện trụ thế gian chư pháp vương tử, hữu lục thập nhị hằng hà sa số, tu pháp thuỳ phạm, giáo hóa chúng sanh, tuỳ thuận chúng sanh. Phương tiện trí huệ các các bất đồng.

Translation: Fourteenth, in this great trichiliocosm with its hundred koṭis of suns and moons, the Dharma Princes now dwelling in the world, sixty-two Ganges' sands in number, cultivate the Dharma as models, teach beings, and accord with beings. Their expedient wisdom each differs.

Commentary: The fourteenth fearlessness power is: in this great trichiliocosm with its hundred koṭis of suns and moons, the Dharma Princes now dwelling in the world, sixty-two Ganges' sands in number — they are now dwelling right in this world — all cultivate the Buddhadharma, serve as models, teach beings, and accord with beings. Their expedient wisdom each differs. They use different skillful expedients and provisional wisdom to teach each different kind of being.

Sutra text: 由我所得圓通本根發妙耳門。然後身心微妙含容遍周法界。能令眾生持我名號。與彼共持六十二恒河沙諸法王子。二人福德正等無異。

Transliteration: Do ngã sở đắc viên thông, bổn căn phát diệu nhĩ môn. Nhiên hậu thân tâm vi diệu hàm dung biến chu pháp giới. Năng linh chúng sanh trì ngã danh hiệu, dữ bỉ cộng trì lục thập nhị hằng hà sa chư Pháp vương tử. Nhị nhơn phước đức chánh đẳng vô dị.

Translation: Because I attained perfect penetration, the sublime ear-door of my original root opened. Then my body and mind, subtle and wonderful, contained and pervaded the Dharma Realm. I can enable beings who uphold my name, compared with those who uphold the names of the sixty-two Ganges' sands of Dharma Princes above, to have merit and virtue exactly equal, without difference.

Commentary: Because I attained perfect penetration, the sublime nature of my ear root opened. I, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, certified to the perfect penetration of the ear root, and obtained the subtle, wonderful powers from the ear root. Then my body and mind, subtle and wonderful, pervade the Dharma Realm. This subtle state pervades all ten directions, throughout the Dharma Realm. Thus I enable beings who uphold my name — those who recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name — compared with those who uphold the names of the sixty-two Ganges' sands of Dharma Princes above, to have merit and virtue exactly equal, without difference.

A person who recites only Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, and another who recites the names of Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of sixty-two Ganges Rivers — each one's meritorious retribution is equal. This shows just how great the merit of reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name is.

Sutra text: 世尊我一號名與彼眾多名號無異,由我修習得真圓通。

Transliteration: Thế tôn, ngã nhất hiệu danh dữ bỉ chúng đa danh hiệu vô dị, do ngã tu tập đắc chơn viên thông.

Translation: World Honored One, my single name is no different from those many names, because through cultivation I attained true perfect penetration.

Commentary: World Honored One, my single name — the name Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva — is no different from those many names, meaning the Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of sixty-two Ganges Rivers. How is this so? How can the merit of one name equal that of so many names? It is because through cultivation I attained true perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 是名十四施無畏力,福備眾生.

Transliteration: Thị danh thập tứ thí vô uý lực, phước bị chúng sanh.

Translation: These are called the fourteen powers of bestowing fearlessness, with which I fully bless all beings.

Commentary: These are called the fourteen powers of bestowing fearlessness, with which I fully bless all beings.

I come to help them; whenever anyone calls for rescue, I at once rescue them.

Sutra text: 世尊我又獲是圓通修證無上道故,又能善獲四不思議無作妙德。一者由我初獲妙妙聞心,心精遺聞。見聞覺知不能分隔,成一圓融清淨寶覺。故我能現眾多妙容。能說無邊祕密神呪。

Transliteration: Thế tôn, Ngã hựu hoạch thị viên thông tu chứng vô thượng đạo cố, hựu năng thiện hoạch tứ bất tư nghì vô tác diệu đức. Nhất giả do ngã sơ hoạch diệu diệu văn tâm, tâm tinh di văn. Kiến văn giác tri bất năng phân cách, thành nhất viên dung thanh tịnh bảo giác. Cố ngã năng hiện chúng đa diệu dung. Năng thuyết vô biên bí mật thần chú.

Translation: World Honored One! Further, having attained this perfect penetration to cultivate and certify to the unsurpassed Way, I have also well attained four inconceivable, non-doing, wondrous virtues: First, when I first attained the sublime hearing-mind, the essence of mind abandoned hearing. Seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing could no longer be separated, merging into one perfect, pure, precious enlightenment. Thus I can manifest many wonderful forms and speak countless secret spirit-mantras.

Commentary: World Honored One! Further, having attained this perfect penetration to cultivate and certify to the unsurpassed Way, I have also well attained four inconceivable, non-doing, wondrous virtues:

What are these four inconceivable merits?

First, when I first attained the sublime hearing-mind, the essence of mind abandoned hearing.

At first, when I certified through the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature — the sublime within the sublime — my mind became utterly refined and all marks of the hearer dissolved. The true mind manifested, and I reached the state of refined subtlety. When the marks of the hearer had dissolved, seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing could no longer be separated. The other sense roots all became perfectly interfused and were no longer divided. I perfected the precious enlightenment, perfectly interfused and pure. This means he certified to oneness; there is no more distinction between subject and object.

Thus I can manifest many wonderful forms and speak countless secret spirit-mantras.

Sutra text: 其中或現一首三首。五首七首九首十一首。如是乃至一百八首。千首萬首八萬四千爍迦囉首。

Transliteration: Kỳ trung hoặc hiện nhất thủ tam thủ. Ngũ thủ thất thủ cửu thủ thập nhất thủ. Như thị nãi chí nhất bá bát thủ. Thiên thủ vạn thủ bát vạn tứ thiên thước-ca-la thủ.

Translation: For instance, I can manifest one head, three heads, five heads, seven heads, nine heads, eleven heads, 108 heads, 1,000 heads, 10,000 heads, up to 84,000 vajra heads.

Commentary: Not only does Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva have a thousand hands and a thousand eyes, he also has countless heads — as many as 84,000 heads. All of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's forms are manifested. He says: I can manifest one head, three heads — the image of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva with three faces — five heads — the image of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva with five faces — seven heads — the image of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva with seven faces — or nine heads, eleven heads, 108 heads, 1,000 heads, 10,000 heads, up to 84,000 vajra heads. "Vajra" means strong and indestructible.

Sutra text: 二臂四臂六臂八臂。十臂十二臂十四十六。十八二十至二十四。如是乃至一百八臂千臂萬臂。

Transliteration: Nhị tý tứ tý lục tý bát tý. Thập tý thập nhị tý thập tứ thập lục. Thập bát nhị thập chí nhị thập tứ. Như thị nãi chí nhất bá bát tý thiên tý vạn tý. Bát vạn tứ thiên mẫu- đà-la tý.

Translation: I can manifest two arms, four arms, six arms, twelve arms, fourteen arms, sixteen arms, eighteen arms, twenty arms, twenty-four arms, 108 arms, then 1,000 arms, 10,000 arms, up to 84,000 mudra arms.

Commentary: Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva can also manifest two arms, four arms, six arms, twelve arms, fourteen arms, sixteen arms, eighteen arms, twenty arms, twenty-four arms. Or manifest 108 arms, then 1,000 arms, 10,000 arms, up to 84,000 mudra arms. "Mudra" is Sanskrit, meaning hand-seal. In the palm of each hand there is a seal.

Sutra text: 二目三目四目九目。如是乃至一百八目千目萬目。八萬四千清淨寶目。或慈或威或定或慧。救護眾生得大自在。

Transliteration: Nhị mục tam mục tứ mục cửu mục. Như thị nãi chí nhất bá bát mục thiên mục vạn mục. Bát vạn tứ thiên thanh tịnh bảo mục. Hoặc từ hoặc oai hoặc định hoặc huệ. Cứu hộ chúng sanh đắc đại tự tại.

Translation: Or manifest two eyes, three eyes, four eyes, nine eyes, 108 eyes, then 1,000 eyes, 10,000 eyes, up to 84,000 pure precious eyes. Sometimes manifesting kindness, sometimes awesomeness, sometimes samadhi, sometimes wisdom, to rescue beings unto great ease.

Commentary: Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's Dharma body can manifest as two eyes, three eyes, four eyes, nine eyes, 108 eyes, then 1,000 eyes, 10,000 eyes, up to 84,000 pure precious eyes. How can Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva manifest so many transformation bodies? Because on the causal ground he cultivated the Great Compassion Mantra and the Forty-Two Hands and Eyes Dharma, so on the fruition ground, when cultivation effort was perfected, he obtained countless transformation bodies.

Or manifesting kindness, sometimes awesomeness, sometimes samadhi, sometimes wisdom, to rescue beings unto great ease.

His eyes sometimes express kindness, sometimes manifest awesomeness. Sometimes his eyes display the light of samadhi power or wisdom. He displays these marks to rescue beings unto perfect ease.

Sutra text: 二者由我聞思脫出六塵。如聲度垣不能為礙。故我妙能現一一形。誦一一呪。其形其呪。能以無畏施諸眾生。是故十方微塵國土。皆名我為施無畏者。

Transliteration: Nhị giả do ngã văn tư thóat xuất lục trần. Như thinh độ viên bất năng vi ngại. Cố ngã diệu năng hiện nhất nhất hình, tụng nhất nhất chú. Kỳ hình kỳ chú năng dĩ vô uý thí chư chúng sanh. Thị cố thập phương vi trần quốc độ. Giai danh ngã vi thí vô uý giả.

Translation: Second, because my hearing and contemplation transcend the six sense-objects, like sound passing through a wall unobstructed, my sublime function can manifest each and every form and recite each and every mantra. Those forms and those mantras can bestow fearlessness upon beings. Therefore the lands of the ten directions, as numerous as dust motes, all call me the Bestower of Fearlessness.

Commentary: The second non-doing wondrous virtue is: Second, because my hearing and contemplation transcend the six sense-objects. I cultivated the wisdom of hearing and the wisdom of contemplation, transcending the six sense-objects of form, sound, scent, taste, touch, and mental objects. I am no longer attached to them. It is like sound passing through a wall, unobstructed. Therefore my sublime function can manifest each and every form and recite each and every mantra.

The forms I manifest and the mantras I recite can all bestow the power of fearlessness upon beings. They all have the power to grant fearlessness. Therefore the lands of the ten directions, as numerous as dust motes, all call me the Bestower of Fearlessness.

Sutra text: 三者由我修習本妙圓通清淨本根,所遊世界,皆令眾生,捨身珍寶求我哀愍。

Transliteration: Tam giả do ngã tu tập bổn diệu viên thông thanh tịnh bổn căn, sở du thế giới, giai linh chúng sanh, xả thân trân bảo cầu ngã ai mẫn.

Translation: Third, because I cultivated the originally sublime, perfectly interfused, pure original root, in whatever world I travel, I cause beings to renounce their bodies and precious treasures to seek my pity.

Commentary: Third, because I cultivated the originally sublime, perfectly interfused, pure original root. He is speaking of the pure original nature of the ear root — the hearing-nature. In whatever world I travel, I cause beings to renounce their bodies and precious treasures to seek my pity. Beings all sacrifice their lives and give up all their precious possessions to seek my help.

Sutra text: 四者我得佛心證於究竟。能以珍寶種種供養十方如來, 傍及法界六道眾生。

Transliteration: Tứ giả ngã đắc Phật tâm, chứng ư cứu cánh. Năng dĩ trân bảo chủng chủng cúng dường thập phương Như Lai, bàng cập pháp giới lục đạo chúng sanh.

Translation: Fourth, because I have attained the Buddha's mind and certified to the ultimate, I can with all kinds of precious treasures make offerings to the Tathagatas of the ten directions, and extensively to the beings of the six paths throughout the Dharma Realm.

Commentary: The fourth non-doing wondrous virtue is: Because I have attained the Buddha's mind and certified to the ultimate. I have certified to the true mind, the Tathagatagarbha. "Ultimate" means the highest station of Buddhahood. Thus I can with all kinds of precious treasures make offerings to the Tathagatas of the ten directions, and extensively to the beings of the six paths throughout the Dharma Realm. Whatever beings wish for, I grant them to fulfillment.

Sutra text: 求妻得妻求子得子。求三昧得三昧。求長壽得長壽。如是乃至求大涅槃得大涅槃。

Transliteration: Cầu thê đắc thê cầu tử đắc tử, cầu tam-muội đắc tam-muội. Cầu trường thọ đắc trường thọ. Như thị nãi chí cầu đại niết-bàn đắc đại niết-bàn.

Translation: Those who seek wives obtain wives; who seek children obtain children; who seek samadhi obtain samadhi; who seek long life obtain long life. Thus even unto seeking great nirvana, they obtain great nirvana.

Commentary: Whatever beings of the six paths in the ten directions wish for is all bestowed. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva knows that everyone wishes for a virtuous wife. Those who seek wives obtain wives; if they hope for an obedient, virtuous wife, they at once obtain an obedient, virtuous wife. That is the highest wish of all beings. Once they have a virtuous wife, they then wish for children. Thus the second thing Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva does is bestow children upon them. Those who seek children obtain children; if they hope to bear sons, at once they obtain sons; if they hope for daughters, at once they obtain daughters.

Third, he says: those who seek samadhi obtain samadhi; who seek long life obtain long life. If people who already have wives and children feel that human life is truly meaningless, and so bring forth the resolve to cultivate to escape the world and hope for samadhi, then they will obtain samadhi. Those who hope for long life will obtain long life. They wish to become immortal and never die; they will have it so. Thus even unto seeking great nirvana, they obtain great nirvana. If any beings hope to become Buddhas, they can attain Buddhahood.

Sutra text: 佛問圓通,我從耳門圓照三昧, 緣心自在。因入流相,得三摩 提,成就菩提。斯為第一。

Transliteration: Phật vấn viên thông, ngã tòng nhĩ môn viên chiếu tam muội, duyên tâm tự tại. Nhân nhập lưu tướng, đắc tam-ma-đề, thành tựu bồ-đề. Tư vi đệ nhất.

Translation: The Buddha asks about perfect penetration; from the ear-door I attained the samadhi of perfect illumination, and my conditioned mind became at ease. Through the mark of entering the flow, I attained samadhi and perfected bodhi. This is foremost.

Commentary: The Buddha asks about perfect penetration. The Buddha asked his disciples by what expedient they first certified to perfect penetration. From the ear-door I attained the samadhi of perfect illumination. I cultivated at the hearing-nature and perfected samadhi power. And my conditioned mind became at ease. Through the mark of entering the flow, I attained samadhi and perfected bodhi. This is foremost. My conditioned mind is no more; I am at ease. I turned the hearing back to recognize the self-nature, and perfected the unsurpassed Way. This is the best method.

Sutra text: 世尊彼佛如來。歎我善得圓通法門。於大會中授記我為觀世音號。

Transliteration: Thế tôn bỉ Phật Như Lai thán ngã thiện đắc viên thông pháp môn. Ư đại hội trung thọ ký ngã vi Quán thế âm hiệu.

Translation: World Honored One, that Buddha, the Tathagata, praised me for well attaining the dharma-door of perfect penetration. In the great assembly he bestowed upon me the name Avalokiteshvara.

Commentary: World Honored One, that Buddha, the Tathagata, praised me for well attaining the dharma-door of perfect penetration. "That Buddha, the Tathagata" refers to the Ancient Buddha, the Tathagata Avalokiteshvara. He praised me for having certified to perfect penetration at ease. Thus in the great assembly he bestowed upon me the name Avalokiteshvara. He called me the one who "regards the sounds of the world" — the same name as his own.

Sutra text: 由我觀聽十方圓明,故觀音名遍十方界.

Transliteration: Do ngã quán thính thập phương viên minh, cố quán âm danh biến thập phương giới.

Translation: Because my regarding and hearing are perfectly luminous throughout the ten directions, the name Guanshiyin pervades the realms of the ten directions.

Commentary: Because my regarding and hearing are perfectly luminous throughout the ten directions — meaning, in every place throughout the ten directions, to the very ends of the Dharma Realms, all joined together, and I am fully aware of it all — therefore the name Guanshiyin pervades the realms of the ten directions. In every Buddha-land throughout the ten directions, all know the name Avalokiteshvara.

tom_tat: VOLUME 6 (PART 2): MANJUSHRI BODHISATTVA SELECTS THE PERFECT PENETRATION ROOT. Brief Commentary on the Shurangama Sutra by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua. The Buddha emits light from his five body parts; the assembly sees the Thus Come Ones; Manjushri is requested to select the best penetration; he chooses the ear root as supreme.
noi_dung:
VOLUME 6 (PART 2): MANJUSHRI BODHISATTVA SELECTS THE PERFECT-PENETRATION ROOT

Brief Commentary on the Shurangama Sutra — Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

THE SUTRA OF THE GREAT BUDDHA CROWN, THE TATHAGATA'S SECRET CAUSE, THE COMPLETE MEANING OF CULTIVATION AND CERTIFICATION, AND THE MYRIAD PRACTICES OF ALL BODHISATTVAS: THE SHURANGAMA

VOLUME 6 – PART 2

— o0o —

LECTURED BY VENERABLE MASTER HSUAN HUA

— o0o —

Sutra text: 爾時世尊於師子座,從其五體同放寶光,遠灌十方微塵如來,及法王子諸菩薩頂.

Transliteration: Nhĩ thời Thế tôn ư sư tử toà, tòng kỳ ngũ thể đồng phóng bảo quang, viễn quán thập phương vi trần Như Lai, cập Pháp vương tử chư Bồ-tát đỉnh.

Translation: At that time the World Honored One, upon the lion's throne, from his fivefold body simultaneously emitted precious light, pouring from afar upon the crowns of the Tathagatas as numerous as dust motes throughout the ten directions, and upon the crowns of the Dharma-Prince Bodhisattvas.

Commentary: At that time the World Honored One, upon the lion's throne, from his fivefold body simultaneously emitted precious light. Shakyamuni Buddha, seated upon the lion's throne, emitted light from his two hands, his two feet, and the crown of his head all at once. Pouring from afar upon the crowns of the Tathagatas as numerous as dust motes and upon the crowns of the Dharma-Prince Bodhisattvas.

Shakyamuni Buddha touching the crowns of the Tathagatas symbolizes that his teaching is the highest, is the crown. The teaching of the Buddhas is likewise. The Tathagatas throughout the ten directions all proclaim this same supreme teaching, just as Shakyamuni Buddha is proclaiming it.

The teachings of the Tathagatas are all identical,
mutually containing one another.

Sutra text: 彼諸如來亦於五體同放寶光。從微塵方來灌佛頂。并灌會中諸大菩薩及阿羅漢。

Transliteration: Bỉ chư Như Lai diệc ư ngũ thể đồng phóng bảo quang, tòng vi trần phương lai quán Phật đỉnh. Tinh quán hội trung chư đại Bồ-tát cập A-la-hán.

Translation: Those Tathagatas, too, from their fivefold bodies simultaneously emitted precious light, coming from lands as numerous as dust motes to pour upon the Buddha's crown, and to pour upon the great Bodhisattvas and Arhats in the assembly.

Commentary: Those Tathagatas, as numerous as dust motes throughout the ten directions, from their fivefold bodies also simultaneously emitted precious light, from worlds as numerous as dust motes. The precious light likewise issued at once from their two hands, two feet, and the crowns of their heads, just like the rays of light Shakyamuni Buddha had emitted. The light came and poured upon the Buddha's crown and upon the crowns of the Bodhisattvas and Arhats in the assembly.

Sutra text: 林木池沼皆演法音。交光相羅如寶絲網。是諸大眾得未曾有。一切普獲金剛三昧。

Transliteration: Lâm mộc trì chiểu giai diễn pháp âm. Giao quang tương la như bảo ty võng. Thị chư đại chúng đắc vị tằng hữu. Nhất thiết phổ hoạch kim cang tam-muội.

Translation: Groves, trees, ponds, and marshes all proclaimed the sounds of Dharma. The interweaving lights formed like a jeweled gauze net. The great assembly obtained what they had never had; all universally attained the Vajra samadhi.

Commentary: Groves, trees, ponds, and marshes all proclaimed the sounds of Dharma. Flowing water, sighing wind, and rustling leaves were all displays of Dharma sounds. The interweaving lights formed like a jeweled gauze net. The light of the Buddhas of the ten directions poured upon Shakyamuni Buddha's crown, and the light from Shakyamuni Buddha issued forth again, pouring upon the crowns of the Tathagatas as numerous as dust motes in the ten directions; the pattern of those interweaving rays formed a most splendid net. The great assembly obtained what they had never had; all universally attained the Vajra samadhi door. They had never before seen such auspicious happenings, which caused everyone to attain the Vajra samadhi door.

Sutra text: 即時天雨百寶蓮華,青黃赤白間錯紛糅。十方虛空成七寶色。

Transliteration: Tức thời thiên vũ bá bảo liên hoa, thanh hoàng xích bạch gián thố phân nhữu. Thập phương hư không thành thất bảo sắc.

Translation: At once there rained from the heavens hundred-jeweled lotus blossoms, blue, yellow, red, and white intermingled in profusion. The empty space of the ten directions took on the colors of the seven precious things.

Commentary: At once — when everyone in the assembly attained the Vajra samadhi — there rained from the heavens hundred-jeweled lotus blossoms, blue, yellow, red, and white intermingled in profusion. These four colors appeared in various combinations upon the lotus petals. Blossoms of blue lotus stood out beside yellow hues. Blossoms of yellow lotus bore red specks within their petals. Blossoms of white lotus glistened with tints of pink. The empty space of the ten directions took on the colors of the seven precious things. The seven precious things are gold, silver, vaidurya, crystal, mother-of-pearl, red pearl, and carnelian. The whole world turned into these colors.

Sutra text: 此娑婆界大地山河俱時不現。唯見十方微塵國土合成一界。梵唄詠歌自然數奏

Transliteration: Thử ta-bà giới đại địa sơn hà câu thời bất hiện. Duy kiến thập phương vi trần quốc độ hợp thành nhất giới. Phạm bái vịnh ca tự nhiên sổ tấu.

Translation: The mountains, rivers, and great earth of this Saha world all vanished from sight at once. Only the lands as numerous as dust motes in the ten directions were seen, merged into a single realm. Sanskrit hymns and songs resounded of themselves.

Commentary: The mountains, rivers, and great earth of this Saha world all vanished from sight at once. Only the lands as numerous as dust motes in the ten directions were seen, merged into a single realm.

The world we dwell in is called Saha. That name means "endurance." It symbolizes that beings must endure suffering in this world. Indeed, it is most hard to bear, yet everyone must directly undergo it, not merely acknowledge suffering. They take suffering for joy. They think it is truly fine here.

Now, however, the Saha realm vanished all at once. That was through Shakyamuni Buddha's spiritual power, displayed for the assembly to see. Buddha-lands as countless as dust motes merged into one. Sanskrit hymns and songs resounded of themselves.

Pure Sanskrit sounds, hymns of praise, resounded everywhere. Before, groves, trees, rivers, and lakes had proclaimed Dharma sounds, but here, the myriad things all proclaimed Dharma sounds in most pure and subtle hymns and songs of praise.

Flowing waters and sighing winds all proclaim the Great Vehicle.
The seven-jeweled lotuses in the lake, four colors blazing, glistening golden. Manjushri Bodhisattva SELECTS THE PERFECT-PENETRATION ROOT

Sutra text: 於是如來告文殊師利法王子: 汝今觀此二十五無學諸大菩薩及阿羅漢,各說最初成道方便,皆言修習真實圓通。彼等修行實無優劣前後差別。

Transliteration: Ư thị Như Lai cáo Văn-thù-sư-lợi Pháp vương tử: “Nhữ kim quán thử nhị thập ngũ vô học chư Đại Bồ-tát cập A-la-hán, các thuyết tối sơ thành đạo phương tiện, giai ngôn tu tập chơn thật viên thông. Bỉ đẳng tu hành thật vô ưu liệt tiền hậu sai biệt.

Translation: Thereupon the Tathagata said to Manjushri, Prince of Dharma: "Now regard these twenty-five great Bodhisattvas and Arhats beyond study; each has described the expedient of his initial accomplishment of the Way, all speaking of cultivating true perfect penetration. In their cultivation there is truly no superiority or inferiority, no difference of earlier or later."

Commentary: Thereupon the Tathagata — Shakyamuni Buddha — said to Manjushri, Prince of Dharma: "Now regard these twenty-five great Bodhisattvas and Arhats beyond study."

Now examine the expedient dharma-doors these twenty-five sages employed in cultivation. "Beyond study" refers to those who have certified to the fourth fruition of Arhatship or higher. Each has described the expedient of his initial accomplishment of the Way; all speak of cultivating true perfect penetration. They have truly certified to the perfect penetration of the sense roots. In their cultivation there is truly no superiority or inferiority, no difference of earlier or later. Indeed, there is no way to distinguish superiority or inferiority, earlier or later, difference among them.

Sutra text: 我今欲令阿難開悟,二十五行,誰當其根。兼我滅後,此界眾生 入菩薩乘,求無上道。何方便門得易成就?

Transliteration: Ngã kim dục linh A-nan khai ngộ, nhị thập ngũ hạnh, thuỳ đương kỳ căn? Kiêm ngã diệt hậu, thử giới chúng sanh, nhập bồ tát thừa cầu vô thượng đạo. Hà phương tiện môn đắc dị thành tựu?

Translation: Now I wish to enable Ananda to become enlightened: among the twenty-five practices, which accords with his root? And after my extinction, when beings of this realm enter the Bodhisattva Vehicle seeking the unsurpassed Way, through which expedient door will accomplishment come easily?"

Commentary: Shakyamuni Buddha says: Now I wish to enable Ananda to become enlightened. Ananda is still at the first fruition of Arhatship. The Tathagata wishes him to become enlightened and certify to the second, third, and fourth fruitions of Arhatship. Then among the twenty-five practices, which accords with Ananda's root? Which dharma-door accords with Ananda's root? Among the eighteen realms and the seven elements, which dharma-door corresponds to Ananda? And after the Tathagata's extinction, when beings of this realm enter the Bodhisattva Vehicle seeking the unsurpassed Way, through which expedient door will accomplishment come easily?

The beings mentioned here are precisely ourselves. We who are hearing Dharma in the Buddhist Lecture Hall are exactly those the Buddha means. Any of you reading this sutra are also included in this group. So do not stand apart and say, "I have no part in it." That way, you only confuse yourselves more. If you place yourselves outside that number, you will fall into a later life, and if you become horses, pigs, cows, dogs, chickens, it will not be easy to hear the Shurangama Sutra. For one thing, you could never leap four flights of stairs in one bound to reach the lecture hall! In Hong Kong, there were ducks that came to hear my sutra lectures, but that was on the ground floor.

Long ago, Shakyamuni Buddha already arranged seats for us in this Dharma assembly, so that it unfolds as it does now. Do not slight yourselves. Of course, if you do not come here now to hear the sutra, then you will have no part.

"Among these dharma-doors, which is most suitable for beings of later ages with great roots who bring forth the resolve seeking the Unsurpassed Way?" the Buddha asks Manjushri. "Which dharma-door most easily leads to accomplishment? Manjushri, take care to select one dharma-door."

Sutra text: 文殊師利法王子奉佛慈旨,即從座起頂禮佛足。承佛威神說偈對佛。

Transliteration: Văn-thù-sư-lợi Pháp vương tử phụng Phật từ chỉ, tức tòng toà khởi đỉnh lễ Phật túc. Thừa phật oai thần, thuyết kệ đối Phật.

Translation: Manjushri, Prince of Dharma, receiving the Buddha's compassionate instruction, at once rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha's feet, and, relying on the Buddha's awesome spirit, answered the Buddha in verse:

Commentary: Manjushri, Prince of Dharma, receiving the Buddha's compassionate instruction, at once rose from his seat.

The Bodhisattva Wonderfully Auspicious was entrusted by the Buddha with selecting, from among the eighteen realms and the seven elements, one method of cultivation to attain perfect penetration. He will find the dharma-door most suitable for Ananda and for all of us to cultivate. The six sense roots, six sense-objects, and six consciousnesses make up the eighteen realms. Earth, water, fire, wind, together with space, consciousness, and perception, make up the seven elements as explained in full detail before.

Hearing the Buddha's compassionate instruction, Manjushri Bodhisattva at once rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha's feet, and, relying on the Buddha's awesome spirit, answered in verse:

The Bodhisattvas and Arhats all had seats around the Buddha, unlike the Vajra Fire Chief, who had to stand in the Dharma assembly. A verse may consist of many syllables and many lines, but it always contains the principles of the sutra.

Sutra text: 覺海性澄圓 圓澄覺元妙 　元明照生所 所立照性亡。

Transliteration: Giác hải tánh trừng viên Viên trừng giác nguyên diệu Nguyên minh chiếu sanh sở Sở lập chiếu tánh vong.

Translation: The sea of enlightenment, its nature clear and perfect; Perfect, clear, the enlightened source sublime; The original brightness shone and produced the "object"; The "object" established, the shining nature was lost.

Commentary: The sea of enlightenment, its nature clear and perfect. The sea of enlightenment is immensely vast, containing within it mountains, rivers, and lands, grasses, trees, and the myriad things. The nature of the sea of enlightenment is both still and perfect. Perfect, clear, the enlightened source sublime. The stillness and perfection of the sea of enlightenment are originally most sublime. But precisely within this sublimity, a single subtle thought of true-and-false arose, and the original brightness shone and produced something like an object (subject/object). The original brightness shone and produced the "object." The "object" established, the shining nature was lost. Fundamentally, the sea of enlightenment contains everything within it. There is nothing that is not within the Tathagatagarbha nature. But the moment a thought of ignorance arises, falseness springs forth. Once there is falseness, there is its object — sense-objects, false objective marks. Because of this false shining, the originally present brightness within the enlightened nature no longer shines, as when the sky is covered by clouds. Once the false objective realm is established, the true shining nature is also lost — that is, the originally present nature within the Tathagatagarbha is turned into the ignorance store-consciousness.

Sutra text: 迷妄有虛空 依空立世界 想澄成國土 知覺乃眾生。

Transliteration: Mê vọng hữu hư không Y không lập thế giới Tưởng trừng thành quốc độ Tri giác nãi chúng sanh.

Translation: In confused falseness there is empty space; Relying on space, worlds are established; Solidified thought becomes lands; Conscious knowing becomes beings.

Commentary: In confused falseness there is empty space. Because of falseness, subject and object (duality, objective/subjective) take shape. Originally, both aspects are false. Within the substance of the sea of enlightened nature, not a bit of phenomena manifests. Originally there is not a single thing. There is no subject or object. Only relying on the true does falseness arise — darkening into empty space, deluded about the nature of emptiness, turning it into stubborn emptiness, until there is entirely empty space; relying on empty space, all phenomenal worlds are falsely established.

"Gazing long, one grows weary." After extending for a time, the prolonging causes weariness. And then falseness and delusion arise into stubborn emptiness. Yet within the sea of enlightened nature there is originally nothing at all, not even empty space. The verse below describes:
Empty space arises within great enlightenment
Like a single bubble in the sea.
How obscure it truly is! And so we think of empty space as something immensely vast. Relying on space, worlds are established. The ten directions and three periods come into being.
Solidified thought becomes lands.
When time and space have arisen from empty space, false thought hardens; it makes dry land.
Conscious knowing becomes beings.
Solidified false thought結 forms lands. Conscious false thought of knowing forms beings.

Sutra text: 空生大覺中 如海一漚發 　有漏微塵國 皆從空所生 　漚滅空本無 況復諸三有。

Transliteration: Không sanh đại giác trung Như hải nhất âu phát, Hữu lậu vi trần quốc, Giai tòng không sở sanh, Âu diệt không bổn vô, Huống phục chư tam hữu.

Translation: Empty space arises within great enlightenment, Like a single bubble rising in the sea; Outflow lands as numerous as dust motes All arise from space. When the bubble bursts, space fundamentally is no more — How much less the Triple Existence!

Commentary: The first line of this verse is:
The sea of enlightenment, its nature clear and perfect;
Perfect, clear, the enlightened source sublime.
The perfect nature of the pure bodhi source is infinitely sublime. Now the verse speaks of: Empty space arises within great enlightenment. We all know of the existence of empty space, but do we know where empty space comes from? I believe no one knows. For empty space is too vast. One cannot know the limits of empty space or its source. Who is the mother of empty space? No one knows. But now the Shurangama Sutra points out its source. Empty space is born from the nature of great enlightenment. And so within that interval, it is extremely subtle. Is it large? It is like a single bubble rising in the sea — like foam-bubbles upon the great ocean.
Outflow lands as numerous as dust motes
All arise from space.

There are three kinds of outflows:
1. The outflow of desire.
2. The outflow of existence.
3. The outflow of ignorance.

Countless outflow lands all arise from empty space. Empty space arises from great enlightenment, and lands arise from empty space.
When the bubble bursts, space fundamentally is no more.
Like a bubble dissolving into the sea, empty space also vanishes into great enlightenment. How much less the Triple Existence!

Sutra text: 歸元性無二 方便有多門 　聖性無不通 順逆皆方便 　初心入三昧 遲速不同倫。

Transliteration: Quy nguyên tánh vô nhị Phương tiện hữu đa môn, Thánh tánh vô bất thông, Thuận nghịch giai phương tiện, Sơ tâm nhập tam muội, Trì tốc bất đồng luân.

Translation: Returning to the source, the nature is non-dual; Expedients have many doors; The sagely nature is all-penetrating; Accord and opposition are both expedients; Beginners entering samadhi Differ in quickness and slowness.

Commentary: In the verse, Manjushri Bodhisattva says that empty space is like a floating bubble in the sea of enlightenment, and the lands born within that empty space are also extremely subtle. If empty space vanishes, then all lands, mountains, rivers, lands, all beings and sentient and material worlds will also vanish. Returning to the source, the nature is non-dual.

"Returning to the source" means accomplishing Buddhahood. There is only one place to return to: your own home base. The world we are living in is not our own nature's home. You at once object, "I have a home!" But that home is not your true home. Becoming a Buddha is recognizing your true home. Before becoming a Buddha, you are a wanderer drifting from one hotel to another. You are ever moving.

Expedients have many doors. As for "expedients," they still involve entanglement. For example, once a child was crawling toward the mouth of a well on the ground. If the child kept crawling, it would fall into the well. The Buddha saw this, but he knew that if he called the child to come back, it would not obey but would crawl forward all the more. So he clenched his fist, raised it high, and called, "Child! Come back! I shall give you candy. Do you like candy?" When the child heard of candy, it at once crawled back. There was in fact no candy in the Buddha's hand. But did the Buddha lie? No. That is an example of expedient dharma. The Buddha used "the empty fist to rescue the child" because at the time there was no other way. Expedient dharma-doors are many. In general, any method you use to rescue people is called an expedient dharma.

The sagely nature is all-penetrating.
Accord and opposition are both expedients.

Once you have certified to the Dharma-nature of a sage, there is nothing you do not understand. Whatever accords is expedient, and whatever opposes is also expedient. Whatever suits your capacity and circumstances, you may apply in cultivation. What is "opposing" — what does not suit one's circumstances yet is still applied in cultivation. Both accord and opposition in one's cultivation effort are expedient dharmas.

Beginners entering samadhi
Differ in quickness and slowness.

Some cultivate very quickly, some slowly. So they cannot be regarded as of one kind.

Sutra text: 色想結成塵 精了不能徹 如何不明徹 於是獲圓通。

Transliteration: Sắc tưởng kết thành trần Tinh liễu bất năng triệt, Như hà bất minh triệt, Ư thị hoạch viên thông

Translation: Form and thought combine to make objects; Their essence cannot penetrate. How from what is not penetrating Can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Form is made from false thought. Form and false thought combine together into "objects." That is form-objects. Their essence cannot penetrate. It is not clear and cannot be fully known.
How from what is not penetrating
Can one attain perfect penetration?
Could you hope to certify to perfect penetration with a method that is neither clear nor thorough? That is impossible. The verse tells us that using form-objects to cultivate perfect penetration is fundamentally not the best method. Some people may certify to fruition through this method, but only because they have special affinities with that particular dharma-door. That is not something everyone can cultivate.

Sutra text: 音聲雜語言 但伊名句味 　一非含一切 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Âm thinh tạp ngữ ngôn Đãn y danh cú vị Nhất phi hàm nhất thiết Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Sound mixed with speech Relies only on words and phrases; Since the one does not contain the all, How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Some people certify to the Way by means of sound-objects. However,
Sound mixed with speech
Relies only on words and phrases.
If the one does not contain the all —
No single word, no single name, no single sentence can speak of everything. Then
How can one attain perfect penetration?
So sound-objects cannot be chosen as the method for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 香以合中知 離則元無有 不恒其所覺 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Hương dĩ hợp trung tri Ly tắc nguyên vô hữu Bất hằng kỳ sở giác Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Fragrance is known only in union; Apart, it fundamentally does not exist. Its object of awareness does not constantly abide — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The Child Fragrance-Adorned certified to the Way through fragrance-objects. But fragrance functions only in union. The nose must inhale the fragrance before it knows there is fragrance. Apart, it fundamentally does not exist. Fragrance does not exist.
Its object of awareness does not constantly abide —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
Because the nature of fragrance is neither constant nor unchanging, we do not always have awareness of it, and so fragrance-objects are not regarded as the best method for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 味性非本然 要以味時有 其覺不恒一 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Vị tánh phi bản nhiên Yếu dĩ vị thời hữu Kỳ giác bất hằng nhất Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: The nature of flavor is not inherent; Only when tasted does it exist. Its awareness is not constant and single — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Though some have become enlightened through flavor-objects, flavor is not inherently existent. The nature of flavor is not the perfect self-nature. For only when tasted does it exist. Flavor exists only when there is something flavored; only then do flavor-objects exist.
Its awareness is not constant and single —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
The knowing-nature of flavor is not always present. Therefore this method is not given as a dharma-door for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 觸以所觸明 無所不明觸 　合離性非定 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Xúc dĩ sở xúc minh Vô sở bất minh xúc Hợp ly tánh phi định Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Touch is known through what is touched; Without something, touch is unknown. Its nature in union and separation is indeterminate — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Touch is known through what is touched.
Though some become enlightened through cultivating touch-objects, touch exists only when there is something touching.
Without something, touch is unknown.
The only way to feel touch is for someone to create contact with something.
In union and separation, its nature is indeterminate.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
Therefore, touch-objects are likewise not used as a method for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 法稱為內塵 憑塵必有所 能所非遍涉 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Pháp xưng vi nội trần Bằng trần tất hữu sở Năng sở phi biến thiệp Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Dharmas are called inner objects; Relying on objects, there must be a "somewhere." Subject and object do not wholly interpenetrate — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Mahakashyapa cultivated the mind root through dharma-objects, and he certified to the samadhi of the cessation of feeling and thought.
Dharmas are called inner objects.
Dharma-objects are the objects of the mind root.
Relying on objects, there must be a "somewhere." (sense faculty)
Since they are objective realms, they must have a location. Since they have a location, they cannot be at the level of "empty yet not empty."
Subject and object do not wholly interpenetrate. The interfusion of subject and object (subject/object) is not yet thorough, not yet complete.
How can one attain perfect penetration?

Sutra text: 見性雖洞然 明前不明後 四維虧一半 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Kiến tánh tuy đỗng nhiên Minh tiền bất minh hậu Tứ duy khuy nhất bán Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: The seeing-nature, though clear and penetrating, Sees before but not behind; Of the four directions, half is lacking — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The seeing-nature, though clear and penetrating. The eye can see clearly and penetratingly. But it sees before but not behind. If the eyes look forward, they cannot see behind. If they look right, they cannot see left. Of the four directions, half is lacking. One can see only two of the four directions at once.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
So that is not the method selected for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 鼻息出入通 現前無交氣 支離匪涉入 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Tỵ tức xuất nhập thông Hiện tiền vô giao khí Chi ly phỉ thiệp nhập Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: The nose's breath goes out and in; Between, at present there is no exchange of breath; Fragmented, not interfused — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The nose's breath goes out and in.
This verse discusses the nose root. Between, at present there is no exchange of breath. Sometimes the breath is held. Breathing stops.

Fragmented, not interfused. This state is a deficiency and makes the nose root unsuitable too. It is not entirely perfect. How can one attain perfect penetration? Therefore it cannot be chosen as the method for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 舌非入無端 因味生覺了 味亡了無有 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Thiệt phi nhập vô đoan Nhơn vị sanh giác liễu Vị vong liễu vô hữu Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: The tongue without flavor has no ground for entering; Through flavors awareness arises. When flavors vanish, awareness is utterly gone — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The tongue without flavor has no ground for entering. Flavor must contact the tongue (the tongue root) before that taste-awareness exists. Without flavor, nothing is known. Through flavors awareness arises. The experience of awareness comes through flavor-objects. When flavors vanish, awareness is utterly gone.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
You cannot use this method to cultivate perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 身與所觸同 各非圓覺觀 　涯量不冥會 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Thân dữ sở xúc đồng Các phi viên giác quán Nhai lượng bất minh hội Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: The body aware of touch is the same as its object of touch; Neither is a perfect, enlightened regard. Limited, not darkly merged — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The body aware of touch is the same as its object of touch.
The method of using the body root (for cultivation) is also like touch-objects. Neither is pervasive, neither complete.
Their knowing-nature is not yet fully complete.
Limited, not darkly merged —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
It is measured by limits and quantity, and that is an unseen relationship with touch-objects; therefore it is not chosen as the best perfect-penetration cultivation.

Sutra text: 知根雜亂思 湛了終無見 想念不可脫 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Tri căn tạp loạn tư Trạm liễu chung vô kiến Tưởng niệm bất khả thóat Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: The knowing root is mixed with scattered thought; In still clarity there is ultimately no seeing. If discursive thought cannot be cast off — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The knowing root is mixed with scattered thought. What the mind knows is dharma-objects — a mixture of scattered thoughts.
In still clarity there is ultimately no seeing.
If discursive thought cannot be cast off —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
It never reaches what is called still extinction, nor ever reaches the ultimate, because people can never transcend while thought-moments — false thoughts and waves of consciousness — still exist. How could these factors lead to perfect penetration?

Sutra text: 識見雜三和 詰本稱非相 自體先無定 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Thức kiến tạp tam hoà Cật bổn xưng phi tướng Tự thể tiên vô định Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Conscious seeing is mixed of the threefold union; Probed to its root, it is called markless. Its own substance fundamentally lacks fixity — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Conscious seeing arises through root and object.
This verse passage concerns the consciousnesses, which are the union of the six inner roots and the six outer objects. The six roots have knowing, while the six objects do not. Thus the six consciousnesses are half-knowing and half-unknowing. These three components combine to make consciousness. Probed to its root, it is called markless. Consciousness has no self-marks.
Its own substance fundamentally lacks fixity.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
For the consciousnesses themselves are in a state of constant flux. How could one use them to cultivate perfect penetration? Hence eye-consciousness is also not selected.

Sutra text: 心聞洞十方 生于大因力 初心不能入 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Tâm văn đỗng thập phương Sanh vu đại nhân lực Sơ tâm bất năng nhập Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Mind-hearing penetrates the ten directions, Born of the power of a great cause; Beginners' minds cannot enter it — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Mind-hearing penetrates the ten directions. The dharma-door Samantabhadra Bodhisattva cultivated is ear-consciousness. But the hearing-nature pervades only through the power of a great causal condition.
This dharma-door requires power from a most supreme causal condition. Only then can this dharma-door be cultivated. Beginners' minds cannot enter it. Beings who have just brought forth the resolve to cultivate the Bodhisattva Way will not suit this dharma-door. Since beginners cannot cultivate this dharma-door, then How can one attain perfect penetration? This dharma-door is also not selected.

Sutra text: 鼻想本權機 秖令攝心住 　住成心所住 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Tỵ tưởng bổn quyền cơ Kỳ linh nhiếp tâm trụ Trụ thành tâm sở trụ Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Contemplating the nose-tip is but a provisional device, Only to gather the mind to dwell. Dwelling makes the mind something dwelt-in — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Contemplating the nose-tip is but a provisional device. Sundarananda cultivated the contemplation of the white mark on the nose-tip. Cultivating this dharma-door involves thought, so it is a skillful device. Only to gather the mind to dwell. That method serves to settle the mind.
If the object contemplated becomes "something dwelt-in" —
The goal of this method is to bring the mind to dwell in one place, but since there continues to be a place for the mind to dwell, then How can one attain perfect penetration? So this dharma-door is also not selected.

Sutra text: 說法弄音文 開悟先成者 名句非無漏 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Thuyết pháp lộng âm văn Khai ngộ tiên thành giả Danh cú phi vô lậu Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Speaking Dharma employs sounds and words; It awakens only those already accomplished. Names and phrases are not unconditioned — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Purna Maitrayaniputra spoke Dharma and became enlightened through the tongue root. Speaking Dharma employs sounds and words. When speaking Dharma and lecturing sutras, the spoken sounds must be beautiful and must be perfectly expressed in writing. So it only awakens those who have already planted Buddha seeds in the past. Names and phrases are not unconditioned. How can one attain perfect penetration?

Since these are objects of conditioned dharmas, that dharma-door cannot be chosen as the means to cultivate perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 持犯但束身 非身無所束 元非遍一切 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Trì phạm đãn thúc thân Phi thân vô sở thúc Nguyên phi biến nhất thiết Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Keeping or breaking precepts only binds the body; Apart from the body, what is there to bind? Fundamentally not pervading all — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The Elder Upali specialized in upholding precepts. Keeping precepts only binds the body. Keeping or breaking precepts lies with the body. This is a body-related dharma concerning body and mind. Apart from the body, what is there to bind?
If you had no body, there would be nothing to restrain or control.
Fundamentally not pervading all —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
This method is not complete. So it is not selected as the means to cultivate perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 神通本宿因 何關法分別 念緣非離物 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Thần thông bổn túc nhơn Hà quan pháp phân biệt Niệm duyên phi ly vật Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Spiritual powers come from past-life causes; What have they to do with discriminating dharmas? Thought-moments never leave things — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Maudgalyayana was foremost in spiritual powers, which he obtained through consciousness.
Spiritual powers come from past-life causes.
Having spiritual powers comes from causes accumulated in past lives. That has nothing to do with discriminating consciousness. That is an entirely different matter from discriminating consciousness.
Thought-moments never leave things.
Yet spiritual powers still require the process of thought-moments. Thus spiritual powers are not separate from the physical category, so in themselves they are not complete. How can one attain perfect penetration? So cultivating to obtain spiritual powers is also not the best way.

Sutra text: 若以地性觀 堅礙非通達 　有為非聖性 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Nhược dĩ địa tánh quán Kiên ngại phi thông đạt Hữu vi phi thánh tánh Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: If one contemplates the nature of earth, Its hardness obstructs, not penetrating. The conditioned is not the sagely nature — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: If one contemplates the nature of earth.
Its hardness obstructs, not penetrating.
The Bodhisattva Upholding Earth used the method of contemplating the nature of the earth element. Earth has the qualities of hardness and obstruction. It is not interfused. That is a conditioned dharma, not a dharma-door for entering the sagely flow.
The conditioned is not the sagely nature —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
It cannot be regarded as the best method for reaching perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 若以水性觀 想念非真實 如如非覺觀 云何獲圓通

Transliteration: Nhược dĩ thuỷ tánh quán Tưởng niệm phi chơn thật Như như phi giác quán Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: If one contemplates the nature of water, Contemplative thought is not true; Suchness is not perceiving regard — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Some cultivators wish to cultivate by contemplating the water element and entering the Water-Contemplation samadhi as Moonlight Youth cultivated.
If one contemplates the nature of water,
Contemplative thought is not true,
For when the cultivator enters samadhi by this method, the process of thought-moments, the state of subtle deliberation, is still involved at first. But since the realm of suchness is not perceiving regard, the method of contemplating the water element is not a method of contemplating the original nature.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
Hence the method of contemplating the Water element is not selected as the perfect-penetration cultivation.

Sutra text: 若以火性觀 厭有非真離 　非初心方便 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Nhược dĩ hoả tánh quán Yếm hữu phi chơn ly Phi sơ tâm phương tiện Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: Contemplating the fire element to dispel the fire of lust Comes from weariness with suffering, not true departure. It is not an expedient for beginners — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The Vajra Fire Chief Ucchushma cultivated the contemplation of the Fire element, because he had a very strong lustful mind. The Buddha taught him to contemplate the fire of lust within his body.
Contemplating the fire element to dispel the fire of lust
Comes from weariness with suffering, not true departure.
This resolve to abandon the lustful mind is not in itself true departure. This is not an expedient for beginners. Duality is not the unsurpassed bodhi dharma. How can one attain perfect penetration? This method cannot be chosen as the dharma-door for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 若以風性觀 動寂非無對 對非無上覺 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Nhược dĩ phong tánh quán Động tịch phi vô đối Đối phi vô thượng giác Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: If one contemplates the nature of wind, Movement and stillness are not without duality; What is dual is not the unsurpassed enlightenment — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: The Prince Vaidurya Light used the Wind element to cultivate perfect penetration. If one contemplates the nature of wind —
Movement and stillness are not without duality.
Movement and stillness are two dualities, not absolutes.
What is dual is not the unsurpassed enlightenment.
Duality is not the supreme enlightened dharma.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
This method cannot be given for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 若以空性觀　 　昏鈍先非覺 　無覺異菩提　　 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Nhược dĩ không tánh quán Hôn độn tiên phi giác Vô giác dị bồ đề Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: If one contemplates the nature of space, Space, dull and dark, is fundamentally unaware. Unawareness differs from bodhi — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: If one contemplates the nature of space. The Bodhisattva Space Treasury cultivated by contemplating his body as vast as empty space and became enlightened. But in this verse, Manjushri Bodhisattva says: I regard the nature of the Space element and see that space, dull and dark, is fundamentally unaware. This factor lacks the brightness that would suit beginners.
Unawareness differs from bodhi —
How can one attain perfect penetration?
This method is not selected as the dharma-door for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 若以識性觀 觀識非常住 存心乃虛妄 云何獲圓通。

Transliteration: Nhược dĩ thức tánh quán, Quán thức phi thường trụ, Tồn tâm nãi hư vọng, Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: If one contemplates the nature of consciousness, Consciousness contemplated is not constantly abiding; Dwelling on mind is falseness — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Maitreya Bodhisattva cultivated from the Consciousness element. He contemplated the nature of the six consciousnesses. If one contemplates the nature of consciousness, consciousness contemplated is not constantly abiding. Just look at the discriminating mind-consciousness: it does not dwell long. Dwelling on mind is falseness. Wherever there is an object to contemplate and a contemplating thought, there is falseness. How can one attain perfect penetration? So this method is not regarded as perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 諸行是無常 念性無生滅 　因果今殊感 云何獲圓通 。

Transliteration: Chư hành thị vô thường, Niệm tánh vô sanh diệ, Nhân quả kim thù cảm, Vân hà hoạch viên thông?

Translation: All activities are impermanent; The nature of mindfulness is within birth and death. Cause and effect are now vastly different — How can one attain perfect penetration?

Commentary: Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva cultivated the Seeing element. He gathered in all six sense roots without selection, with pure mindfulness in succession.
All activities are impermanent.
Mindfulness is by nature within birth and death.
Both the nature of the mindfulness and the object of mindfulness belong to birth and death. When you recite, it appears; when you stop reciting, it vanishes.
Cause and effect are now vastly different.
We hope to transcend the idea of cause and effect.
How can one attain perfect penetration?
So the Buddha-recitation dharma-door is also unsuitable for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 我今白世尊 佛出娑婆界 此方真教體 清淨在音聞 欲取三摩提　　 實以聞中入。

Transliteration: Ngã kim bạch Thế tôn Phật xuất ta-bà giới Thử phương chơn giáo thể Thanh tịnh tại âm văn Dục thủ tam ma đề Thật dĩ văn trung nhập.

Translation: I now address the World Honored One: The Buddha appears in the Saha world; The true teaching-substance of this land Dwells purely in sound-hearing. Wishing to attain samadhi, One truly enters through hearing.

Commentary: At this point, Manjushri Bodhisattva has finished presenting the dharma-doors the sages certified to. He continues:
I now address the World Honored One.
The Buddha appears in the Saha world.
The true teaching-substance of this land
Dwells purely in sound.
In this world called "endurance," where the Buddha has manifested out of compassion, the true method for teaching beings is the purity of sound. That refers to the dharma-door of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature.
Wishing to attain samadhi,
One truly enters through hearing.
The effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature is truly the most sublime, the best of all dharma-doors.

Sutra text: 離苦得解脫 良哉觀世音

Transliteration: Ly khổ đắc giải thoát Lương tai Quán Thế Âm

Translation: Leaving suffering, attaining liberation — Excellent, O Avalokiteshvara!

Commentary: Leaving suffering, attaining liberation. We can leave suffering far behind and attain liberation. Leaving suffering is liberation. Liberation is precisely leaving suffering far behind. Excellent, O Avalokiteshvara! Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's dharma-door is truly sublime!

Sutra text: 於恒沙劫中 入微塵佛國 得大自在力 無畏施眾生。

Transliteration: Ư hằng sa kiếp trung Nhập vi trần phật quốc Đắc đại tự tại lực Vô uý thí chúng sanh.

Translation: Through kalpas as numerous as Ganges' sands, Entering Buddha-lands as numerous as dust motes, Attaining the power of great ease, Bestowing fearlessness upon beings.

Commentary: Why does Manjushri Bodhisattva praise Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva? Through kalpas as numerous as Ganges' sands, entering Buddha-lands as numerous as dust motes. Through many kalpas, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva entered countless Buddha-lands as numerous as dust motes. Attaining the power of great ease.
Bestowing fearlessness upon beings. With spiritual powers and great ease, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva enabled all beings to be without fear.

Sutra text: 妙音觀世音 梵音海潮音 救世悉安寧 出世獲常住。

Transliteration: Diệu âm Quán Thế Âm Phạm âm hải triều âm Cứu thế tất an ninh Xuất thế hoạch thường trụ.

Translation: Sublime the sound of Guanshiyin — Pure sound, ocean-tide sound — Rescuing the world, all find peace; Transcending the world, attaining permanence.

Commentary: Sublime the sound of Guanshiyin.
Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva is infinitely sublime.
Pure sound, ocean-tide sound.
His pure and clear sound is like the roar of the ocean waves. Rescuing the world, all find peace. He rescues all beings in this world, bringing peace and contentment to all.
Transcending the world, attaining permanence.
He transcends the world and certifies to the ever-abiding enlightened nature. He attains indestructible spiritual powers of ease, and ever-abiding.

Sutra text: 我今啟如來 如觀音所說 譬如人靜居 十方俱擊皷 十處一時聞 此則圓真實。

Transliteration: Ngã kim khải Như Lai Như Quán Âm sở thuyết Thí như nhân tĩnh cư Thập phương câu kích cổ Thập xứ nhất thời văn Thử tắc viên chơn thật.

Translation: I now address the Tathagata: As Avalokiteshvara has described — Suppose a person dwelling in stillness, While in the ten directions drums are beaten; Heard in ten places at a single time — This is perfect truth.

Commentary: I now address the Tathagata.
As Avalokiteshvara has described his cultivation and certification of perfect penetration.
Suppose a person dwelling in stillness,
While in the ten directions drums are beaten,
Heard in ten places at a single time.
In each place of the ten directions drums are beaten at the same time. Though the drum sounds come from ten directions, a person in a quiet room can hear those drum sounds at the same time.
This is perfect truth.
This (hearing) nature is truly perfect.

Sutra text: 目非觀障外 口鼻亦復然 　身以合方知 心念紛無緒。

Transliteration: Mục phi quán chướng ngoại Khẩu tỵ diệc phục nhiên Thân dĩ hợp phương tri Tâm niệm phân vô tự

Translation: The eye cannot see beyond obstructions; Mouth and nose are likewise. The body knows only in union; Mind-thoughts are tangled without order.

Commentary: The eye cannot see beyond obstructions.
"Eye" here is not the Buddha eye, wisdom eye, Dharma eye, heavenly eye, or flesh eye — it is not the flesh eye. What is meant here is the ordinary eye. These eyes can see only within limits; they cannot see penetratingly or above. They cannot see through obstructing things. For instance, if we close the windows and let down the curtains, we cannot see the scenery outside at all. Even in perceiving things close at hand for use, a single layer of skin blocks us from seeing the way. As with our inability to see anything inside the body with ordinary eyes. The eyes of sages are another matter, but here we are discussing the capacity of the ordinary eye. It cannot see through even a thin sheet of paper! Likewise, looking right it cannot see left, and looking left it cannot see right.
Mouth and tongue are likewise.
Between breaths there is also a pause when no air enters or leaves the nose. And the tongue must have flavor before the tasting-nature is known. With nothing to taste, the tongue is useless. So these two roots are both more or less like the eye root.
The body knows only in union.
The body must contact the object of touch before touch-awareness exists; thus it too is not complete.
Mind-thoughts are tangled without order.
Thought-moments are scattered and confused, with no order to them at all; so they too are not entirely good for cultivating perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 隔垣聽音響 遐邇俱可聞 五根所不齊 是則通真實。

Transliteration: Cách viên thính âm hưởng Hà nhĩ câu khả văn Ngũ căn sở bất tề Thị tắc thông chơn thật

Translation: Through walls, sounds are heard; Far and near, all can be heard. The five roots cannot match this — This is true penetration.

Commentary: With the ear root, through walls, sounds are heard. You still hear what is on the other side of a wall. Far and near, all can be heard.
The five roots cannot match this. Eyes, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not function like the ear root — it is more perfect than these roots. Its function is entirely interfused and unobstructed. The other roots cannot compare with the ear root. This is true penetration. Those other five senses lack this true penetration.

Sutra text: 音聲性動靜 聞中為有無 　無聲號無聞 非實聞無性。

Transliteration: Âm thinh tánh động tĩnh Văn trung vi hữu vô Vô thinh hiệu vô văn Phi thật văn vô tánh.
