Translation: The nature of sound has movement and stillness; Within hearing these become "existing" and "non-existing." When soundless, it is called "not hearing" — But truly the hearing-nature is not absent.

Commentary: The nature of sound has movement and stillness.
Sometimes there is sound, sometimes no sound. When there is no sound, it is called stillness. Within hearing these become "existing" and "non-existing." The hearing-nature recognizes the movement of sound and the stillness when there is no sound. When soundless, it is called "not hearing." We call it so. But truly the hearing-nature is not absent. The hearing-nature definitely does not vanish. When we say we do not hear, the hearing-nature in fact never vanishes.

Sutra text: 聲無既無滅 聲有亦非生 　生滅二圓離 是則常真實。

Transliteration: Thinh vô ký vô diệt Thinh hữu diệc phi sanh Sanh diệt nhị viên ly Thị tắc thường chơn thật.

Translation: When soundless, the hearing-nature is not extinguished; When sounding, the hearing-nature does not arise. Both arising and ceasing fully transcended — This is eternal truth.

Commentary: When soundless, the hearing-nature is not extinguished.
The absence of sound does not mean the hearing-nature has been lost. When sounding, the hearing-nature does not arise. When hearing sound, nothing changes in the hearing-nature.
Both arising and ceasing fully transcended —
This is eternal truth.
The hearing-nature is eternally self-sufficient within itself and apart from both ideas of arising and ceasing. Arising and ceasing have become entirely interfused. The hearing-nature is the ever-abiding nature, unchanging, not an object of arising and ceasing.

Sutra text: 縱令在夢想 不為不思無 覺觀出思惟 身心不能及。

Transliteration: Túng linh tại mộng tưởng Bất vị bất tư vô Giác quán xuất tư duy Thân tâm bất năng cập

Translation: Even amid dreams and thoughts, It is not that, unthought of, it is absent. Awakened regard transcends thought; Body and mind cannot reach it.

Commentary: Whether there is sound or no sound, whether sound has just arisen or has entirely vanished, the hearing-nature never vanishes. People can recognize this in the ordinary waking state. But it is ever present even amid dreams and thoughts.
Someone fast asleep still hears the pounding of the washing mallets and the rice-hulling pestles like bells and drums playing together. This proves that the hearing-nature is present even in dreams.
It is not that, unthought of, it is absent.
Unlike the mind, which does not exist when not thinking.
Awakened regard transcends thought. The knowing of that hearing-nature transcends thinking.
Body and mind cannot reach it.
Body and mind can never compare with the hearing-nature of the ear root.

Sutra text: 今此娑婆國 聲論得宣明 眾生迷本聞 循聲故流轉 阿難縱強記 不免落邪思 豈非隨所淪 旋流獲無妄。

Transliteration: Kim thử ta-bà quốc Thanh luận đắc tuyên minh Chúng sanh mê bổn văn Tuần thinh cố lưu chuyển A-nan túng cường ký Bất miễn lạc tà tư Khởi phi tuỳ sở luân Triền lưu hoạch vô vọng.

Translation: Now in this Saha land, The doctrine of sound is proclaimed; Beings have lost their original hearing, Following sounds, thus they turn. Ananda, though of strong memory, Could not avoid falling into deviant thought. Is it not through what engulfs one That, turning the flow, one attains freedom from falseness?

Commentary: Now in this Saha land,
The doctrine of sound is proclaimed.
Beings have lost their original hearing.

They do not recognize their inherent hearing-nature. Following sounds, thus they turn.
They do not know to turn the hearing back to recognize their own nature. They delight in seeking outside; they listen outwardly. They chase after sound-objects and seek outwardly. If one lets the ear root chase after sound-objects instead of turning the hearing back inward, one will fall into the flow of birth and death. That is also a knot. With birth and death, there are knots. It begins because you chase after sound-objects. You cannot pull it back.
Ananda, though of strong memory. Ananda is most intelligent and of strong memory. He could memorize by heart the sutras of the Tripitaka. Yet he could not avoid falling into deviant thought.

Though intelligent, Ananda still could not escape the calamity with Matanga's daughter and the Brahma-heaven mantra. Ananda was captured by the outsiders' deviant magic.
Is it not through what engulfs one
That, turning the flow, one attains freedom from falseness?

If you can return the hearing to hear the self-nature, then naturally you will have no falseness to resist. You will no longer make such mistakes. The reason Ananda was so easily caught by deviant magic is that Ananda was always seeking outside. Ananda studied this, then learned that, and mastered this sutra, then that sutra, but never turned the light back to shine within. Ananda never stopped to consider why he thought and acted as he did. All Ananda did was study. He studied so much he forgot what he himself was. This reminds me of Confucius's answer when someone asked:
"Is there anyone in the world like..." the questioner began.
"Like what?" Confucius asked.
"It goes, taking everyone along with it — taking along family relatives, except its own wife. It forgets to take its wife along. Is there such a kind of person?"
Can you guess how Confucius answered? Did Confucius answer that forgetting to take one's wife along is impossible? Or did he answer that forgetting to take one's wife along is possible for people?
Confucius answered: "Nowadays, people even forget themselves!" Not only do they forget their wives, they forget their own bodies. That is, they do not know that in the future their bodies will die. They forget that they will pass through old age, sickness, and death.

Because Ananda focused on studying things outside himself and on developing his scholarly ability, Ananda neglected cultivating to develop samadhi power. Because Ananda neglected samadhi power, he did not know how to apply the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature; so Ananda chased after sound-objects. Ananda did not return sound-objects to his own nature, so Ananda fell into calamity with Matanga's daughter.

Sutra text: 阿難汝諦聽 我承佛威力 　宣說金剛王 如幻不思議 　佛母真三昧。

Transliteration: A-nan nhữ đế thính Ngã thừa Phật oai lực Tuyên thuyết Kim cang vương Như huyễn bất tư nghị Phật mẫu chơn tam muội.

Translation: Ananda, listen attentively! Relying on the Buddha's awesome power, I proclaim the Vajra King's samadhi — Illusory, inconceivable, the true samadhi that is mother of Buddhas.

Commentary: When Manjushri Bodhisattva reached this point, he called to Ananda. Manjushri Bodhisattva is a Dharma Prince of most venerable age, while Ananda is still very young. Here, Manjushri Bodhisattva speaks on behalf of Shakyamuni Buddha proclaiming the teaching, so he draws Ananda's attention. Ananda! Listen attentively!
Pay attention! Listen to every word; slight none of it. Do not sit there dozing while I speak this verse! You should know that this verse I am speaking is not from my own idea. The verse is proclaimed through the awesome power the Buddha transmitted to me. The Buddha appointed me to speak and expound this content. He told me to select the dharma-door for your cultivation. You should not think it is I, Manjushri, speaking this to you; it is precisely the Buddha speaking to you. Do you understand now?
Proclaiming the Vajra King's samadhi. Relying on the Buddha, I shall proclaim the dharma-door of the Vajra King.
Illusory, inconceivable,
The true samadhi that is mother of Buddhas.

This is a cultivation that needs no cultivation. Cultivating yet not cultivating. Not cultivating yet cultivating. It is rather like a game, so at the same time it is real. The subtlety lies there. You cannot imagine how sublime this dharma-door is. You cannot imagine it or express that sublimity in words. That samadhi is the mother of Buddhas. All Buddhas are born from this samadhi. So pay attention. Do you wish to become a Buddha? If so, attend to what I shall say. And then you must apply effort. Do not merely waste effort on outer skills. You must attain the effort of inner regard.

Sutra text: 汝聞微塵佛 一切祕密門 欲漏不先除 　畜聞成過誤。

Transliteration: Nhữ văn vi trần Phật Nhất thiết bí mật môn Dục lậu bất tiên trừ Súc văn thành quá ngộ

Translation: You have heard the Buddhas as numerous as dust motes And all their secret doors; If desire-outflows are not first removed, Hoarded hearing becomes error.

Commentary: Manjushri Bodhisattva continues:
You have heard the Buddhas as numerous as dust motes
And all their secret doors.

Ananda, you have heard countless Buddhas speak of secret dharma-doors. "Secret" means you say something for one person to hear that a second person does not know. Or you speak about the second person what the first person does not know. Each person does not know what was said to the other. Why does the Buddha have secret dharma-doors? Because beings' natures differ. Each being likes different things. Moreover, each person cultivated different dharma-doors in past lives. Therefore the Buddha regards potentials; he examines which dharma-door you cultivated in a past life, and on that basis teaches you how you should cultivate now.
Regarding potentials, bestowing teaching.
Teaching Dharma to each person individually.

He does not teach you a dharma-door unsuited to you.
If desire-outflows are not first removed,
Hoarded hearing becomes error.

Though the Buddha has many secret dharma-doors, you still have not rid yourself of desire-outflows. "Desire" is truly most hard to subdue. The moment you have lust, you have outflows. The gravest lust, which everyone finds hardest to cut off, is lust for fame and beauty. If you can rid yourself of this, you are extraordinary. When you study the Buddhadharma, you must rid yourself of lust before you can eliminate all outflows.

The fourth fruition of Arhatship is without outflows. The first fruition of Arhatship is the stage of seeing the Way — the result of cutting off the eighty-eight portions of view-delusions. The second fruition of Arhatship is called the stage of cultivating the Way. The fourth fruition of Arhatship is called the stage of certifying to the Way. At the first, second, and third fruitions of Arhatship, one is not yet called certified to the outflow-free fruition. Only at the fourth fruition is the outflow-free fruition certified. Attaining the outflow-free fruition is most important. Why has Ananda not reached this fruition? Because Ananda has not rid himself of lust. Ananda still delights in certain things. Ananda is not yet pure; hence the Dharma Prince Manjushri says to Ananda, "If you do not cultivate and extinguish the greedy mind for fame and beauty, you will not accord with the Buddhadharma. If you devote yourself solely to erudition, you will fall into error. That is why you met with calamity with Matanga's daughter. If you renounce lust and outflows, you will no longer meet such calamities."

When we see a clever person like Ananda still making this mistake, we should note that not only have we not been strict with lust, we even intend to pursue it. We have never thought of ridding ourselves of it. Do you see that as another error? By now, everyone should turn the light back to shine within. Do we still have lust? Have we rid ourselves of it? If not, there is nothing to discuss. If you wish to rid yourselves of it, then quickly begin cultivating the effort of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature. Study Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's dharma-door of the ear-root's perfect penetration.

Sutra text: 將聞持佛佛 　何不自聞聞。

Transliteration: Tương văn trì phật phật Hà bất tự văn văn?

Translation: Taking hearing to uphold the Buddhas' Dharma — Why not hear your own hearing?

Commentary: "Taking hearing to uphold the Buddhas' Dharma. You have wasted effort studying the Buddhadharma," Manjushri says to Ananda. "With that effort, why not hear your own hearing? Why do you not turn the hearing back to recognize your own hearing-nature? Why do you not develop this cultivation effort? Why do you not turn back to look into yourself?"

Sutra text: 聞非自然生 　因聲有名字 旋聞與聲脫 能脫欲誰名。

Transliteration: Văn phi tự nhiên sanh Nhơn thinh hữu danh tự Triền văn dữ thinh thóat Năng thóat dục thuỳ danh.

Translation: Hearing does not arise of itself; Because of sound it has a name. Turn the hearing back, apart from sound; What name for that which is apart?

Commentary: Ananda, do not continue to be so intent on study that you neglect cultivating samadhi power. Hearing does not arise of itself. In itself it utterly does not come from nature.
Because of sound it has a name. Because there are sound-objects, there is hearing. We call the recognition of sound-objects "hearing sound." Turn the hearing back, apart from sound. What name for that which is apart? We say there is hearing because there is sound — but when there is no sound, does hearing remain? Hearing remains. For the hearing-nature is not an object of birth and death. Therefore, turn the hearing back. From now on, do not chase after the six roots and six objects. Bring the six roots and six objects back to the self-nature.
Return the hearing to hear the self-nature,
And one becomes the Unsurpassed Way.

What is your self-nature? When you listen, you will recognize it. Now, before you recognize it, you will not understand until I tell you. For instance, when I drink this cup of tea, I myself know whether the tea is cold or hot, but you still know nothing. If you wish to know, you must drink the tea yourself. If you wish to recognize your own self-nature, first of all, you must turn the hearing back. If you do not, how can you hope to recognize your self-nature? You ask:
"When turning the hearing back, how does one hear?"

Use your ears, but do not listen to outer sounds. Do not try to find out what is happening on the street, or who is saying what. Turn the hearing inward and listen to your own inside. In this way your self-nature will manifest. That is how you practice. Do you understand now?

When turning the hearing back, one is at ease with outer sounds. "What name for that which is apart?" If you yourself can be entirely apart from outer sounds — hearing yet not hearing — is this not truly the hearing-nature? It is, and it is not. Not, yet it is. Hearing yet not hearing. That means being at ease with sounds. One hears, but not as one heard before. Though one knows ordinary hearing can hear far or near, it still has a limit. If you truly attain the effort of turning the hearing inward to recognize your own nature, then you can hear throughout the entire Dharma Realm. But you may also choose to hear nothing of the entire Dharma Realm's sounds. You must be in control. Like the telegraph. If I wish to send, I can send to people everywhere at any time. If I do not wish to send a telegram, I shall not do it. If I wish to hear any sounds in the Dharma Realm, I can switch it on. Try it and see. What is such ease with sounds called? It fundamentally has no name. It is what transcends the names of hearing and the true hearing-nature.

Sutra text: 一根既返源 六根成解脫

Transliteration: Nhất căn ký phản nguyên Lục căn thành giải thoát

Translation: Once one root has returned to the source, The six roots are liberated.

Commentary: As soon as names are no more, one may say that the mind root has been opened.
Once one root has returned to the source,
The six roots are liberated.

"Source" is the Tathagatagarbha nature. When one sense root returns to the Tathagatagarbha nature, all six roots merge together. The elder brothers return home and the younger siblings follow along. But if you do not bring one root back, none of the roots will follow along. They are related to one another, for fundamentally they are one, but they have been divided into six.

Sutra text: 見聞如幻翳 　三界若空花 聞復翳根除 　塵銷覺圓淨。

Transliteration: Kiến văn như huyễn ế Tam giới nhược không hoa Văn phục ế căn trừ Trần tiêu giác viên tịnh.

Translation: Seeing and hearing are like illusory films over the eyes; The Triple Realm like flowers in space. Hearing restored, the film-root removed; Objects dissolved, awareness perfectly pure.

Commentary: Why have we not yet become Buddhas? We are bound by the six roots and six objects. So we must find a method to attain liberation. It is not only we who are bound by roots and objects; at the same time, Ananda shares this problem. We are in the same dilemma. Ananda took this path to liberation, and we are now most fortunate to study that method. We, too, can walk this path and be liberated.
Seeing and hearing are like films over the eyes.

Seeing and hearing are something unreal. They are like an illusion, like a thin film veiling the eyes, like clouds in the sky.
The Triple Realm like flowers in space.
The Desire Realm, Form Realm, and Formless Realm make up the three realms. We are within them, staring into empty space until the staring wearies us. So it looks as if flowers are dancing in empty space. At the start of this verse, Manjushri said:
Empty space arises within great enlightenment
Like a single bubble in the sea.
Empty space arises within great enlightenment
Like a single bubble rising in the sea.

Empty space arises in the vast sea of the enlightened nature, likened to a bubble rising amid the sea of empty space.
Hearing restored, the film-root removed.

When we turn the hearing back to recognize our own nature, that thin film veiling the eyes vanishes.
Objects dissolved, awareness perfectly pure.

When sensory perceptions are no more, guest-objects no longer trouble you. So one's awareness-nature is entirely pure.

Sutra text: 淨極光通達 寂照含虛空 却來觀世間 猶如夢中事 摩登伽在夢 誰能留汝形。

Transliteration: Tịnh cực quang thông đạt Tịch chiếu hàm hư không Khước lai quán thế gian Du như mộng trung sự Ma-đăng-già tại mộng Thuỳ năng lưu nhữ hình?

Translation: Utmost purity, light penetrating; Still shining, containing empty space. Returning to regard the world, It is like a matter within a dream. Matanga's daughter is in the dream — Who can detain your form?

Commentary: Ah! Manjushri Bodhisattva speaks most forcefully. He needs not a bit of elegance. He is bluntly scolding Ananda:
"Utmost purity, light penetrating. Once your enlightened nature is perfect and pure, reaching the utmost, luminous wisdom pervades everywhere. You become enlightened. Still shining, containing empty space. When you attain this effort, empty space is right within you. Your own nature is precisely the all-pervading enlightened nature. When you return to the original nature that has always been yours, you pervade all of empty space.
Returning to regard the world,
It is like a matter within a dream.

As you continue applying this effort, you regard the world and will see it as nothing more than a dream.
Matanga's daughter is but a dream.
Who can detain you?
She is part of the dream. Who is it that could capture you? You lost face. You wanted to be there. You liked her. If you attained the level of effort I have just described, who could restrain you?" You see there is not a bit of elegance. Is there?

Sutra text: 如世巧幻師 幻作諸男女 雖見諸根動 要以一機抽 息機歸寂然 諸幻成無性。

Transliteration: Như thế xảo huyễn sư Huyễn tác chư nam nữ Tuy kiến chư căn động Yếu dĩ nhất cơ trừu Tức cơ quy tịch nhiên Chư huyễn thành vô tánh.

Translation: Like the clever illusionists of the world Who conjure up men and women — Though the roots are seen to move, It all hangs on a single mechanism; When the mechanism rests, all returns to stillness, And the illusions become without nature.

Commentary: Like the clever illusionists of the world.
This is like the puppet shows of old, when puppets danced and performed behind a colored screen. Behind were puppets made of donkey hide, attached to strings worked by the puppeteer, and the audience saw the puppets' shadows reflected upon the curtain. Today we have cinema. The puppets look like real people, but in fact they are worked by puppet-masters. They often fight noisily on stage with swords and guns. I remember watching from childhood.
Who conjure up men and women —
The puppets wear clothes like men and women, then dance upon the stage.
Though the roots are seen to move,
It all hangs on a single mechanism.

They seem able to move arms and legs and even to blink eyes and lips, but in fact it is all machinery. They are connected to a mechanism. Yet the viewers are still stunned.
When the mechanism rests, all returns to stillness,
And the illusions become without nature.
Ultimately, they are nothing at all. In this chapter, Manjushri Bodhisattva explains why all dharmas are like illusions and dreams. The previous chapter already explained clearly why we are within illusions and dreams.

Sutra text: 六根亦如是 　元依一精明 分成六和合 一處成休復 六用皆不成 塵垢應念銷 成圓明淨妙

Transliteration: Lục căn diệc như thị Nguyên y nhất tinh minh Phân thành lục hoà hợp Nhất xứ thành hưu phục Lục dụng giai bất thành Trần cấu ứng niệm tiêu Thành viên minh tịnh diệu.

Translation: The six roots are likewise: Originally relying on one refined brightness, Divided into sixfold union; When one dwelling attains rest and return, The six functions all cease to be; Defiling dust vanishes in a thought, Becoming perfect, luminous purity.

Commentary: Why does Manjushri Bodhisattva speak of dreams and illusions? Because the six roots are like illusory tricks.
The six roots are likewise.
The six roots are like puppet shows performed by puppeteers. It is as if a single mechanism controls them. But if one root becomes pure, the other roots also become at ease.
Originally relying on one refined brightness.
Originally just one refined-bright nature within the Tathagatagarbha. It divides into sixfold union.
Divided into eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
When one dwelling attains rest and return — when the knots have been untied — then the six functions all cease to be.
If one root no longer functions, the other roots will also stop; they no longer have functions.
Defiling dust vanishes in a thought.
Every connection between the six roots and six objects ceases.
Becoming perfect, luminous purity.
They become the luminous, subtle true mind, the ever-abiding pure substance of the Tathagatagarbha.

Sutra text: 餘塵尚諸學 明極即如來。

Transliteration: Dư trần thượng chư học Minh cực tức Như Lai.

Translation: Remaining dust still means learners; Utmost brightness is precisely the Tathagata.

Commentary: Remaining dust still means learners.
When ignorance is first removed, there still remains subtle ignorance called birth-mark ignorance. This means remaining dust — afflictions remaining like dust motes. Bodhisattvas must still eliminate these subtle afflictions.
Utmost brightness is precisely the Tathagata.
That is the nature of the Tathagatagarbha.

Sutra text: 大眾及阿難 旋汝倒聞機 反聞聞自性 性成無上道 圓通實如是。

Transliteration: Đại chúng cập A-nan Triền nhữ đảo văn cơ Phản văn văn tự tánh Tánh thành vô thượng đạo Viên thông thật như thị.

Translation: Great assembly and Ananda: Turn back your inverted hearing mechanism; Return the hearing to hear the self-nature; The nature realized is the unsurpassed Way. Perfect penetration truly is just so.

Commentary: Great assembly and Ananda.
Turn back your inverted hearing mechanism.
You should cultivate by this method. Do not run seeking outside. Turn back. Look within and find yourselves again.
Return the hearing to hear the self-nature.
The nature realized is the unsurpassed Way.
Your nature can perfect the Unsurpassed Way.
Perfect penetration truly is just so.

Why did Manjushri Bodhisattva choose the ear root? Because it is the easiest way to cultivate successfully. I believe some of you already know how to develop this cultivation effort, and some do not. What is meant by turning the hearing inward to recognize one's own nature? It is the effort used in investigating Chan. When investigating Chan, do not spend all your energy seeking outside. You must turn the light back to shine within. Then ask yourself: "Who is reciting the Buddha's name?" "Who?" Place the "Who?" in your mind and listen with your ears. Pursue the "Who?" Do this continuously, without stopping. Do not let your effort be interrupted. Hold this meditation topic in whatever you are doing.
Walking, standing, sitting, lying down, never leave this effort.
If you leave the effort, you have gone wrong.

What is "this"? That is the question. "Who is reciting the Buddha's name?" You need not recite aloud; just ask in your mind and listen with your ears. Listen within, not without. Once you have heard within, your mind and your hearing-nature will finally merge into one. And then, unexpectedly, at an unanticipated moment, you suddenly become enlightened. But you absolutely must bring your mind and your nature back into one. Do not let them scatter in many directions. Do not let them dissipate outward. Gather them inward. Turn the hearing inward to recognize your own nature. Eventually and naturally your effort will develop. Investigating Chan and the effort of turning the hearing inward to recognize your own nature are the same. And now everyone knows that using the ear root to cultivate perfect penetration is the easiest method. So put all your mind's strength into cultivating this method.

Sutra text: 此是微塵佛 　一路涅槃門 過去諸如來 　斯門已成就 現在諸菩薩 　今各入圓明 未來修學人 　當依如是法 我亦從中證 　非唯觀世音。

Transliteration: Thử thị vi trần Phật Nhất lộ niết-bàn môn Quá khứ chư Như Lai Tư môn dĩ thành tựu Hiện tại chư bồ tát Kim các nhập viên minh Vị lai tu học nhơn Đương y như thị pháp Ngã diệc tòng trung chứng Phi duy Quán Thế Âm.

Translation: This is the Buddhas as numerous as dust motes' Single road, the door to nirvana; The Tathagatas of the past Have already perfected this door. The Bodhisattvas of the present Now each enter perfect brightness. Future students Should rely on this Dharma. I too was certified through it — Not Avalokiteshvara alone.

Commentary: Now Manjushri Bodhisattva certifies the authenticity of the dharma-door he has selected.
This is the Buddhas as numerous as dust motes'
Single road, the door to nirvana.
He says: "Not only did Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva become enlightened using this cultivation — the cultivation effort leading to the perfect penetration I have explained — I myself, Manjushri, also certify to this ear-root perfect-penetration dharma-door. Not only I, but the Buddhas as numerous as dust motes in the past also found this road for entering nirvana."
The Tathagatas of the past
Have already perfected this door.

They perfected enlightenment through the perfect-penetration cultivation arising from the effort of turning the hearing inward to recognize one's own nature.
The Bodhisattvas of the present
Now each enter perfect brightness.
The Bodhisattvas cultivating in this life all walk this same path.
Future students
Should rely on this Dharma.

People in future lives who have not met the Buddhadharma will choose this cultivation. I too was certified through this Dharma. Long ago I perfected this dharma-door and certified to perfect penetration. Not Avalokiteshvara alone.

Sutra text: 誠如佛世尊 詢我諸方便 以救諸末劫 求出世間人 成就涅槃心 觀世音為最。

Transliteration: Thành như Phật Thế tôn Tuân ngã chư phương tiện Dĩ cứu chư mạt kiếp Cầu xuất thế gian nhơn Thành tựu niết-bàn tâm Quán Thế Âm vi tối.

Translation: Truly as the World Honored Buddha Asks me about expedients, To rescue in the final kalpas Those who seek transcendence, To perfect the nirvana mind — Guanshiyin is supreme.

Commentary: Truly as the World Honored Buddha
Asks me about expedients.
O Buddha, I speak the truth; I speak what is truly so. The method to rescue in the final kalpas —
Those who seek transcendence,
To perfect the nirvana mind.
Among the eighteen realms and seven elements, which dharma-door is most perfectly penetrating? Which best suits the potentials of beings in the Dharma-Ending Age? Those who wish to leave the world and seek transcendence — how can they perfect their aspiration to cultivate the Way and certify to nirvana?
Guanshiyin is supreme.
The best method is regarding the sounds of the world.
Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, now manifesting in the Saha realm, best accords with this dharma-door. This dharma-door is most suitable, most fitting for everyone's potentials.

Sutra text: 自餘諸方便 皆是佛威神 即事捨塵勞 非是長修學 淺深同說法。

Transliteration: Tự dư chư phương tiện Giai thị Phật oai thần Tức sự, xả trần lao Phi thị trường tu học Thiển thâm đồng thuyết pháp.

Translation: As for all other expedients, They all rely on the Buddha's awesome spirit; Right within phenomena, abandoning worldly toil. They are not the long-term cultivation and study Equally taught to the shallow and deep.

Commentary: As for all other expedients,
They all rely on the Buddha's awesome spirit.
In cultivating any expedient dharma-doors other than ear-root perfect penetration, we must all rely on the Buddhas' protection to succeed. Without the Buddhas' support, we can accomplish nothing.
Right within phenomena, abandoning worldly toil.
They are not the long-term cultivation and study
Equally taught to the shallow and deep.

Though some have used these expedients to abandon worldly toil, afflictions, and false thoughts, that is not the only method everyone can apply. When speaking Dharma, one must regard causes and conditions. One must regard each person's potentials. For the wise, one must speak the profound, sublime Dharma. For those lacking wisdom, one should explain simple principles. Dharma can never always be spoken in the same way. Only the ear root is the most perfectly-penetrating dharma-door for every root of cultivation. I consider this dharma-door the most perfectly penetrating.

Sutra text: 頂禮如來藏 無漏不思議 　願加被未來 於此門無惑 　方便易成就 堪以教阿難 　及末劫沈淪 但以此根修 　圓通超餘者 真實心如是。

Transliteration: Đảnh lễ Như Lai tạng Vô lậu bất tư nghị Nguyện gia bị vị lai Ư thử môn vô hoặc Phương tiện dị thành tựu Kham dĩ giáo A-nan Cập mạt kiếp trầm luân Đãn dĩ thử căn tu Viên thông siêu dư giả Chơn thật tâm như thị.

Translation: I bow to the Tathagatagarbha, The unconditioned, inconceivable; I vow to aid the future, That in this door there be no delusion. The expedient easy to perfect Is fit to teach Ananda And the submerged of the final kalpa: Just cultivate with this root; Perfect penetration surpasses all others. The true mind is just so.

Commentary: After Manjushri Bodhisattva finished presenting this verse, he reverently bowed to the Triple Jewel.
I bow to the Tathagatagarbha.
"Tathagata" is the Buddhas; "garbha" (treasury) is the Tripitaka — that is, the Dharma.
The unconditioned, inconceivable.
"And the unconditioned ones" is the Sangha. The unconditioned Bodhisattvas and Arhats have all certified to inconceivable states. Their spiritual powers and sublime functions are hard to conceive. Manjushri Bodhisattva bows to the sages of the Sangha.

I vow to aid the future,
That in this door there be no delusion.
I vow to ask them to aid all beings in future lives, that they have not a shred of doubt about the transliteration-door of returning the hearing to hear the self-nature.
The expedient easy to perfect
Is fit to teach Ananda.

This method is both easy to cultivate and easy to perfect. It is the best dharma-door for Ananda to cultivate. There is no better dharma-door.
And the submerged of the final kalpa:
Just cultivate with this root.
This dharma-door suits not only Ananda, but all potentials of beings in the Dharma-Ending Age. Just use the ear root as the means of cultivation.
Perfect penetration surpasses all others.
The true mind is just so.
This perfect-penetration cultivation surpasses the other twenty-five expedient dharma-doors. Easier, and bringing surpassing results. The true mind attained through this cultivation is as I have explained above.

Sutra text: 於是阿難及諸大眾,身心了然得大開示。觀佛菩提及大涅槃猶如有人因事遠遊未得歸還。明了其家所歸道路。

Transliteration: Ư thị A-nan cập chư đại chúng, thân tâm liễu nhiên, đắc đại khai thị. Quán Phật bồ-đề cập đại niết-bàn du như hữu nhân nhân sự viễn du vị đắc quy hoàn. Minh liễu kỳ gia sở quy đạo lộ.

Translation: Thereupon Ananda and the great assembly, body and mind all-clear, received the great instruction. They regarded the Buddhas' bodhi and great nirvana like a person who, traveling far on business, has not yet returned home, but clearly knows the road home.

Commentary: Thereupon Ananda and the great assembly, body and mind all-clear. They attained thorough understanding. Receiving the profound instruction. Regarding the Buddhas' bodhi and great nirvana.
They fully recognized the Buddha's and Manjushri Bodhisattva's profound, sublime teaching. They regarded the teaching on bodhi-nirvana like a person who, traveling far on business, has not yet returned home, but clearly knows the road home.
These people have gone far on business and have not yet returned home. But they have gone far enough to still remember the road home. The meaning is that although Ananda and the assembly members have not yet certified to the first, second, or third Arhat fruitions, now at least they have recognized the principle.

Sutra text: 普會大眾天龍八部有學二乘,及諸一切新發心菩薩,其數凡有十恒河沙皆得本心,遠塵離垢獲法眼淨。

Transliteration: Phổ hội đại chúng thiên long bát bộ hữu học nhị thừa, cập chư nhất thiết tân phát tâm Bồ-tát, kỳ số phàm hữu thập hằng hà sa giai đắc bổn tâm, viễn trần ly cấu hoạch pháp nhãn tịnh.

Translation: The entire assembly — gods, dragons, and the eight divisions, learners of the Two Vehicles, and all newly-resolved Bodhisattvas, ten Ganges' sands in number — all attained their original minds, left dust and defilement far behind, and gained the pure Dharma eye.

Commentary: The entire assembly — gods, dragons, and the eight divisions.
Ghosts and spirits; the eight divisions comprise gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, dragons.
Learners of the Two Vehicles — referring to Hearers awakened to the principle of Conditioned Origination. Together with all newly-resolved Bodhisattvas, ten Ganges' sands in number, they all attained their original minds. Unlike before, when they had not recognized their original minds. They left dust-marks far behind; thus they gained the pure Dharma eye.

Sutra text: 性比丘尼聞說偈已成阿羅漢。

Transliteration: Tánh tỷ-khưu-ni văn thuyết kệ dĩ thành A-la-hán.

Translation: The bhikshuni Xing, hearing the verse spoken, became an Arhat.

Commentary: The bhikshuni named Xing was Matanga's daughter. She certified to Arhatship right after hearing Manjushri speak this verse. By then, she had surpassed Ananda, for she had certified to the second Arhat fruition, while Ananda had only certified to the first fruition.

Sutra text: 無量眾生皆發無等等阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心

Transliteration: Vô lượng chúng sanh giai phát vô đẳng đẳng A-nậu-đa-la Tam-miệu tam-bồ-đề tâm.

Translation: Countless beings all brought forth the resolve for unsurpassed, equal-and-unequal anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Commentary: By this time, countless immeasurable beings in the Dharma assembly brought forth the resolve for unsurpassed, equal-and-unequal anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Nothing can compare with the degree of this resolve. It is utterly true. Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi means unsurpassed, right and equal, right enlightenment.
Anuttara means unsurpassed, with nothing comparable.
Samyak means right (proper) and equal. Sambodhi is right enlightenment, true enlightenment. Their vow is to become Buddhas.

***
(End of volume 5, start of volume 6 according to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas edition.)

Sutra text: 阿難整衣服。望大眾中,合掌頂禮。心迹圓明,悲欣交集。欲益未來諸眾生故,稽首白佛大悲世尊。我今已悟成佛法門。是中修行得無疑惑。常聞如來說如是言。自未得度先度人者菩薩發心。自覺已圓能覺他者如來應世。我雖未度願度末劫一切眾生。

Transliteration: A-nan chỉnh y phục. Vọng đại chúng trung, hợp chưởng đảnh lễ. Tâm tích viên minh, bi hân giao tập. Dục ích vị lai chư chúng sanh cố, khể thủ bạch Phật: “Đại bi Thế tôn. Ngã kim dĩ ngộ thành Phật pháp môn. Thị trung tu hành đắc vô nghi hoặc. Thường văn Như Lai thuyết như thị ngôn: ‘Tự vị đắc độ, tiên độ nhân giả, Bồ-tát phát tâm. Tự giác dĩ viên, năng giác tha giả, Như Lai ứng thế. Ngã tuy vị độ, nguyện độ mạt kiếp nhất thiết chúng sinh’.”

Translation: Ananda arranged his robes. Facing the great assembly, he joined his palms and bowed. His mind's traces perfectly bright, grief and joy intermingled. Wishing to benefit beings of the future, he bowed his head and said to the Buddha: "Greatly compassionate World Honored One, I have now awakened to the dharma-door for becoming a Buddha. Cultivating within it, I attain freedom from doubt. I often hear the Tathagata say: 'One not yet delivered who first delivers others — that is a Bodhisattva's resolve. Self-enlightenment perfected, able to enlighten others — that is a Tathagata's advent in the world. Though I am not yet delivered, I vow to deliver all beings of the final kalpa.'"

Commentary: After Ananda heard Manjushri Bodhisattva's verse, he stood up and arranged his robes. Ananda straightened his collar and pulled his kashaya robe neat. Ananda never had a bit of carelessness or negligence, never letting his robes be sloppy. Facing the great assembly, he joined his palms and bowed. His mind's nature entirely bright. Ananda was no longer deluded as before. He felt both joy and sorrow. Wishing to benefit beings of future lives, he bowed his head to the Buddha:

Ananda did not know whether to laugh or cry. Do you remember how easily Ananda weeps? Ananda has wept several times since the sutra-lecture assembly began, and now wants to weep again. But Ananda also wants to laugh. What was Ananda's concern? It is because of the saying:

Extreme joy gives birth to sorrow — utmost joy is sorrow.
Ananda was most joyful, thinking: "Now I have obtained the Buddhadharma; I have penetrated the true teaching." Ananda had never been so joyful. But understanding for himself alone was not enough; Ananda wished to benefit beings in future lives. So Ananda bowed to the Buddha and said:

"Greatly compassionate World Honored One, I have now awakened to the dharma-door for becoming a Buddha. Cultivating within it, I attain freedom from doubt.
I shall rely on the Dharma to cultivate and shall never again have a shred of doubt. "I often hear the Tathagata say..."

Ananda often proved what he said by citing the Buddha's own teachings. Here Ananda says, "I hear the Buddha teach that, 'One not yet delivered who first delivers others — that is a Bodhisattva's resolve.'"
When oneself is not yet enlightened, yet one can aspire to teach others first — that is the way of Bodhisattvas.
"Self-enlightenment perfected, able to enlighten others — that is a Tathagata's advent in the world."

You help people become enlightened through the principle you have certified — that is what the Buddhas did.
Though I am not yet delivered, I vow to deliver all beings of the final kalpa.
Though I have not yet certified to the Way, I wish to help all beings of the Dharma-Ending Age be delivered. I wish them all to receive benefit in the Buddhadharma.

Sutra text: 世尊,此諸眾生去佛漸遠。邪師說法如恒河沙。欲攝其心入三摩地。云何令其安立道場遠諸魔事,於菩提心得無退屈?

Transliteration: Thế tôn, thử chư chúng sanh khứ Phật tiệm viễn. Tà sư thuyết pháp như hằng hà sa. Dục nhiếp kỳ tâm nhập tam-ma-địa, vân hà linh kỳ an lập đạo tràng, viễn chư ma sự, ư bồ-đề tâm đắc vô thối khuất?

Translation: World Honored One, these beings grow ever farther from the Buddha. Deviant teachers speaking Dharma are as numerous as Ganges' sands. Wishing to gather their minds into samadhi, how shall they be made to establish a Way-place, stay far from demonic deeds, and never retreat in the bodhi resolve?

Commentary: World Honored One, these beings grow ever farther from the Buddha. Beings of the Dharma-Ending Age gradually grow distant from the Buddha and even from the Buddhadharma.

Deviant teachers speaking Dharma are as numerous as Ganges' sands. That is the situation now. Deviant teachers proclaim they understand what they really do not understand. Unenlightened, they say they are enlightened. Uncertified to sagely fruition, they say they are certified. I ask them: "Have you certified to the first, second, third, fourth Arhat fruitions? Which fruition have you certified to? Have you become enlightened? What have you awakened to?" They fall silent. I continue: "You are a Buddha, yet you cannot say which fruition you have certified to. How did you leap into Buddhahood?" Still they persist, saying that not only are they Buddhas, but "Everyone is a Buddha." That is their tune. This is great false speech. When you have not reached that state, you cannot speak at will. Nothing is worse than a deviant teacher. Take care never to become such a person, whether or not you know the Buddhadharma. Do not be like one of them who, when someone comes asking about Dharma, answers, "I am old; I have forgotten."

What does forgetting mean? He does not know where to begin. That way of speaking deliberately deceives people. If you know, say you know. If you do not know, say you do not know. One cannot say one has forgotten when one never understood what was asked.

When deviant teachers proclaim their methods, hoping for offerings, the teaching they speak is deviant. For instance, lust is wrong, but they say it is good. "That is the best dharma-door." They praise it, deluding people so they cannot distinguish the true teaching. What is wrong, they call right; what is right, they call wrong. They hold deviant knowledge and deviant views. Their outlook is incorrect.

Ananda says, "In the Dharma-Ending Age, such deviant teachers are very many."

Wishing to gather their minds into samadhi —
Though at that time there will be as many deviant teachers as Ganges' sands, still I vow that beings will give rise to right knowledge and right views.

How shall they be made to establish a Way-place, stay far from demonic deeds, and never retreat in the bodhi resolve?

For instance, there are some deviant teachers and outsiders who only know how to cheat people with their doctrines. They speak much about relations between men and women, claiming the more lust, the sooner Buddhahood. This is utterly wrong. Utterly deviant! You must note this. Do not let these people cheat you. In the right Dharma, every mention of lust as approval is wrong. Methods teaching people so are demons' exploitation. Ananda vows to help people of the Dharma-Ending Age dwell in the bodhi resolve. Some people study the Buddhadharma for a while, then retreat from the bodhi resolve. "I shall study no more Buddhadharma. It is too hard! I must abandon all my faults. But what if I cannot abandon them? Better that I do not study at all."
They lose their zeal. They accept retreat. They are subdued by demons.
Ananda wishes to know how to keep this from happening.

Sutra text: 爾時世尊於大眾中,稱讚阿難。善哉!善哉!如汝所問,安立道場救護眾生末劫沈溺。汝今諦聽,當為汝說。阿難大眾唯然奉教

Transliteration: Nhĩ thời Thế tôn ư đại chúng trung, xưng tán A-nan Thiện tai! Thiện tai! Như nhữ sở vấn, an lập đạo tràng cứu hộ chúng sanh mạt kiếp trầm nịch. Nhữ kim đế thính, đương vị nhữ thuyết. A-nan đại chúng duy nhiên phụng giáo.

Translation: Thereupon the World Honored One, amid the great assembly, praised Ananda: "Excellent! Excellent! As you ask, about establishing Way-places to rescue beings drowning in the final kalpa. Now listen attentively; I shall speak for you." Ananda and the assembly respectfully accepted the teaching.

Commentary: Ananda says he wishes beings of the Dharma-Ending Age never to retreat from the bodhi resolve. Ananda wishes them to have firm faith, vowing to protect the Buddhadharma, study the Buddhadharma, and never retreat from the bodhi resolve. But how is Ananda to help them do so? When Shakyamuni Buddha heard Ananda ask thus, he was most delighted. The Buddha dwells in the realm of thusness, unmoving, yet when someone brings forth the resolve to protect the Buddhadharma and help all beings become Buddhas, it still delights him.

Thereupon the World Honored One, amid the great assembly, praised Ananda: "Excellent! Excellent!"
The Buddha was pleased. "Ananda! You are most good!" He praised Ananda twice.
As you ask, about establishing Way-places to rescue beings drowning in the final kalpa.
You wish to rescue beings of the Dharma-Ending Age drowning in water and fire.

Now listen attentively; I shall speak for you. Ananda and the assembly respectfully accepted the teaching.
When they heard the Buddha agree to speak Dharma, their joy grew greater. Perhaps the Buddha said, "Do you wish to hear this?" Everyone answered without hesitation. "We wish to hear. We wish to hear."
When deviant teachers teach their doctrines, the sole topic is lust. What they present runs counter to principle. This you should distinguish clearly. Sometimes Bodhisattvas also use kindness, loving speech, and protective minds to teach beings, because they know beings are submerged in lust. All beings have false thoughts of lust. So Bodhisattvas do not expect them to cut off greedy lust all at once. Rather they use every expedient to bring beings through and beyond lust. Then each being sets its own stopping point. This is the case with Bodhisattvas — entirely different from what deviant outsider teachers do.

Once Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva transformed into a fish-seller — a most beautiful woman going through the village with a basket of fish. No one in the village believed in the Buddha. But when the young men of the village saw this fish-selling girl, they all desired her. The village was not large, but there were at least a hundred men there, and everyone wished to marry this girl as wife. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, basket of fish in hand, said, "You are too many! I cannot marry a hundred people! But I have thought of a way to choose one of you as husband. I shall marry whichever of you first memorizes the Universal Door chapter of the Dharma Flower Sutra. Go home and study. I give you three days."

Three days later, some forty or fifty people had memorized this sutra. The fish-selling woman said, "Still too many. Though you have qualified, I cannot take fifty as husbands. Now go home and memorize the Vajra Sutra. I shall marry whoever first memorizes this sutra within five days." So these fifty top candidates went home and began studying the Vajra Sutra. Five days later twenty people had memorized this sutra. The fish-selling woman said, "Still too many. I cannot marry you all. I have another condition. Whoever can memorize the Dharma Flower Sutra within seven days shall deserve to be my husband."
The twenty men returned to study the Dharma Flower Sutra; seven days later one man had memorized this sutra. His name was Ma, born of a wealthy family. So a grand wedding took place and everyone in the village was invited. That night, after the feast ended, they went home — but who knew the bride suffered a heart attack and suddenly died.
And the groom had wasted all his effort. He had memorized the Universal Door chapter, the Vajra Sutra, the Dharma Flower Sutra, yet still had not married a wife. At once a funeral was held; a monk appeared among the mourners in a purple kashaya. The monk asked: "What has happened?"
"Our new daughter-in-law has suddenly died; we are holding the funeral."

The monk answered: "There is nothing in the coffin! For whom are you holding the funeral? Open the coffin lid and look!"
Indeed, the coffin was empty. They were all amazed. "Where has she gone? Chase her! Catch her back!"

The monk told them: "She is Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. The people of this village do not believe in the Buddha, so the Bodhisattva manifested as a beautiful girl to teach you, who are so lustful, to understand the Buddhadharma. Then she departed."
When the groom named Ma heard this, he renounced everything in the world and left home. Later, he certified to sagely fruition. This story is true; it happened in China.

Sutra text: 佛告阿難,汝常聞我毘奈耶中,宣說修行三決定義。所謂攝心為戒,因戒生定,因定發慧。是則名為三無漏學。

Transliteration: Phật cáo A-nan, nhữ thường văn ngã tỳ-nại-da trung, tuyên thuyết tu hành tam quyết định nghĩa. Sở vị nhiếp tâm vi giới, nhơn giới sanh định, nhơn định phát huệ. Thị tắc danh vi tam vô lậu học.

Translation: The Buddha said to Ananda: "You often hear me in the Vinaya proclaim the three decisive meanings of cultivation: gathering the mind is called precepts; from precepts samadhi arises; from samadhi wisdom unfolds. These are called the three unconditioned studies."

Commentary: When everyone in the Dharma assembly was of one mind to protect the teaching, the Buddha said to Ananda: "You often hear me in the Tathagata's Vinaya proclaim the three decisive meanings of cultivation."

"Vinaya" comprises the precepts for both the Great and Small Vehicles. Within it are the precept rules. These three certain aspects cannot be changed. That is: gathering the mind is called precepts; from precepts samadhi power arises; from samadhi there is wisdom. These are called the three unconditioned studies.

That is precepts, samadhi, wisdom. You gather the mind, like a magnet drawing all iron filings. This refers especially to our seeking, clinging minds — always seeking advantage. Driven by the seeking mind, one is always noticing others. One is always scheming to draw near the rich or the powerful. Such thoughts continue day after day. That is called the seeking mind, meaning one has not yet gathered the mind. Gather the mind back; do not let it seek to satisfy advantages. Do not let it run wild. But the mind is what we chase after, though we do not wish it so.

We may forbid it to have false thoughts, but a moment later another false thought arises. This false thought stops, another arises. The first thought has just vanished, the next at once recurs. And before the first thought has entirely vanished, the next has already arisen. The mind clinging to other things never stops. What you must do is gather your own mind. Bring the mind back to one place. The greatest reason we have not yet become Buddhas, not become enlightened, not certified to the Way, is that we cannot control our minds. If you gather all your mind-thoughts, there is nothing you cannot do. You will accomplish everything. So precepts serve to gather the mind. The precepts put an end to all evils and prevent transgressions.

From precepts samadhi power arises. Upholding precepts is like letting a cup of muddy water settle, until the mud sinks and the water becomes clear. Samadhi means "stopping — unmoving." And from samadhi there is wisdom.

As Manjushri Bodhisattva's verse says:
Samadhi utmost, perfectly bright.
When you become enlightened, within samadhi true wisdom arises. These are called the three unconditioned studies.
Through keeping precepts, from precepts there is samadhi. Through samadhi wisdom unfolds.

THE FOUR CLEAR AND UNALTERABLE EXPOSITIONS
1. ONE MUST END LUST

Sutra text: 阿難,云何攝心我名為戒。若諸世界六道眾生其心不婬。則不隨其生死相續。

Transliteration: A-nan, vân hà nhiếp tâm, ngã danh vi giới? Nhược chư thế giới lục đạo chúng sanh kỳ tâm bất dâm, tắc bất tuỳ kỳ sanh tử tương tục.

Translation: Ananda, why do I call gathering the mind precepts? If beings of the six paths in all worlds had no lustful minds, they would not follow the continuity of birth and death.

Commentary: Ananda, why do I call gathering the mind precepts? The Tathagata will now tell you. If beings of the six paths in all worlds had no lustful minds. The six paths — the realms of gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and beings in the hells. If those beings had no lustful thoughts, then they would not follow the continuity of birth and death. They would cut off birth and death.

Sutra text: 汝修三昧,本出塵勞。婬心不除,塵不可出。

Transliteration: Nhữ tu tam-muội, bổn xuất trần lao. Dâm tâm bất trừ trần bất khả xuất.

Translation: In cultivating samadhi, your fundamental aim is to transcend worldly toil. If the lustful mind is not removed, one cannot transcend the dust.

Commentary: The Buddha says to Ananda: In cultivating samadhi, your fundamental aim is to transcend worldly toil. You wish to transcend birth and death. If the lustful mind is not removed, one cannot transcend worldly toil. If you do not cut off lustful desire, you can never transcend the toil and affliction of the world. For lustful thought itself is defilement. It is itself worldly toil and affliction. Not to speak of engaging in lustful acts — the mere presence of this idea is already defilement. If you do not abandon the lustful mind, there is utterly no reason to hope for enlightenment and Buddhahood.

Keeping the lustful mind on the one hand and hoping to perfect enlightenment on the other is the most stupid thinking. Some think that method is hard to teach. Even if Shakyamuni Buddha himself manifested in the world right now, he would have no way to bring such people to enlightenment. Such people are of the dullest kind.

Sutra text: 縱有多智禪定現前,如不斷婬.必落魔道。上品魔王,中品魔民,下品魔女。

Transliteration: Túng hữu đa trí thiền định hiện tiền, như bất đoạn dâm, tất lạc ma đạo. Thượng phẩm ma vương, trung phẩm ma dân, hạ phẩm ma nữ.

Translation: Though one has much wisdom and samadhi manifests, if lust is not cut off, one will surely fall into the demonic paths. The highest grade becomes demon kings; the middle grade becomes demon people; the lowest grade becomes demon women.

Commentary: Though one has much wisdom and samadhi manifests, if lust is not cut off, one will surely fall into the demonic paths.

You may have intelligence, and when you sit in meditation you may feel light and at ease and feel most free — meaning you can enter meditative concentration. So do you suppose you have wisdom? If you do not cut off the lustful mind, in the end you will become a demon.

The highest grade becomes demon kings in the heaven of the Six Desires; the middle grade becomes demon people — ordinary kinds of demons. The lowest grade becomes demon women. They are most beautiful, but most vicious. Wise people should be careful. Intelligent people should note this passage of sutra. Do not let cleverness in the end turn back to harm yourselves. Do not take the attitude: "You do not know, but I know. You are not clear, but I am clear." That is only petty cleverness, vulgar understanding. Do not let your promising future be ruined.

Sutra text: 彼等諸魔亦有徒眾。各各自謂成無上道。

Transliteration: Bỉ đẳng chư ma diệc hữu đồ chúng. Các các tự vị thành vô thượng đạo.

Translation: Those demons also have retinues. Each claims to have perfected the unsurpassed Way.

Commentary: These people, with a little knowledge, unable to cut off the lustful mind, are always talking about lust. "I love you, and you love me." And they love back and forth until they become demons. Then what happens? Those demons also have retinues. Each claims to have perfected the unsurpassed Way.

They too have disciples and supporters. They are utterly shameless, always loudly proclaiming they have perfected the supreme Way. "I am a Buddha! We are all unsurpassed and none compare!" Fundamentally such people are demons, but they do not admit it; they proclaim themselves in place of the Buddhas. You see, there are still false Buddhas. But they do not see themselves as false. They see themselves as true. They believe: Above heaven, below earth, I alone am honored.

Sutra text: 我滅度後末法之中,多此魔民熾盛世間。廣行貪婬為善知識,令諸眾生。落愛見坑失菩提路。

Transliteration: Ngã diệt độ hậu mạt pháp chi trung, đa thử ma dân xí thạnh thế gian. Quảng hành tham dâm, vi thiện tri thức, linh chư chúng sanh lạc ái kiến khanh, thất bồ-đề lộ.

Translation: After my extinction, in the Dharma-Ending Age, many of these demon people will blaze across the world. Committing lustful acts far and wide, posing as good spiritual teachers, they cause beings to fall into pits of love and views, losing the road to bodhi.

Commentary: Shakyamuni Buddha says: "While the Tathagata is still in the world, these demons dare not display themselves, but after the Tathagata's extinction, many of these demon people will blaze across the world."

That is precisely our own age being mentioned in the sutra. As the teaching approaches ruin, there will be very many such demons about, going everywhere proclaiming lust. And they themselves are intoxicated with lust, whether as men or as women. At the same time, they think they are enlightened and have become Buddhas.

How can I recognize such people — they say they have become Buddhas — I no longer pay attention to their names. He says he is a Buddha. I say he is a demon.

He asks back: "Who is a demon?"
I answer: "You are a demon."

How do I know? Because he is like what I just described above. He is always talking about feelings and love. "Love, love. I love everyone."

How shameful. By what right do you love everyone? These demons commit lustful acts far and wide.

They blaze fiercely in the world. Deluded people become entangled with them, supposing everything they say is reasonable. Especially will it agree with the thinking of young people. As the saying goes, "Those with the same atrocious tastes flock together." They often praise one another in falling into this path. If they do not approve someone's views, they will not act so.

If the other person's way does not suit, they will not cooperate together. But if their thinking is alike, then the blind lead the blind. How pitiful. Here I am not scolding anyone, but:

If a deluded person
Teaches delusion to others,
When all is said and done,
Then no one understands.
The teacher falls into the hells;
The student must follow along.
The teacher also falls into the hells, and when the disciple also appears there, the teacher asks in surprise, "Why have you come here too? This is a most terrible place."

The disciple answers: "You came here first, and you are our teacher; of course we must follow you."
Posing as good spiritual teachers.
They boast, "I teach in many places to very many people." How ridiculous!
Causing beings to fall into pits of love and views, losing the road to enlightenment.
They cause all who associate with them to fall into pits of lustful love, making them lose the bodhi mind and end their lives in the hells.

Sutra text: 汝教世人修三摩地先斷心婬。是名如來先佛世尊第一決定清淨明誨。

Transliteration: Nhữ giáo thế nhân tu tam-ma-địa, tiên đoạn tâm dâm. Thị danh Như Lai tiên Phật Thế tôn đệ nhất quyết định thanh tịnh minh hối.

Translation: Teach people of the world to cultivate samadhi by first cutting off the lustful mind. This is called the former Buddhas, the World Honored Ones' first decisive, pure, clear instruction.

Commentary: Demon kings promote love. The difference between demon kings and the Bodhisattvas' teaching is most subtle — like turning the palm up or down. How do they differ?

Bodhisattvas also love people, but their love is sheltering compassion, far from lust. But a current of lust runs through everything demon kings say. Demon kings openly approve lust, to the point of saying the more indulgent in lust, the sooner one reaches certification. Such deviant doctrine harms people. Bodhisattvas no longer have lust; they make no distinction between beings and themselves. Demon kings have their own motives; they are greedy for wealth. Bodhisattvas have no motives behind and are not greedy. Related to this is the Buddha's teaching on the Twelvefold Conditioned Origination.

Teach people of the world to cultivate samadhi by first cutting off the lustful mind. Teach them to rid themselves of lustful thoughts. This is called the former Buddhas, the World Honored Ones' first decisive, pure, clear instruction.

This is the teaching method the Tathagata Buddhas employed. This is the decision of the Buddhas of past lives. This is the clear instruction teaching people how to attain a pure mind. Everyone must rid themselves of the lustful mind. There is not a shred of leeway. One cannot say one may both indulge lust and not. Everyone must rid themselves of it. If you wish to reach enlightenment yet retain lustful thoughts, then surely you are a disciple of demons.

Sutra text: 是故阿難若不斷婬修禪定者。如蒸沙石欲其成飯。經百千劫秖名熱沙。何以故此非飯本石沙 成故。

Transliteration: Thị cố A-nan, nhược bất đoạn dâm tu thiền định giả, như chưng sa thạch dục kỳ thành phạn. Kinh bá thiên kiếp kỳ danh nhiệt sa. Hà dĩ cố? Thử phi phạn bổn, thạch sa thành cố.

Translation: Therefore, Ananda, cultivating dhyana without cutting off lust is like cooking sand and stone hoping to make rice. After hundreds of thousands of kalpas, it is still called hot sand. Why? Because it is not the basis of rice; it is made of stone and sand.

Commentary: You see, now the Buddha gives an analogy. He tells Ananda, "You do not yet believe this, so the Tathagata will explain for you. Therefore, Ananda, cultivating dhyana without cutting off lust is like cooking sand hoping to make rice."

If one is not strict with lust yet daily cultivates dhyana, then on the one hand one cultivates, on the other one still leaks (outflows). Everything gained in cultivation effort will be lost tenfold through outflows; if one cultivates tenfold, one will lose a hundredfold through outflows. If one cannot rid oneself of lust, yet sits in meditation longing for enlightenment, aiming at a topsy-turvy joy, this is just like cooking sand hoping to make rice.

After hundreds of thousands of kalpas, it is still just hot sand. It is simply futile. Why? Because it is not the basis of rice; it is only sand and stone.

You hope for enlightenment without abandoning lust. That is just like cooking sand hoping to make rice.

There is nothing more to say here. If you are strict with lust, then though you spend all day with objects of lust, there is no problem. There will be nothing lustful — no male marks, no female marks, no human marks, no self marks, no being marks, no life-span marks. Some shameless people say, "That is my way of life." Just saying it is your way of life is not enough. There is no proof. How do you know it is your way of life? If you live that way, basically you will not know who you are. Do you suppose you have no lustful ideas?

If not, then simply not. No need to go around advertising it. Just show that you truly do not live that way. If you truly have no lust, then:
Nhãn kiến sắc, nội vô hữu
Nhĩ văn trần, tâm bất tri.
The eye sees forms, yet within nothing remains;
The ear hears sense-objects, yet the mind does not know. Then you have some provisions with you. And if you can reach the point of walking, standing, sitting, and lying down together with someone who is an object of lust with no problem at all — no sexual thought arising — that counts. One cannot say the mind still chases lust while gritting one's teeth and insisting, "I can still endure it." That is not enough. It must truly be that in the mind not a single lustful thought arises, the mind unmoving — only then is there truly not a trace of lust in one's mind. That is genuine. If from time to time you still notice what a woman eats, then you still fail as usual.

One day someone became enlightened and sought a teacher for certification.
The teacher asked: "What have you awakened to?"
The person answered: "Oh! Before I never realized it, but now I know clearly that bhikshunis are women."
With the Buddha eye, the teacher saw the person had indeed become enlightened. The teacher certified:
"You speak rightly."
You will say: "Who does not know that?"

If you have not yet become enlightened, you cannot speak so. Because that monk was enlightened, he expressed such a view. This is something you cannot deceive people about — especially since his teacher had attained the Buddha eye. The teacher looked at the monk and saw the monk had certified to the first Arhat fruition.

Sutra text: 汝以婬身求佛妙果,縱得妙悟皆是婬根。根本成婬,輪轉三途,必不能出。如來涅槃,何路修證?

Transliteration: Nhữ dĩ dâm thân cầu Phật diệu quả, túng đắc diệu ngộ giai thị dâm căn. Căn bổn thành dâm, luân chuyển tam đồ, tất bất năng xuất. Như Lai niết-bàn, hà lộ tu chứng?

Translation: Seeking the Buddhas' sublime fruition with a lustful body, though you attain sublime awakening, it is all the lust-root. The root become lust, you must turn in the three paths, surely unable to escape. By what road shall the Tathagata's nirvana be cultivated and certified?

Commentary: The Buddha says to Ananda, "Your fondness for Matanga's daughter concerns not only lustful thoughts, but your lust-root."

Seeking the Buddhas' sublime fruition with a lustful body, though you attain sublime awakening, it is all the lust-root. Though you certify to the quintessence of the sublime principle, you still have not rid yourself of the lust-root.

The root become lust, you must turn in the three paths, surely unable to escape. In the future, you will surely fall into the hells. The "three paths" are the realms of animals, hungry ghosts, and hells. You will surely be involved with these three realms and never escape.

By what road shall the Tathagata's nirvana be cultivated and certified?
Within these realms, which road leads you to the fruitions?

Sutra text: 必使婬機,身心俱斷 。斷性亦無。於佛菩提,斯可希冀。

Transliteration: Tất sử dâm cơ, thân tâm câu đoạn. Đoạn tánh diệc vô. Ư Phật bồ-đề, tư khả hy ký.

Translation: One must cause the lust-mechanism to be cut off in both body and mind. Even the nature of cutting off is gone. Then the Buddhas' bodhi may be hoped for.

Commentary: One must cause the lust-mechanism to be cut off in both body and mind. You must rid yourself of every lustful thought, however slight and subtle. That means ignorance itself must be cut off entirely. It must be done with both body and mind. Even the nature of cutting off is gone. Even the idea of cutting off ignorance must be cut off. Then the Buddhas' bodhi may be hoped for.

Sutra text: 如我此說名為佛說。不如此說即波旬說

Transliteration: Như ngã thử thuyết, danh vi Phật thuyết. Bất như thử thuyết tức ba-tuần thuyết.

Translation: What I say thus is spoken by the Buddhas. What is not spoken thus is spoken by Papiyan.

Commentary: What I say thus is spoken by the Buddhas. This is how the Buddhas speak the Buddhadharma. What is not spoken thus is spoken by Papiyan. It is the demons' speech. "Papiyan" is Sanskrit, meaning "the evil one," referring to Mara, the demon king. All who come to hear sutra lectures surely must be people who can see. The blind cannot come hear the sutra; nor can the deaf and mute. The more people come hear sutra lectures, the cleverer they become. Everyone should open the true wisdom eye and truly turn the ear root back into their own nature. Do not hope to seek outside.

2. ONE MUST END KILLING

Sutra text: 阿難,又諸世界六道眾生,其心不殺,則不隨其生死相續。

Transliteration: A-nan, hựu chư thế giới lục đạo chúng sanh, kỳ tâm bất sát, tắc bất tuỳ kỳ sanh tử tương tục.

Translation: Further, Ananda, if beings of the six paths in all worlds had no killing in their minds, they would not follow the continuity of birth and death.

Commentary: If gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, beings in the hells, bore no heavy thoughts of killing, but instead stopped killing entirely and liberated all beings, then they could leave the wheel of birth and death. Here only thoughts of killing (mental karma) are mentioned, not yet acts of killing (bodily karma). If people stop the karma of killing, they will avoid drifting in birth and death through the six paths, and being lords of karma having to undergo birth-and-death accordingly.

Sutra text: 汝修三昧本出塵勞。殺心不除塵不可出。

Transliteration: Nhữ tu tam-muội, bổn xuất trần lao. Sát tâm bất trừ trần bất khả xuất.

Translation: In cultivating samadhi, your fundamental aim is to transcend worldly toil. If the killing mind is not removed, one cannot transcend the dust.

Commentary: Ananda, you wish to cultivate samadhi power. In cultivating samadhi, your fundamental aim is to transcend worldly toil. From the start, you hoped to escape worldly toil. If the killing mind is not removed, one cannot transcend worldly toil. How can we rid ourselves of killing thoughts? Stop killing entirely and liberate all beings. Above, the sutra text says, "If lustful thoughts are not removed, one cannot transcend worldly toil." So you must be strict with lustful thoughts to hope to escape worldly toil. That is the only way you can escape the wheel of birth and death. But if you still scatter the mind in lustful thoughts and still harbor a heavy killing mind, you can never leave the world. You can never transcend birth and death.

Sutra text: 縱有多智禪定現前,如不斷殺必落神道。上品之人為大力鬼。中品即為飛行夜叉諸鬼帥等。下品當 為地行羅剎。

Transliteration: Túng hữu đa trí thiền định hiện tiền, như bất đoạn sát, tất lạc thần đạo. Thượng phẩm chi nhơn vi đại lực quỷ. Trung phẩm tức vi phi hành dạ-xoa, chư quỷ soái đẳng. Hạ phẩm thượng vi địa hành la-sát.

Translation: Though one has much wisdom and samadhi manifests, if killing is not cut off, one will surely fall among spirits. The highest grade becomes powerful ghosts. The middle grade becomes flying yakshas, ghost commanders, and the like. The lowest grade becomes earth-traveling rakshasas.

Commentary: Though one has much wisdom and samadhi manifests, if killing is not cut off, one will surely fall among spirits. "Wisdom" here refers to worldly cleverness and skill in debate, not transcendental wisdom. It is a kind of ordinary cleverness giving people a certain ability to argue. And though you cultivate to the point of effort in dhyana — you have some responses — still, if you do not rid yourself of killing karma, you will fall into the realm of spirits. That is, you may become a god-spirit ruling the heavens. The highest grade becomes powerful ghosts. That is, mighty soldiers of the heavens. The middle grade becomes flying yakshas, ghost commanders, and the like. Flying yakshas are ghosts that fly through the sky. Or one becomes a commander of ghosts. The lowest grade becomes earth-traveling rakshasas.

Sutra text: 彼諸鬼神亦有徒眾。各各自謂成無上道。

Transliteration: Bỉ chư quỷ thần diệc hữu đồ chúng. Các các tự vị thành vô thượng đạo.

Translation: Those ghosts and spirits also have retinues. Each claims to have perfected the unsurpassed Way.

Commentary: The commanding gods, the powerful ghosts of the heavens, the yaksha ghosts and rakshasa ghosts of the human realm, the ghosts of the hell realm also have retinues. There are some ten thousand different kinds of ghosts. Kuan Ti Kung of China is an example of a god of wealth. But after he took refuge with the Buddha, he was called the Bodhisattva Ch'ieh Lan, a Dharma-protecting spirit. In the Buddha's Dharma assembly, he only stands; he is not permitted to sit. However, the ghosts spoken of here all proclaim themselves to have perfected the unsurpassed Way.

Sutra text: 我滅度後末法之中,多此神鬼熾盛世間。自言食肉得菩提路。

Transliteration: Ngã diệt độ hậu mạt pháp chi trung, đa thử thần quỷ xí thạnh thế gian. Tự ngôn thực nhục đắc bồ đề lộ.

Translation: After my extinction, in the Dharma-Ending Age, many such ghosts and spirits will blaze across the world, claiming that eating meat leads to the bodhi way.

Commentary: After my extinction, in the Dharma-Ending Age, many such ghosts and spirits will blaze across the world. That is precisely the Buddha speaking of the present age — the age you and I are living in. There are countless ghosts and spirits in this Dharma-Ending Age, all because in past lives they did not abandon killing karma. They cultivated, but could not stop killing, so they fell into the realm of spirits. In the Dharma-Ending Age, these kinds will proclaim that eating meat leads to the bodhi way.

They say, "Eating meat and becoming a Buddha are the same. I need not abandon killing or eat vegetarian, yet I am enlightened and have certified to the bodhi way — that is, I am a Buddha." This is like someone proclaiming himself a Buddha yet eating meat, drinking wine, smoking, keeping a group of young disciples and teaching them to smoke marijuana and take drugs. Has anyone ever heard of an enlightened person acting so? When the Buddha became enlightened, he did not use such drugs. Now you use drugs to poison your nervous system, overturn your balanced inner energy, and bring yourself to the brink of death, yet insist you are enlightened. I ask you, is that upside-down or not?

Sutra text: 阿難,我令比丘食五淨肉。此肉皆我神力化生本無命根。汝婆羅門地多蒸濕,加以沙石,草菜不生。我以大悲神力所加。因大慈悲假名為肉。汝得其味。奈何如來滅度之後,食眾生肉名為釋子。

Transliteration: A-nan, ngã linh tỷ-khưu thực ngũ tịnh nhục. Thử nhục giai ngã thần lực hóa sanh, bổn vô mạng căn. Nhữ Bà-la-môn địa đa chưng thấp, gia dĩ sa thạch, thảo thái bất sanh. Ngã dĩ đại bi thần lực sở gia. Nhân đại từ bi giả danh vi nhục. Nhữ đắc kỳ vị. Nại hà Như Lai diệt độ chi hậu, thực chúng sanh nhục danh vi Thích tử?

Translation: Ananda, I permit bhikshus to eat the five kinds of pure meat. Such meat is all transformed by my spiritual power, fundamentally without a life-root. Your brahman land is mostly damp and steamy, and moreover sandy and rocky; vegetables do not grow. I, with the aid of great compassionate spiritual power, provisionally call it meat out of great kindness. You obtain its flavor. How, after the Tathagata's extinction, can those who eat beings' flesh call themselves Shakya's sons?

Commentary: Ananda, I permit bhikshus to eat the five kinds of pure meat.

The Buddha's teaching permits consuming five kinds of meat, as follows:
1) Meat of animals one did not see killed.
2) Meat of animals one did not hear killed.
3) Meat of animals one is certain were not killed for one's own eating.
4) Meat of animals already dead (killed by no one).
5) Meat left over after birds have pecked at it.

Such meat is all transformed by my spiritual power, fundamentally without a life-root. The Buddha himself created these kinds of meat; they did not come from living beings at all. They have no life-root — meaning no consciousness, no warmth, no breath. Your brahman land is mostly damp and steamy, and moreover sandy and rocky; vegetables do not grow.

You are practitioners of pure conduct, yet live in a land full of sand, rock, damp, and heat. I, with the aid of compassionate spiritual power, provisionally call it meat out of great kindness. You obtain its flavor. That is in substance what you are eating. Now the Tathagata permits you to eat such meat. But after the Tathagata's extinction, how can those who eat beings' flesh call themselves Shakya's sons? They do not eat the five kinds of pure meat; they entirely eat beings' flesh. Can they be called the Buddha's disciples? They do not deserve to be regarded as Shakyamuni's disciples — that is, they do not deserve to be monastics.

Sutra text: 汝等當知是食肉人,縱得心開似三摩地,皆大羅剎。報終必沈生死苦海 。非佛弟子。如是之人相殺相吞,相食未已。云何是人得出三界?

Transliteration: Nhữ đẳng đương tri thị thực nhục nhân, túng đắc tâm khai, tợ tam-ma-đề, giai đại la-sát. Báo chung tất trầm sanh tử khổ hải. Phi Phật đệ tử. Như thị chi nhân tương sát tương thôn, tương thực vị dĩ. Vân hà thị nhân đắc xuất tam giới?

Translation: You should know that such meat-eaters, though their minds open as if in samadhi, are all great rakshasas. When their retribution ends, they must sink into the bitter sea of birth and death. They are not the Buddha's disciples. Such people kill and devour one another, eating without end. How can such people transcend the Triple Realm?

Commentary: You should know that such meat-eaters, though their minds open as if in samadhi, are all great rakshasas. With no regard for what kind of meat they are eating. They do not care whether it is among the three kinds of pure meat or the five kinds of pure meat. If it is meat, they eat it. Ananda, you should know that after the Tathagata's extinction, such people will disguise themselves as the Buddha's disciples, and they will use both wine and meat. They are most unrestrained, saying everyone is free to do whatever they wish. Though they have a little awakening or a little wisdom, they only resemble being in samadhi." In truth it is not so. They are like those who came here and proclaimed themselves the Sixth Patriarch.

I asked: "What proof do you have for calling yourself the Sixth Patriarch?"
The person answered: "I have no proof that I am not." He thought that a clever retort. In truth, he belongs to the same kind as those described in this sutra passage. Such people seem to have a little samadhi power, but in fact they are great rakshasas, great demon kings, great ghosts and spirits. When their retribution ends, they must sink into the bitter sea of birth and death. They are not the Buddha's disciples. Though such people wear the Buddha's kashaya and eat the Buddha's food, they are not the Buddha's disciples. Such people kill and devour one another, eating without end. They live and eat meat, minding nothing at all. They keep devouring one another. They kill one another; you eat me, I eat you back; killing and eating; then in turn being killed and eaten.

How can such people transcend the Triple Realm? Thus they create an endless wheel of birth and death. This life you eat my flesh; next life I eat yours. The life after, back again you eat mine, and on it goes. How can such beings transcend the Desire Realm, Form Realm, and Formless Realm?

Sutra text: 汝教世人修三摩地,次斷殺生。是名如來先佛世尊第二決定清淨明誨。

Transliteration: Nhữ giáo thế nhân tu tam-ma-địa, thứ đoạn sát sanh. Thị danh Như Lai Tiên Phật Thế Tôn đệ nhị quyết định thanh tịnh minh hối.

Translation: Teach people of the world to cultivate samadhi by next cutting off killing. This is called the Tathagatas, the former Buddhas, the World Honored Ones' second decisive, pure, clear instruction.

Commentary: Teach people of the world to cultivate samadhi by next cutting off killing. First, cut off lust; then also restrain killing thoughts. This is called the Tathagatas, the former Buddhas, the World Honored Ones' second decisive, pure, clear instruction. This is the teaching the Buddha proclaims. Both the Buddhas of the past and the Buddhas of this age proclaim this decisive, pure, clear teaching. You must surely honor this teaching. Otherwise, you can never transcend the three realms.

Sutra text: 是故阿難,若不斷殺修禪定者,譬如有人自塞其耳,高聲大叫求人不聞。此等名為欲隱彌露。

Transliteration: Thị cố A-nan, nhược bất đoạn sát tu thiền định giả, thí như hữu nhân tự tắc kỳ nhĩ, cao thanh đại khiếu, cầu nhân bất văn. Thử đẳng danh vi dục ẩn di lộ.

Translation: Therefore, Ananda, cultivating dhyana without cutting off killing is like a person who stops his own ears, shouts loudly, and hopes no one hears. Such ones are called those who, wishing to hide, reveal all the more.

Commentary: Therefore, Ananda, cultivating dhyana without cutting off killing. They must be strict with their seeds of compassion. Having lost the compassionate mind, it is like a person who stops his own ears, shouts loudly, and hopes no one hears. This is like the person who stops his ears to steal a bell, supposing that if he himself does not hear the bell, others will not hear either. Such ones are called those who, wishing to hide, reveal all the more. The more they wish to hide their deeds, the more they are revealed. Likewise, those who cultivate dhyana yet refuse to stop killing can hardly attain what they hope for.

Sutra text: 清淨比丘及諸菩薩,於岐路行不踏生草,況以手拔。云何大悲取諸眾生血肉充食?

Transliteration: Thanh tịnh tỷ-khưu cập chư Bồ-tát, ư kỳ lộ hành bất đạp sanh thảo, huống dĩ thủ bạt. Vân hà đại bi thủ chư chúng sanh huyết nhục sung thực?

Translation: Pure bhikshus and Bodhisattvas, walking along a forked road, do not tread on living grass, much less pull it up by hand. How can those practicing great compassion take beings' blood and flesh for food?

Commentary: Pure bhikshus and Bodhisattvas cultivating extremely pure conduct, walking along a road, do not tread on living grass. Where there are several paths, grass often grows beside the road. Pure bhikshus and Bodhisattvas will never step on living grass, fearing to kill the grass. Much less pull it up by hand. Nor do they uproot a single plant. How can those practicing great compassion take beings' blood and flesh for food? That cannot be.

Sutra text: 若諸比丘不服東方絲綿絹帛,及是此土靴覆裘毳乳酪醍醐。如是比丘於世真脫。酬還宿債不遊三界。

Transliteration: Nhược chư tỷ-khưu bất phục đông phương ty miên quyên bạch, cập thị thử độ ngoa phú cừu thuế, nhũ lạc đề hồ. Như thị tỷ-khưu ư thế chơn thóat. Thù hoàn túc trái, bất du tam giới.
